# generic_array - Rust

Source: https://fizyk20.github.io/generic-array/generic_array/

## Expand description

This crate implements a structure that can be used as a generic array type.

**Requires minimum Rust version of 1.65.0**

[Documentation on GH Pages](https://fizyk20.github.io/generic-array/generic_array/)
may be required to view certain types on foreign crates.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#upgrading-from-014-or-using-with-hybrid-array-04)Upgrading from 0.14 or using with `hybrid-array 0.4`

`generic-array 0.14` has been officially deprecated, so here’s a quick guide on how to upgrade from `generic-array 0.14` to `1.x`. Note that libraries depending on `generic-array` will need to update their usage as well. Some libraries are moving to `hybrid-array 0.4` instead, which we provide interoperability with `generic-array 1.x` via the `hybrid-array-0_4` feature flag.

## Click to expand

To upgrade to `1.x`, change your `Cargo.toml` to use the new version:

```
[dependencies]
generic-array = "1"
```
then in your code, go through and remove the `<T>` from `ArrayLength<T>` bounds, as the type parameter has been removed. It’s now just `ArrayLength`.

If you *need* to interoperate with `generic-array 0.14`, enable the `compat-0_14` feature flag:

```
[dependencies]
generic-array = { version = "1", features = ["compat-0_14"] }
```
then use the `to_0_14`/`from_0_14`/`as_0_14`/`as_0_14_mut` methods on `GenericArray` to convert between versions, or use the `From`/`AsRef`/`AsMut` implementations.

The `arr!` macro has changed to no longer require a type parameter, so change:

For interoperability with `hybrid-array 0.4`, enable the `hybrid-array-0_4` feature flag:

```
[dependencies]
generic-array = { version = "1", features = ["hybrid-array-0_4"] }
```
then use the `to_ha0_4`/`from_ha0_4`/`as_ha0_4`/`as_ha0_4_mut` methods on `GenericArray` to convert between versions, or use the `From`/`AsRef`/`AsMut` implementations.

We also implement the `AssocArraySize` and `AsArrayRef`/`AsArrayMut` traits from `hybrid-array` for `GenericArray`.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#usage)Usage

Before Rust 1.51, arrays `[T; N]` were problematic in that they couldn’t be
generic with respect to the length `N`, so this wouldn’t work:

Since 1.51, the below syntax is valid:

```
struct Foo<const N: usize> {
    data: [i32; N],
}
```
However, the const-generics we have as of writing this are still the minimum-viable product (`min_const_generics`), so many situations still result in errors, such as this example:

[ⓘ](https://fizyk20.github.io)

```
trait Bar {
    const LEN: usize;
    // Error: cannot perform const operation using `Self`
    fn bar(&self) -> Foo<{ Self::LEN }>;
}
```
**generic-array** defines a new trait [ ArrayLength](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.ArrayLength.html) and a struct

[, which lets the above be implemented as:](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html)

`GenericArray<T, N: ArrayLength>````
use generic_array::{GenericArray, ArrayLength};
struct Foo<N: ArrayLength> {
    data: GenericArray<i32, N>
}
trait Bar {
    type LEN: ArrayLength;
    fn bar(&self) -> Foo<Self::LEN>;
}
```
The [ ArrayLength](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.ArrayLength.html) trait is implemented for

[unsigned integer types](https://fizyk20.github.io/typenum/marker_traits/trait.Unsigned.html)from

[typenum](https://fizyk20.github.io/typenum/index.html). For example,

[would work almost like](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html)

`GenericArray<T, U5>``[T; 5]`:```
use generic_array::typenum::U5;
struct Foo<T, N: ArrayLength> {
    data: GenericArray<T, N>
}
let foo = Foo::<i32, U5> { data: GenericArray::default() };
```
The `arr!` macro is provided to allow easier creation of literal arrays, as shown below:

```
let array = arr![1, 2, 3];
//  array: GenericArray<i32, typenum::U3>
assert_eq!(array[2], 3);
```
[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#feature-flags)Feature flags

```
[dependencies.generic-array]
features = [
    "serde",            # Serialize/Deserialize implementation
    "zeroize",          # Zeroize implementation for setting array elements to zero
    "const-default",    # Compile-time const default value support via trait
    "alloc",            # Enables From/TryFrom implementations between GenericArray and Vec<T>/Box<[T]>
    "faster-hex",       # Enables internal use of the `faster-hex` crate for faster hex encoding via SIMD
    "subtle",           # Enables `subtle` crate support for constant-time equality checks and conditional selection
    "arbitrary",        # Enables `arbitrary` crate support for fuzzing
    "bytemuck",         # Enables `bytemuck` crate support
    "bitvec",           # Enables `bitvec` crate support to use GenericArray as a storage backend for bit arrays
    "as_slice",         # Enables `as-slice` crate trait impls
    "compat-0_14",      # Enables interoperability with `generic-array` 0.14
    "hybrid-array-0_4"  # Enables interoperability with `hybrid-array` 0.4
]
```

# generic_array - Rust

Source: https://fizyk20.github.io/generic-array/generic_array/index.html

## Expand description

This crate implements a structure that can be used as a generic array type.

**Requires minimum Rust version of 1.65.0**

[Documentation on GH Pages](https://fizyk20.github.io/generic-array/generic_array/)
may be required to view certain types on foreign crates.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#upgrading-from-014-or-using-with-hybrid-array-04)Upgrading from 0.14 or using with `hybrid-array 0.4`

`generic-array 0.14` has been officially deprecated, so here’s a quick guide on how to upgrade from `generic-array 0.14` to `1.x`. Note that libraries depending on `generic-array` will need to update their usage as well. Some libraries are moving to `hybrid-array 0.4` instead, which we provide interoperability with `generic-array 1.x` via the `hybrid-array-0_4` feature flag.

## Click to expand

To upgrade to `1.x`, change your `Cargo.toml` to use the new version:

```
[dependencies]
generic-array = "1"
```
then in your code, go through and remove the `<T>` from `ArrayLength<T>` bounds, as the type parameter has been removed. It’s now just `ArrayLength`.

If you *need* to interoperate with `generic-array 0.14`, enable the `compat-0_14` feature flag:

```
[dependencies]
generic-array = { version = "1", features = ["compat-0_14"] }
```
then use the `to_0_14`/`from_0_14`/`as_0_14`/`as_0_14_mut` methods on `GenericArray` to convert between versions, or use the `From`/`AsRef`/`AsMut` implementations.

The `arr!` macro has changed to no longer require a type parameter, so change:

For interoperability with `hybrid-array 0.4`, enable the `hybrid-array-0_4` feature flag:

```
[dependencies]
generic-array = { version = "1", features = ["hybrid-array-0_4"] }
```
then use the `to_ha0_4`/`from_ha0_4`/`as_ha0_4`/`as_ha0_4_mut` methods on `GenericArray` to convert between versions, or use the `From`/`AsRef`/`AsMut` implementations.

We also implement the `AssocArraySize` and `AsArrayRef`/`AsArrayMut` traits from `hybrid-array` for `GenericArray`.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#usage)Usage

Before Rust 1.51, arrays `[T; N]` were problematic in that they couldn’t be
generic with respect to the length `N`, so this wouldn’t work:

Since 1.51, the below syntax is valid:

```
struct Foo<const N: usize> {
    data: [i32; N],
}
```
However, the const-generics we have as of writing this are still the minimum-viable product (`min_const_generics`), so many situations still result in errors, such as this example:

[ⓘ](https://fizyk20.github.io)

```
trait Bar {
    const LEN: usize;
    // Error: cannot perform const operation using `Self`
    fn bar(&self) -> Foo<{ Self::LEN }>;
}
```
**generic-array** defines a new trait [ ArrayLength](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.ArrayLength.html) and a struct

[, which lets the above be implemented as:](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html)

`GenericArray<T, N: ArrayLength>````
use generic_array::{GenericArray, ArrayLength};
struct Foo<N: ArrayLength> {
    data: GenericArray<i32, N>
}
trait Bar {
    type LEN: ArrayLength;
    fn bar(&self) -> Foo<Self::LEN>;
}
```
The [ ArrayLength](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.ArrayLength.html) trait is implemented for

[unsigned integer types](https://fizyk20.github.io/typenum/marker_traits/trait.Unsigned.html)from

[typenum](https://fizyk20.github.io/typenum/index.html). For example,

[would work almost like](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html)

`GenericArray<T, U5>``[T; 5]`:```
use generic_array::typenum::U5;
struct Foo<T, N: ArrayLength> {
    data: GenericArray<T, N>
}
let foo = Foo::<i32, U5> { data: GenericArray::default() };
```
The `arr!` macro is provided to allow easier creation of literal arrays, as shown below:

```
let array = arr![1, 2, 3];
//  array: GenericArray<i32, typenum::U3>

```

[99](https://fizyk20.github.io#99)//!     fn bar(&self) -> Foo<Self::LEN>;
[100](https://fizyk20.github.io#100)//! }
[101](https://fizyk20.github.io#101)//! ```
[102](https://fizyk20.github.io#102)//!
[103](https://fizyk20.github.io#103)//! The [`ArrayLength`] trait is implemented for
[104](https://fizyk20.github.io#104)//! [unsigned integer types](typenum::Unsigned) from
[105](https://fizyk20.github.io#105)//! [typenum]. For example, [`GenericArray<T, U5>`] would work almost like `[T; 5]`:
[106](https://fizyk20.github.io#106)//!
[107](https://fizyk20.github.io#107)//! ```rust
[108](https://fizyk20.github.io#108)//! # use generic_array::{ArrayLength, GenericArray};
[109](https://fizyk20.github.io#109)//! use generic_array::typenum::U5;
[110](https://fizyk20.github.io#110)//!
[111](https://fizyk20.github.io#111)//! struct Foo<T, N: ArrayLength> {
[112](https://fizyk20.github.io#112)//!     data: GenericArray<T, N>
[113](https://fizyk20.github.io#113)//! }
[114](https://fizyk20.github.io#114)//!
[115](https://fizyk20.github.io#115)//! let foo = Foo::<i32, U5> { data: GenericArray::default() };
[116](https://fizyk20.github.io#116)//! ```
[117](https://fizyk20.github.io#117)//!
[118](https://fizyk20.github.io#118)//! The `arr!` macro is provided to allow easier creation of literal arrays, as shown below:
[119](https://fizyk20.github.io#119)//!
[120](https://fizyk20.github.io#120)//! ```rust
[121](https://fizyk20.github.io#121)//! # use generic_array::arr;
[122](https://fizyk20.github.io#122)//! let array = arr![1, 2, 3];
[123](https://fizyk20.github.io#123)//! //  array: GenericArray<i32, typenum::U3>
[124](https://fizyk20.github.io#124)//! assert_eq!(array[2], 3);
[125](https://fizyk20.github.io#125)//! ```
[126](https://fizyk20.github.io#126)//! ## Feature flags
[127](https://fizyk20.github.io#127)//!
[128](https://fizyk20.github.io#128)//! ```toml
[129](https://fizyk20.github.io#129)//! [dependencies.generic-array]
[130](https://fizyk20.github.io#130)//! features = [
[131](https://fizyk20.github.io#131)//!     "serde",            # Serialize/Deserialize implementation
[132](https://fizyk20.github.io#132)//!     "zeroize",          # Zeroize implementation for setting array elements to zero
[133](https://fizyk20.github.io#133)//!     "const-default",    # Compile-time const default value support via trait
[134](https://fizyk20.github.io#134)//!     "alloc",            # Enables From/TryFrom implementations between GenericArray and Vec<T>/Box<[T]>
[135](https://fizyk20.github.io#135)//!     "faster-hex",       # Enables internal use of the `faster-hex` crate for faster hex encoding via SIMD
[136](https://fizyk20.github.io#136)//!     "subtle",           # Enables `subtle` crate support for constant-time equality checks and conditional selection
[137](https://fizyk20.github.io#137)//!     "arbitrary",        # Enables `arbitrary` crate support for fuzzing
[138](https://fizyk20.github.io#138)//!     "bytemuck",         # Enables `bytemuck` crate support
[139](https://fizyk20.github.io#139)//!     "bitvec",           # Enables `bitvec` crate support to use GenericArray as a storage backend for bit arrays
[140](https://fizyk20.github.io#140)//!     "as_slice",         # Enables `as-slice` crate trait impls

[142](https://fizyk20.github.io#142)//!     "hybrid-array-0_4"  # Enables interoperability with `hybrid-array` 0.4

[209](https://fizyk20.github.io#209)
[210](https://fizyk20.github.io#210)/// `ArrayLength` is a type-level [`Unsigned`] integer used to
[211](https://fizyk20.github.io#211)/// define the number of elements in a [`GenericArray`].
[212](https://fizyk20.github.io#212)///
[213](https://fizyk20.github.io#213)/// Consider `N: ArrayLength` to be equivalent to `const N: usize`
[214](https://fizyk20.github.io#214)///
[215](https://fizyk20.github.io#215)/// ```
[216](https://fizyk20.github.io#216)/// # use generic_array::{GenericArray, ArrayLength};
[217](https://fizyk20.github.io#217)/// fn foo<N: ArrayLength>(arr: GenericArray<i32, N>) -> i32 {
[218](https://fizyk20.github.io#218)///     arr.iter().sum()
[219](https://fizyk20.github.io#219)/// }
[220](https://fizyk20.github.io#220)/// ```
[221](https://fizyk20.github.io#221)/// is equivalent to:
[222](https://fizyk20.github.io#222)/// ```
[223](https://fizyk20.github.io#223)/// fn foo<const N: usize>(arr: [i32; N]) -> i32 {
[224](https://fizyk20.github.io#224)///     arr.iter().sum()
[225](https://fizyk20.github.io#225)/// }
[226](https://fizyk20.github.io#226)/// ```
[227](https://fizyk20.github.io#227)///
[228](https://fizyk20.github.io#228)/// # Safety
[229](https://fizyk20.github.io#229)///
[230](https://fizyk20.github.io#230)/// This trait is effectively sealed due to only being allowed on [`Unsigned`] types,
[231](https://fizyk20.github.io#231)/// and therefore cannot be implemented in user code.
[232](https://fizyk20.github.io#232)///
[233](https://fizyk20.github.io#233)/// Furthermore, this is limited to lengths less than or equal to `usize::MAX`.
[234](https://fizyk20.github.io#234)/// ```compile_fail
[235](https://fizyk20.github.io#235)/// # #![recursion_limit = "256"]
[236](https://fizyk20.github.io#236)/// # use generic_array::{GenericArray, ArrayLength};
[237](https://fizyk20.github.io#237)/// # use generic_array::typenum::{self, Unsigned};
[238](https://fizyk20.github.io#238)/// type Empty = core::convert::Infallible; // Uninhabited ZST, size_of::<Empty>() == 0
[239](https://fizyk20.github.io#239)///
[240](https://fizyk20.github.io#240)/// // 2^64, greater than usize::MAX on 64-bit systems
[241](https://fizyk20.github.io#241)/// type TooBig = typenum::operator_aliases::Shleft<typenum::U1, typenum::U64>;
[242](https://fizyk20.github.io#242)///
[243](https://fizyk20.github.io#243)/// // Compile Error due to ArrayLength not implemented for TooBig
[244](https://fizyk20.github.io#244)/// let _ = GenericArray::<Empty, TooBig>::from_slice(&[]);
[245](https://fizyk20.github.io#245)/// ```
[246](https://fizyk20.github.io#246)pub unsafe trait ArrayLength: Unsigned + 'static {
[247](https://fizyk20.github.io#247)    /// Associated type representing the underlying contiguous memory
[248](https://fizyk20.github.io#248)    /// that constitutes an array with the given number of elements.
[249](https://fizyk20.github.io#249)    ///
[250](https://fizyk20.github.io#250)    /// This is an implementation detail, but is required to be public in cases where certain attributes
[251](https://fizyk20.github.io#251)    /// of the inner type of [`GenericArray`] cannot be proven, such as [`Copy`] bounds.
[252](https://fizyk20.github.io#252)    ///
[253](https://fizyk20.github.io#253)    /// [`Copy`] example:
[254](https://fizyk20.github.io#254)    /// ```
[255](https://fizyk20.github.io#255)    /// # use generic_array::{GenericArray, ArrayLength};
[256](https://fizyk20.github.io#256)    /// struct MyType<N: ArrayLength> {
[257](https://fizyk20.github.io#257)    ///     data: GenericArray<f32, N>,
[258](https://fizyk20.github.io#258)    /// }
[259](https://fizyk20.github.io#259)    ///
[260](https://fizyk20.github.io#260)    /// impl<N: ArrayLength> Clone for MyType<N> where N::ArrayType<f32>: Copy {
[261](https://fizyk20.github.io#261)    ///     fn clone(&self) -> Self { MyType { ..*self } }
[262](https://fizyk20.github.io#262)    /// }
[263](https://fizyk20.github.io#263)    ///
[264](https://fizyk20.github.io#264)    /// impl<N: ArrayLength> Copy for MyType<N> where N::ArrayType<f32>: Copy {}
[265](https://fizyk20.github.io#265)    /// ```
[266](https://fizyk20.github.io#266)    ///
[267](https://fizyk20.github.io#267)    /// Alternatively, using the entire `GenericArray<f32, N>` type as the bounds works:
[268](https://fizyk20.github.io#268)    /// ```ignore
[269](https://fizyk20.github.io#269)    /// where GenericArray<f32, N>: Copy
[270](https://fizyk20.github.io#270)    /// ```
[271](https://fizyk20.github.io#271)    type ArrayType<T>: Sealed;
[272](https://fizyk20.github.io#272)}
[273](https://fizyk20.github.io#273)
[274](https://fizyk20.github.io#274)unsafe impl ArrayLength for UTerm {
[275](https://fizyk20.github.io#275)    #[doc(hidden)]
[276](https://fizyk20.github.io#276)    type ArrayType<T> = [T; 0];
[277](https://fizyk20.github.io#277)}
[278](https://fizyk20.github.io#278)
[279](https://fizyk20.github.io#279)/// Implemented for types which can have an associated [`ArrayLength`],
[280](https://fizyk20.github.io#280)/// such as [`Const<N>`] for use with const-generics.
[281](https://fizyk20.github.io#281)///
[282](https://fizyk20.github.io#282)/// ```
[283](https://fizyk20.github.io#283)/// use generic_array::{GenericArray, IntoArrayLength, ConstArrayLength, typenum::Const};
[284](https://fizyk20.github.io#284)///
[285](https://fizyk20.github.io#285)/// fn some_array_interopt<const N: usize>(value: [u32; N]) -> GenericArray<u32, ConstArrayLength<N>>
[286](https://fizyk20.github.io#286)/// where
[287](https://fizyk20.github.io#287)///     Const<N>: IntoArrayLength,
[288](https://fizyk20.github.io#288)/// {
[289](https://fizyk20.github.io#289)///     let ga = GenericArray::from(value);
[290](https://fizyk20.github.io#290)///     // do stuff
[291](https://fizyk20.github.io#291)///     ga
[292](https://fizyk20.github.io#292)/// }
[293](https://fizyk20.github.io#293)/// ```
[294](https://fizyk20.github.io#294)///
[295](https://fizyk20.github.io#295)/// This is mostly to simplify the `where` bounds, equivalent to:
[296](https://fizyk20.github.io#296)///
[297](https://fizyk20.github.io#297)/// ```
[298](https://fizyk20.github.io#298)/// use generic_array::{GenericArray, ArrayLength, typenum::{Const, U, ToUInt}};
[299](https://fizyk20.github.io#299)///
[300](https://fizyk20.github.io#300)/// fn some_array_interopt<const N: usize>(value: [u32; N]) -> GenericArray<u32, U<N>>
[301](https://fizyk20.github.io#301)/// where
[302](https://fizyk20.github.io#302)///     Const<N>: ToUInt,
[303](https://fizyk20.github.io#303)///     U<N>: ArrayLength,
[304](https://fizyk20.github.io#304)/// {
[305](https://fizyk20.github.io#305)///     let ga = GenericArray::from(value);
[306](https://fizyk20.github.io#306)///     // do stuff
[307](https://fizyk20.github.io#307)///     ga
[308](https://fizyk20.github.io#308)/// }
[309](https://fizyk20.github.io#309)/// ```
[310](https://fizyk20.github.io#310)pub trait IntoArrayLength {

[364](https://fizyk20.github.io#364)// NOTE: These `Clone` impls are intentionally never reached in normal use:
[365](https://fizyk20.github.io#365)// `GenericArray<T, N>::clone` delegates to `self.map(Clone::clone)`, so the recursive
[366](https://fizyk20.github.io#366)// container's own `Clone` is never invoked. Bodied as `unreachable!()` (rather than the
[367](https://fizyk20.github.io#367)// recursive clone) to avoid emitting the recursive-clone codegen that would otherwise be
[368](https://fizyk20.github.io#368)// dead. The `GenericArrayImpl*` types are `#[doc(hidden)]` internals; they must remain
[369](https://fizyk20.github.io#369)// nameable via `<N as ArrayLength>::ArrayType<T>` for `typenum` reasons, so a caller can
[370](https://fizyk20.github.io#370)// technically construct one and call `.clone()` on it. That misuse now panics
[371](https://fizyk20.github.io#371)// deterministically instead of hitting `unreachable_unchecked()` (UB).
[372](https://fizyk20.github.io#372)impl<T: Clone, U: Clone> Clone for GenericArrayImplEven<T, U> {
[373](https://fizyk20.github.io#373)    #[inline(always)]
[374](https://fizyk20.github.io#374)    fn clone(&self) -> GenericArrayImplEven<T, U> {
[375](https://fizyk20.github.io#375)        unreachable!(
[376](https://fizyk20.github.io#376)            "GenericArrayImplEven::clone should never be called; \
[377](https://fizyk20.github.io#377)             clone a GenericArray<T, N> instead of its internal ArrayType<T>"
[378](https://fizyk20.github.io#378)        )
[379](https://fizyk20.github.io#379)    }
[380](https://fizyk20.github.io#380)}
[381](https://fizyk20.github.io#381)
[382](https://fizyk20.github.io#382)impl<T: Clone, U: Clone> Clone for GenericArrayImplOdd<T, U> {
[383](https://fizyk20.github.io#383)    #[inline(always)]
[384](https://fizyk20.github.io#384)    fn clone(&self) -> GenericArrayImplOdd<T, U> {
[385](https://fizyk20.github.io#385)        unreachable!(
[386](https://fizyk20.github.io#386)            "GenericArrayImplOdd::clone should never be called; \
[387](https://fizyk20.github.io#387)             clone a GenericArray<T, N> instead of its internal ArrayType<T>"
[388](https://fizyk20.github.io#388)        )
[389](https://fizyk20.github.io#389)    }
[390](https://fizyk20.github.io#390)}
[391](https://fizyk20.github.io#391)
[392](https://fizyk20.github.io#392)// Even if Clone is never used, they can still be byte-copyable.
[393](https://fizyk20.github.io#393)impl<T: Copy, U: Copy> Copy for GenericArrayImplEven<T, U> {}

[428](https://fizyk20.github.io#428)
[429](https://fizyk20.github.io#429)/// Struct representing a generic array - `GenericArray<T, N>` works like `[T; N]`
[430](https://fizyk20.github.io#430)///
[431](https://fizyk20.github.io#431)/// For how to implement [`Copy`] on structs using a generic-length `GenericArray` internally, see
[432](https://fizyk20.github.io#432)/// the docs for [`ArrayLength::ArrayType`].
[433](https://fizyk20.github.io#433)///
[434](https://fizyk20.github.io#434)/// # Usage Notes
[435](https://fizyk20.github.io#435)///
[436](https://fizyk20.github.io#436)/// ### Initialization
[437](https://fizyk20.github.io#437)///
[438](https://fizyk20.github.io#438)/// Initialization of known-length `GenericArray`s can be done via the [`arr![]`](arr!) macro,
[439](https://fizyk20.github.io#439)/// or [`from_array`](GenericArray::from_array)/[`from_slice`](GenericArray::from_slice).
[440](https://fizyk20.github.io#440)///
[441](https://fizyk20.github.io#441)/// For generic arrays of unknown/generic length, several safe methods are included to initialize
[442](https://fizyk20.github.io#442)/// them, such as the [`GenericSequence::generate`] method:
[443](https://fizyk20.github.io#443)///
[444](https://fizyk20.github.io#444)/// ```rust
[445](https://fizyk20.github.io#445)/// use generic_array::{GenericArray, sequence::GenericSequence, typenum, arr};
[446](https://fizyk20.github.io#446)///
[447](https://fizyk20.github.io#447)/// let evens: GenericArray<i32, typenum::U4> =
[448](https://fizyk20.github.io#448)///            GenericArray::generate(|i: usize| i as i32 * 2);
[449](https://fizyk20.github.io#449)///
[450](https://fizyk20.github.io#450)/// assert_eq!(evens, arr![0, 2, 4, 6]);
[451](https://fizyk20.github.io#451)/// ```
[452](https://fizyk20.github.io#452)///
[453](https://fizyk20.github.io#453)/// Furthermore, [`FromIterator`] and [`try_from_iter`](GenericArray::try_from_iter) exist to construct them
[454](https://fizyk20.github.io#454)/// from iterators, but will panic/fail if not given exactly the correct number of elements.
[455](https://fizyk20.github.io#455)///
[456](https://fizyk20.github.io#456)/// ### Utilities
[457](https://fizyk20.github.io#457)///
[458](https://fizyk20.github.io#458)/// The [`GenericSequence`], [`FunctionalSequence`], [`Lengthen`], [`Shorten`], [`Split`], and [`Concat`] traits implement
[459](https://fizyk20.github.io#459)/// some common operations on generic arrays.
[460](https://fizyk20.github.io#460)///
[461](https://fizyk20.github.io#461)/// ### Optimizations
[462](https://fizyk20.github.io#462)///
[463](https://fizyk20.github.io#463)/// Prefer to use the slice iterators like `.iter()`/`.iter_mut()` rather than by-value [`IntoIterator`]/[`GenericArrayIter`] if you can.
[464](https://fizyk20.github.io#464)/// Slices optimize better. Using the [`FunctionalSequence`] methods also optimize well.
[465](https://fizyk20.github.io#465)///
[466](https://fizyk20.github.io#466)/// # How it works
[467](https://fizyk20.github.io#467)///
[468](https://fizyk20.github.io#468)/// The `typenum` crate uses Rust's type system to define binary integers as nested types,
[469](https://fizyk20.github.io#469)/// and allows for operations which can be applied to those type-numbers, such as `Add`, `Sub`, etc.
[470](https://fizyk20.github.io#470)///
[471](https://fizyk20.github.io#471)/// e.g. `6` would be `UInt<UInt<UInt<UTerm, B1>, B1>, B0>`
[472](https://fizyk20.github.io#472)///
[473](https://fizyk20.github.io#473)/// `generic-array` uses this nested type to recursively allocate contiguous elements, statically.
[474](https://fizyk20.github.io#474)/// The [`ArrayLength`] trait is implemented on `UInt<N, B0>`, `UInt<N, B1>` and `UTerm`,
[475](https://fizyk20.github.io#475)/// which correspond to even, odd and zero numeric values, respectively.
[476](https://fizyk20.github.io#476)/// Together, these three cover all cases of `Unsigned` integers from `typenum`.
[477](https://fizyk20.github.io#477)/// For `UInt<N, B0>` and `UInt<N, B1>`, it peels away the highest binary digit and
[478](https://fizyk20.github.io#478)/// builds up a recursive structure that looks almost like a binary tree.
[479](https://fizyk20.github.io#479)/// Then, within `GenericArray`, the recursive structure is reinterpreted as a contiguous
[480](https://fizyk20.github.io#480)/// chunk of memory and allowing access to it as a slice.
[481](https://fizyk20.github.io#481)///
[482](https://fizyk20.github.io#482)/// <details>
[483](https://fizyk20.github.io#483)/// <summary><strong>Expand for internal structure demonstration</strong></summary>
[484](https://fizyk20.github.io#484)///
[485](https://fizyk20.github.io#485)/// For example, `GenericArray<T, U6>` more or less expands to (at compile time):
[486](https://fizyk20.github.io#486)///
[487](https://fizyk20.github.io#487)/// ```ignore
[488](https://fizyk20.github.io#488)/// GenericArray {
[489](https://fizyk20.github.io#489)///     // 6 = UInt<UInt<UInt<UTerm, B1>, B1>, B0>
[490](https://fizyk20.github.io#490)///     data: EvenData {
[491](https://fizyk20.github.io#491)///         // 3 = UInt<UInt<UTerm, B1>, B1>
[492](https://fizyk20.github.io#492)///         left: OddData {
[493](https://fizyk20.github.io#493)///             // 1 = UInt<UTerm, B1>
[494](https://fizyk20.github.io#494)///             left: OddData {
[495](https://fizyk20.github.io#495)///                 left: (),  // UTerm
[496](https://fizyk20.github.io#496)///                 right: (), // UTerm
[497](https://fizyk20.github.io#497)///                 data: T,   // Element 0
[498](https://fizyk20.github.io#498)///             },
[499](https://fizyk20.github.io#499)///             // 1 = UInt<UTerm, B1>
[500](https://fizyk20.github.io#500)///             right: OddData {
[501](https://fizyk20.github.io#501)///                 left: (),  // UTerm
[502](https://fizyk20.github.io#502)///                 right: (), // UTerm
[503](https://fizyk20.github.io#503)///                 data: T,   // Element 1
[504](https://fizyk20.github.io#504)///             },
[505](https://fizyk20.github.io#505)///             data: T        // Element 2
[506](https://fizyk20.github.io#506)///         },
[507](https://fizyk20.github.io#507)///         // 3 = UInt<UInt<UTerm, B1>, B1>
[508](https://fizyk20.github.io#508)///         right: OddData {
[509](https://fizyk20.github.io#509)///             // 1 = UInt<UTerm, B1>
[510](https://fizyk20.github.io#510)///             left: OddData {
[511](https://fizyk20.github.io#511)///                 left: (),  // UTerm
[512](https://fizyk20.github.io#512)///                 right: (), // UTerm
[513](https://fizyk20.github.io#513)///                 data: T,   // Element 3
[514](https://fizyk20.github.io#514)///             },
[515](https://fizyk20.github.io#515)///             // 1 = UInt<UTerm, B1>
[516](https://fizyk20.github.io#516)///             right: OddData {
[517](https://fizyk20.github.io#517)///                 left: (),  // UTerm
[518](https://fizyk20.github.io#518)///                 right: (), // UTerm
[519](https://fizyk20.github.io#519)///                 data: T,   // Element 4
[520](https://fizyk20.github.io#520)///             },
[521](https://fizyk20.github.io#521)///             data: T        // Element 5
[522](https://fizyk20.github.io#522)///         }
[523](https://fizyk20.github.io#523)///     }
[524](https://fizyk20.github.io#524)/// }
[525](https://fizyk20.github.io#525)/// ```
[526](https://fizyk20.github.io#526)///
[527](https://fizyk20.github.io#527)/// This has the added benefit of only being `log2(N)` deep, which is important for things like `Drop`
[528](https://fizyk20.github.io#528)/// to avoid stack overflows, since we can't implement `Drop` manually.
[529](https://fizyk20.github.io#529)///
[530](https://fizyk20.github.io#530)/// Then, we take the contiguous block of data and cast it to `*const T` or `*mut T` and use it as a slice:
[531](https://fizyk20.github.io#531)///
[532](https://fizyk20.github.io#532)/// ```ignore
[533](https://fizyk20.github.io#533)/// unsafe {
[534](https://fizyk20.github.io#534)///     slice::from_raw_parts(
[535](https://fizyk20.github.io#535)///         self as *const GenericArray<T, N> as *const T,
[536](https://fizyk20.github.io#536)///         <N as Unsigned>::USIZE
[537](https://fizyk20.github.io#537)///     )
[538](https://fizyk20.github.io#538)/// }
[539](https://fizyk20.github.io#539)/// ```
[540](https://fizyk20.github.io#540)///
[541](https://fizyk20.github.io#541)/// </details>
[542](https://fizyk20.github.io#542)#[repr(transparent)]

[546](https://fizyk20.github.io#546)}

[594](https://fizyk20.github.io#594)    fn from_iter<I>(iter: I) -> GenericArray<T, N>

[600](https://fizyk20.github.io#600)            Err(_) => from_iter_length_fail(N::USIZE),

[611](https://fizyk20.github.io#611)unsafe impl<T, N: ArrayLength> GenericSequence<T> for GenericArray<T, N>
[612](https://fizyk20.github.io#612)where
[613](https://fizyk20.github.io#613)    Self: IntoIterator<Item = T>,
[614](https://fizyk20.github.io#614){
[615](https://fizyk20.github.io#615)    type Length = N;
[616](https://fizyk20.github.io#616)    type Sequence = Self;
[617](https://fizyk20.github.io#617)
[618](https://fizyk20.github.io#618)    #[inline(always)]
[619](https://fizyk20.github.io#619)    fn generate<F>(mut f: F) -> GenericArray<T, N>
[620](https://fizyk20.github.io#620)    where
[621](https://fizyk20.github.io#621)        F: FnMut(usize) -> T,
[622](https://fizyk20.github.io#622)    {
[623](https://fizyk20.github.io#623)        unsafe {
[624](https://fizyk20.github.io#624)            let mut array = MaybeUninit::<GenericArray<T, N>>::uninit();
[625](https://fizyk20.github.io#625)            let mut builder = IntrusiveArrayBuilder::new_alt(&mut array);
[626](https://fizyk20.github.io#626)
[627](https://fizyk20.github.io#627)            let (builder_iter, position) = builder.iter_position();
[628](https://fizyk20.github.io#628)
[629](https://fizyk20.github.io#629)            builder_iter.enumerate().for_each(|(i, dst)| {
[630](https://fizyk20.github.io#630)                dst.write(f(i));
[631](https://fizyk20.github.io#631)                *position += 1;
[632](https://fizyk20.github.io#632)            });
[633](https://fizyk20.github.io#633)
[634](https://fizyk20.github.io#634)            builder.finish_and_assume_init()
[635](https://fizyk20.github.io#635)        }
[636](https://fizyk20.github.io#636)    }
[637](https://fizyk20.github.io#637)
[638](https://fizyk20.github.io#638)    #[inline(always)]
[639](https://fizyk20.github.io#639)    fn inverted_zip<B, U, F>(
[640](https://fizyk20.github.io#640)        self,
[641](https://fizyk20.github.io#641)        lhs: GenericArray<B, Self::Length>,
[642](https://fizyk20.github.io#642)        mut f: F,
[643](https://fizyk20.github.io#643)    ) -> MappedSequence<GenericArray<B, Self::Length>, B, U>
[644](https://fizyk20.github.io#644)    where
[645](https://fizyk20.github.io#645)        GenericArray<B, Self::Length>:
[646](https://fizyk20.github.io#646)            GenericSequence<B, Length = Self::Length> + MappedGenericSequence<B, U>,
[647](https://fizyk20.github.io#647)        Self: MappedGenericSequence<T, U>,
[648](https://fizyk20.github.io#648)        F: FnMut(B, Self::Item) -> U,
[649](https://fizyk20.github.io#649)    {
[650](https://fizyk20.github.io#650)        unsafe {
[651](https://fizyk20.github.io#651)            let mut left = ManuallyDrop::new(lhs);
[652](https://fizyk20.github.io#652)            let mut right = ManuallyDrop::new(self);
[653](https://fizyk20.github.io#653)
[654](https://fizyk20.github.io#654)            if mem::needs_drop::<T>() || mem::needs_drop::<B>() {
[655](https://fizyk20.github.io#655)                let mut left = IntrusiveArrayConsumer::new(&mut left);
[656](https://fizyk20.github.io#656)                let mut right = IntrusiveArrayConsumer::new(&mut right);
[657](https://fizyk20.github.io#657)
[658](https://fizyk20.github.io#658)                let (left_array_iter, left_position) = left.iter_position();
[659](https://fizyk20.github.io#659)                let (right_array_iter, right_position) = right.iter_position();
[660](https://fizyk20.github.io#660)
[661](https://fizyk20.github.io#661)                FromIterator::from_iter(left_array_iter.zip(right_array_iter).map(|(l, r)| {
[662](https://fizyk20.github.io#662)                    let left_value = ptr::read(l);
[663](https://fizyk20.github.io#663)                    let right_value = ptr::read(r);
[664](https://fizyk20.github.io#664)
[665](https://fizyk20.github.io#665)                    *left_position += 1;
[666](https://fizyk20.github.io#666)                    *right_position = *left_position;
[667](https://fizyk20.github.io#667)
[668](https://fizyk20.github.io#668)                    f(left_value, right_value)
[669](https://fizyk20.github.io#669)                }))
[670](https://fizyk20.github.io#670)            } else {
[671](https://fizyk20.github.io#671)                // Neither right nor left require `Drop` be called, so choose an iterator that's easily optimized,
[672](https://fizyk20.github.io#672)                // though we still keep them in `ManuallyDrop` out of paranoia.
[673](https://fizyk20.github.io#673)                //
[674](https://fizyk20.github.io#674)                // Note that because ArrayConsumer checks for `needs_drop` itself, if `f` panics then nothing
[675](https://fizyk20.github.io#675)                // would have been done about it anyway. Only the other branch needs `ArrayConsumer`
[676](https://fizyk20.github.io#676)                FromIterator::from_iter(left.iter().zip(right.iter()).map(|(l, r)| {
[677](https://fizyk20.github.io#677)                    f(ptr::read(l), ptr::read(r)) //
[678](https://fizyk20.github.io#678)                }))
[679](https://fizyk20.github.io#679)            }
[680](https://fizyk20.github.io#680)        }
[681](https://fizyk20.github.io#681)    }
[682](https://fizyk20.github.io#682)
[683](https://fizyk20.github.io#683)    #[inline(always)]
[684](https://fizyk20.github.io#684)    fn inverted_zip2<B, Lhs, U, F>(self, lhs: Lhs, mut f: F) -> MappedSequence<Lhs, B, U>
[685](https://fizyk20.github.io#685)    where
[686](https://fizyk20.github.io#686)        Lhs: GenericSequence<B, Length = Self::Length> + MappedGenericSequence<B, U>,
[687](https://fizyk20.github.io#687)        Self: MappedGenericSequence<T, U>,
[688](https://fizyk20.github.io#688)        F: FnMut(Lhs::Item, Self::Item) -> U,
[689](https://fizyk20.github.io#689)    {
[690](https://fizyk20.github.io#690)        unsafe {
[691](https://fizyk20.github.io#691)            if mem::needs_drop::<T>() {
[692](https://fizyk20.github.io#692)                let mut right = ManuallyDrop::new(self);
[693](https://fizyk20.github.io#693)                let mut right = IntrusiveArrayConsumer::new(&mut right);
[694](https://fizyk20.github.io#694)
[695](https://fizyk20.github.io#695)                let (right_array_iter, right_position) = right.iter_position();
[696](https://fizyk20.github.io#696)
[697](https://fizyk20.github.io#697)                FromIterator::from_iter(right_array_iter.zip(lhs).map(|(r, left_value)| {
[698](https://fizyk20.github.io#698)                    let right_value = ptr::read(r);
[699](https://fizyk20.github.io#699)
[700](https://fizyk20.github.io#700)                    *right_position += 1;
[701](https://fizyk20.github.io#701)
[702](https://fizyk20.github.io#702)                    f(left_value, right_value)
[703](https://fizyk20.github.io#703)                }))
[704](https://fizyk20.github.io#704)            } else {
[705](https://fizyk20.github.io#705)                let right = ManuallyDrop::new(self);
[706](https://fizyk20.github.io#706)
[707](https://fizyk20.github.io#707)                // Similar logic to `inverted_zip`'s no-drop branch
[708](https://fizyk20.github.io#708)                FromIterator::from_iter(right.iter().zip(lhs).map(|(r, left_value)| {
[709](https://fizyk20.github.io#709)                    f(left_value, ptr::read(r)) //
[710](https://fizyk20.github.io#710)                }))
[711](https://fizyk20.github.io#711)            }
[712](https://fizyk20.github.io#712)        }
[713](https://fizyk20.github.io#713)    }

[729](https://fizyk20.github.io#729)unsafe impl<T, N: ArrayLength> FallibleGenericSequence<T> for GenericArray<T, N>

[733](https://fizyk20.github.io#733)    type Error = core::convert::Infallible;
[734](https://fizyk20.github.io#734)
[735](https://fizyk20.github.io#735)    #[inline(always)]
[736](https://fizyk20.github.io#736)    fn try_generate<F, E>(mut f: F) -> Result<Result<Self::Sequence, E>, Self::Error>
[737](https://fizyk20.github.io#737)    where
[738](https://fizyk20.github.io#738)        F: FnMut(usize) -> Result<T, E>,
[739](https://fizyk20.github.io#739)    {
[740](https://fizyk20.github.io#740)        unsafe {
[741](https://fizyk20.github.io#741)            let mut array = MaybeUninit::<GenericArray<T, N>>::uninit();
[742](https://fizyk20.github.io#742)            let mut builder = IntrusiveArrayBuilder::new_alt(&mut array);
[743](https://fizyk20.github.io#743)
[744](https://fizyk20.github.io#744)            let (builder_iter, position) = builder.iter_position();
[745](https://fizyk20.github.io#745)
[746](https://fizyk20.github.io#746)            if let Err(e) = builder_iter
[747](https://fizyk20.github.io#747)                .enumerate()
[748](https://fizyk20.github.io#748)                .try_for_each(|(i, dst)| match f(i) {
[749](https://fizyk20.github.io#749)                    // NOTE: Using a match here instead of ? results in better codegen
[750](https://fizyk20.github.io#750)                    Ok(value) => {
[751](https://fizyk20.github.io#751)                        dst.write(value);
[752](https://fizyk20.github.io#752)                        *position += 1;
[753](https://fizyk20.github.io#753)                        Ok(())
[754](https://fizyk20.github.io#754)                    }
[755](https://fizyk20.github.io#755)                    Err(e) => Err(e),
[756](https://fizyk20.github.io#756)                })
[757](https://fizyk20.github.io#757)            {
[758](https://fizyk20.github.io#758)                drop(builder); // explicitly drop to run the destructor and drop any initialized elements
[759](https://fizyk20.github.io#759)
[760](https://fizyk20.github.io#760)                return Ok(Err(e));
[761](https://fizyk20.github.io#761)            }
[762](https://fizyk20.github.io#762)
[763](https://fizyk20.github.io#763)            Ok(Ok(builder.finish_and_assume_init()))
[764](https://fizyk20.github.io#764)        }
[765](https://fizyk20.github.io#765)    }

[962](https://fizyk20.github.io#962)    /// Borrows each element and returns a `GenericArray` of references
[963](https://fizyk20.github.io#963)    /// with the same length as `self`.
[964](https://fizyk20.github.io#964)    ///
[965](https://fizyk20.github.io#965)    /// This method is const since Rust 1.83.0, but non-const before.
[966](https://fizyk20.github.io#966)    ///
[967](https://fizyk20.github.io#967)    /// See also [`each_mut`](GenericArray::each_mut) for mutable references.
[968](https://fizyk20.github.io#968)    ///
[969](https://fizyk20.github.io#969)    /// # Example
[970](https://fizyk20.github.io#970)    ///
[971](https://fizyk20.github.io#971)    /// ```
[972](https://fizyk20.github.io#972)    /// # use generic_array::{arr, GenericArray};
[973](https://fizyk20.github.io#973)    /// let ga = arr![1, 2, 3];
[974](https://fizyk20.github.io#974)    /// let refs: GenericArray<&i32, _> = ga.each_ref();
[975](https://fizyk20.github.io#975)    /// assert_eq!(*refs[0], 1);
[976](https://fizyk20.github.io#976)    /// assert_eq!(*refs[1], 2);
[977](https://fizyk20.github.io#977)    /// assert_eq!(*refs[2], 3);
[978](https://fizyk20.github.io#978)    /// ```
[979](https://fizyk20.github.io#979)    #[rustversion::attr(since(1.83), const)] // needed for `as_mut_slice` to be const
[980](https://fizyk20.github.io#980)    pub fn each_ref(&self) -> GenericArray<&T, N> {
[981](https://fizyk20.github.io#981)        let mut out: GenericArray<MaybeUninit<*const T>, N> = GenericArray::uninit();
[982](https://fizyk20.github.io#982)
[983](https://fizyk20.github.io#983)        {
[984](https://fizyk20.github.io#984)            // only slices allow `const` indexing
[985](https://fizyk20.github.io#985)            let (this, out) = (self.as_slice(), out.as_mut_slice());
[986](https://fizyk20.github.io#986)
[987](https://fizyk20.github.io#987)            let mut i = 0;
[988](https://fizyk20.github.io#988)            while i < N::USIZE {
[989](https://fizyk20.github.io#989)                out[i].write(ptr::addr_of!(this[i]));
[990](https://fizyk20.github.io#990)                i += 1;
[991](https://fizyk20.github.io#991)            }
[992](https://fizyk20.github.io#992)        }
[993](https://fizyk20.github.io#993)
[994](https://fizyk20.github.io#994)        // SAFETY: `*const T` has the same layout as `&T`, and we've also initialized each pointer as a valid reference.
[995](https://fizyk20.github.io#995)        unsafe { const_transmute(out) }
[996](https://fizyk20.github.io#996)    }

[1033](https://fizyk20.github.io#1033)    /// Converts a slice of `T` elements into a slice of `GenericArray<T, N>` chunks.
[1034](https://fizyk20.github.io#1034)    ///
[1035](https://fizyk20.github.io#1035)    /// Any remaining elements that do not fill the array will be returned as a second slice.
[1036](https://fizyk20.github.io#1036)    ///
[1037](https://fizyk20.github.io#1037)    /// # Panics
[1038](https://fizyk20.github.io#1038)    ///
[1039](https://fizyk20.github.io#1039)    /// Panics if `N` is `U0` _AND_ the input slice is not empty.
[1040](https://fizyk20.github.io#1040)    pub const fn chunks_from_slice(slice: &[T]) -> (&[GenericArray<T, N>], &[T]) {
[1041](https://fizyk20.github.io#1041)        if N::USIZE == 0 {
[1042](https://fizyk20.github.io#1042)            assert!(slice.is_empty(), "GenericArray length N must be non-zero");
[1043](https://fizyk20.github.io#1043)            return (&[], &[]);
[1044](https://fizyk20.github.io#1044)        }
[1045](https://fizyk20.github.io#1045)
[1046](https://fizyk20.github.io#1046)        // NOTE: Using `slice.split_at` adds an unnecessary assert
[1047](https://fizyk20.github.io#1047)        let num_chunks = slice.len() / N::USIZE; // integer division
[1048](https://fizyk20.github.io#1048)        let num_in_chunks = num_chunks * N::USIZE;
[1049](https://fizyk20.github.io#1049)        let num_remainder = slice.len() - num_in_chunks;
[1050](https://fizyk20.github.io#1050)
[1051](https://fizyk20.github.io#1051)        unsafe {
[1052](https://fizyk20.github.io#1052)            (
[1053](https://fizyk20.github.io#1053)                slice::from_raw_parts(slice.as_ptr() as *const GenericArray<T, N>, num_chunks),
[1054](https://fizyk20.github.io#1054)                slice::from_raw_parts(slice.as_ptr().add(num_in_chunks), num_remainder),
[1055](https://fizyk20.github.io#1055)            )
[1056](https://fizyk20.github.io#1056)        }
[1057](https://fizyk20.github.io#1057)    }
[1058](https://fizyk20.github.io#1058)
[1059](https://fizyk20.github.io#1059)    /// Converts a mutable slice of `T` elements into a mutable slice `GenericArray<T, N>` chunks.
[1060](https://fizyk20.github.io#1060)    ///
[1061](https://fizyk20.github.io#1061)    /// Any remaining elements that do not fill the array will be returned as a second slice.
[1062](https://fizyk20.github.io#1062)    ///
[1063](https://fizyk20.github.io#1063)    /// # Panics
[1064](https://fizyk20.github.io#1064)    ///
[1065](https://fizyk20.github.io#1065)    /// Panics if `N` is `U0` _AND_ the input slice is not empty.
[1066](https://fizyk20.github.io#1066)    ///
[1067](https://fizyk20.github.io#1067)    /// This method is `const` since Rust 1.83.0, but non-`const` before.
[1068](https://fizyk20.github.io#1068)    #[rustversion::attr(since(1.83), const)]
[1069](https://fizyk20.github.io#1069)    pub fn chunks_from_slice_mut(slice: &mut [T]) -> (&mut [GenericArray<T, N>], &mut [T]) {
[1070](https://fizyk20.github.io#1070)        if N::USIZE == 0 {
[1071](https://fizyk20.github.io#1071)            assert!(slice.is_empty(), "GenericArray length N must be non-zero");
[1072](https://fizyk20.github.io#1072)            return (&mut [], &mut []);
[1073](https://fizyk20.github.io#1073)        }
[1074](https://fizyk20.github.io#1074)
[1075](https://fizyk20.github.io#1075)        // NOTE: Using `slice.split_at_mut` adds an unnecessary assert
[1076](https://fizyk20.github.io#1076)        let num_chunks = slice.len() / N::USIZE; // integer division
[1077](https://fizyk20.github.io#1077)        let num_in_chunks = num_chunks * N::USIZE;
[1078](https://fizyk20.github.io#1078)        let num_remainder = slice.len() - num_in_chunks;
[1079](https://fizyk20.github.io#1079)
[1080](https://fizyk20.github.io#1080)        // Derive both halves from a single `as_mut_ptr()`. Calling it twice would
[1081](https://fizyk20.github.io#1081)        // reborrow the whole `&mut [T]` for the second pointer, invalidating the
[1082](https://fizyk20.github.io#1082)        // first chunk's provenance under Stacked Borrows even though the regions
[1083](https://fizyk20.github.io#1083)        // are disjoint. This mirrors how `slice::split_at_mut` is implemented.
[1084](https://fizyk20.github.io#1084)        let base = slice.as_mut_ptr();
[1085](https://fizyk20.github.io#1085)
[1086](https://fizyk20.github.io#1086)        unsafe {
[1087](https://fizyk20.github.io#1087)            (
[1088](https://fizyk20.github.io#1088)                slice::from_raw_parts_mut(base as *mut GenericArray<T, N>, num_chunks),
[1089](https://fizyk20.github.io#1089)                slice::from_raw_parts_mut(base.add(num_in_chunks), num_remainder),
[1090](https://fizyk20.github.io#1090)            )
[1091](https://fizyk20.github.io#1091)        }
[1092](https://fizyk20.github.io#1092)    }

[1194](https://fizyk20.github.io#1194)    /// Extracts the values from a generic array of `MaybeUninit` containers.

[1198](https://fizyk20.github.io#1198)    /// It is up to the caller to guarantee that all elements of the array are in an initialized state.
[1199](https://fizyk20.github.io#1199)    ///

[1206](https://fizyk20.github.io#1206)    /// array[0].write(0);

[1211](https://fizyk20.github.io#1211)    /// let array = unsafe {
[1212](https://fizyk20.github.io#1212)    ///     GenericArray::assume_init(array)
[1213](https://fizyk20.github.io#1213)    /// };
[1214](https://fizyk20.github.io#1214)    ///

[1217](https://fizyk20.github.io#1217)    #[inline(always)]

[1219](https://fizyk20.github.io#1219)        const_transmute::<GenericArray<MaybeUninit<T>, N>, GenericArray<T, N>>(array)
[1220](https://fizyk20.github.io#1220)    }

# ArrayLength in generic_array - Rust

Source: https://fizyk20.github.io/generic-array/generic_array/trait.ArrayLength.html

## Expand description

`ArrayLength` is a type-level [ Unsigned](https://fizyk20.github.io/typenum/marker_traits/trait.Unsigned.html) integer used to
define the number of elements in a

[.](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html)

`GenericArray`Consider `N: ArrayLength` to be equivalent to `const N: usize`

```
fn foo<N: ArrayLength>(arr: GenericArray<i32, N>) -> i32 {
    arr.iter().sum()
}
```
is equivalent to:

```
fn foo<const N: usize>(arr: [i32; N]) -> i32 {
    arr.iter().sum()
}
```
[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#safety)Safety

This trait is effectively sealed due to only being allowed on [ Unsigned](https://fizyk20.github.io/typenum/marker_traits/trait.Unsigned.html) types,
and therefore cannot be implemented in user code.

Furthermore, this is limited to lengths less than or equal to `usize::MAX`.

[ⓘ](https://fizyk20.github.io)

```
type Empty = core::convert::Infallible; // Uninhabited ZST, size_of::<Empty>() == 0
// 2^64, greater than usize::MAX on 64-bit systems
type TooBig = typenum::operator_aliases::Shleft<typenum::U1, typenum::U64>;
// Compile Error due to ArrayLength not implemented for TooBig
let _ = GenericArray::<Empty, TooBig>::from_slice(&[]);
```
## Required Associated Types[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#required-associated-types)

Associated type representing the underlying contiguous memory that constitutes an array with the given number of elements.

This is an implementation detail, but is required to be public in cases where certain attributes
of the inner type of [ GenericArray](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html) cannot be proven, such as

[bounds.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html)

`Copy`[ Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html) example:

```
struct MyType<N: ArrayLength> {
    data: GenericArray<f32, N>,
}
impl<N: ArrayLength> Clone for MyType<N> where N::ArrayType<f32>: Copy {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self { MyType { ..*self } }
}
impl<N: ArrayLength> Copy for MyType<N> where N::ArrayType<f32>: Copy {}
```
Alternatively, using the entire `GenericArray<f32, N>` type as the bounds works:

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# GenericArray in generic_array - Rust

Source: https://fizyk20.github.io/generic-array/generic_array/struct.GenericArray.html

`pub struct GenericArray<T, N: `[ArrayLength](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.ArrayLength.html)> { /* private fields */ }## Expand description

Struct representing a generic array - `GenericArray<T, N>` works like `[T; N]`

For how to implement [ Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html) on structs using a generic-length

`GenericArray` internally, see
the docs for [.](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.ArrayLength.html#associatedtype.ArrayType)

`ArrayLength::ArrayType`[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#usage-notes)Usage Notes

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#initialization)Initialization

Initialization of known-length `GenericArray`s can be done via the [ arr![]](https://fizyk20.github.io/macro.arr.html) macro,
or

[/](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html#method.from_array)

`from_array`[.](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html#method.from_slice)

`from_slice`For generic arrays of unknown/generic length, several safe methods are included to initialize
them, such as the [ GenericSequence::generate](https://fizyk20.github.io/sequence/trait.GenericSequence.html#tymethod.generate) method:

```
use generic_array::{GenericArray, sequence::GenericSequence, typenum, arr};
let evens: GenericArray<i32, typenum::U4> =
           GenericArray::generate(|i: usize| i as i32 * 2);
assert_eq!(evens, arr![0, 2, 4, 6]);
```
Furthermore, [ FromIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.FromIterator.html) and

[exist to construct them from iterators, but will panic/fail if not given exactly the correct number of elements.](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html#method.try_from_iter)

`try_from_iter`[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#utilities)Utilities

The [ GenericSequence](https://fizyk20.github.io/sequence/trait.GenericSequence.html),

[,](https://fizyk20.github.io/functional/trait.FunctionalSequence.html)

`FunctionalSequence`[,](https://fizyk20.github.io/sequence/trait.Lengthen.html)

`Lengthen`[,](https://fizyk20.github.io/sequence/trait.Shorten.html)

`Shorten`[, and](https://fizyk20.github.io/sequence/trait.Split.html)

`Split`[traits implement some common operations on generic arrays.](https://fizyk20.github.io/sequence/trait.Concat.html)

`Concat`[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#optimizations)Optimizations

Prefer to use the slice iterators like `.iter()`/`.iter_mut()` rather than by-value [ IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)/

[if you can. Slices optimize better. Using the](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArrayIter.html)

`GenericArrayIter`[methods also optimize well.](https://fizyk20.github.io/functional/trait.FunctionalSequence.html)

`FunctionalSequence`[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#how-it-works)How it works

The `typenum` crate uses Rust’s type system to define binary integers as nested types,
and allows for operations which can be applied to those type-numbers, such as `Add`, `Sub`, etc.

e.g. `6` would be `UInt<UInt<UInt<UTerm, B1>, B1>, B0>`

`generic-array` uses this nested type to recursively allocate contiguous elements, statically.
The [ ArrayLength](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.ArrayLength.html) trait is implemented on

`UInt<N, B0>`, `UInt<N, B1>` and `UTerm`,
which correspond to even, odd and zero numeric values, respectively.
Together, these three cover all cases of `Unsigned` integers from `typenum`.
For `UInt<N, B0>` and `UInt<N, B1>`, it peels away the highest binary digit and
builds up a recursive structure that looks almost like a binary tree.
Then, within `GenericArray`, the recursive structure is reinterpreted as a contiguous
chunk of memory and allowing access to it as a slice.**Expand for internal structure demonstration**

For example, `GenericArray<T, U6>` more or less expands to (at compile time):

[ⓘ](https://fizyk20.github.io)

```
GenericArray {
    // 6 = UInt<UInt<UInt<UTerm, B1>, B1>, B0>
    data: EvenData {
        // 3 = UInt<UInt<UTerm, B1>, B1>
        left: OddData {
            // 1 = UInt<UTerm, B1>
            left: OddData {
                left: (),  // UTerm
                right: (), // UTerm
                data: T,   // Element 0
            },
            // 1 = UInt<UTerm, B1>
            right: OddData {
                left: (),  // UTerm
                right: (), // UTerm
                data: T,   // Element 1
            },
            data: T        // Element 2
        },
        // 3 = UInt<UInt<UTerm, B1>, B1>
        right: OddData {
            // 1 = UInt<UTerm, B1>
            left: OddData {
                left: (),  // UTerm
                right: (), // UTerm
                data: T,   // Element 3
            },
            // 1 = UInt<UTerm, B1>
            right: OddData {
                left: (),  // UTerm
                right: (), // UTerm
                data: T,   // Element 4
            },
            data: T        // Element 5
        }
    }
}
```
This has the added benefit of only being `log2(N)` deep, which is important for things like `Drop`
to avoid stack overflows, since we can’t implement `Drop` manually.

Then, we take the contiguous block of data and cast it to `*const T` or `*mut T` and use it as a slice:

**crate feature**only.

`alloc`Alternative to `Box::<GenericArray<T, N>>::default()` that won’t overflow the stack for very large arrays.

The standard `Box::default()` calls `default` on the inner type, creating it on the stack,
and then moves it onto the heap. Optimized release builds often remove this step, but debug builds
may have issues.

Borrows each element and returns a `GenericArray` of references
with the same length as `self`.

This method is const since Rust 1.83.0, but non-const before.

See also [ each_mut](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html#method.each_mut) for mutable references.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#example)Example

```
let ga = arr![1, 2, 3];
let refs: GenericArray<&i32, _> = ga.each_ref();
assert_eq!(*refs[0], 1);
assert_eq!(*refs[1], 2);
assert_eq!(*refs[2], 3);
```

```
let mut ga = arr![1, 2, 3];
let mut_refs: GenericArray<&mut i32, _> = ga.each_mut();
for r in mut_refs {
    *r *= 2;
}
assert_eq!(ga, arr![2, 4, 6]);
```

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/generic_array/lib.rs.html#1218-1220)#### pub const unsafe fn [assume_init](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.assume_init)(array: [GenericArray](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html)<[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<T>, N>) -> Self

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/generic_array/lib.rs.html#1218-1220)

#### pub const unsafe fn [assume_init](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.assume_init)(array: [GenericArray](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.GenericArray.html)<[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<T>, N>) -> Self

Extracts the values from a generic array of `MaybeUninit` containers.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#safety)Safety

It is up to the caller to guarantee that all elements of the array are in an initialized state.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#example-2)Example

```
let mut array: GenericArray<MaybeUninit<i32>, U3> = GenericArray::uninit();
array[0].write(0);
array[1].write(1);
array[2].write(2);
// SAFETY: Now safe as we initialised all elements
let array = unsafe {
    GenericArray::assume_init(array)
};
assert_eq!(array, arr![0, 1, 2]);
```

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/generic_array/lib.rs.html#1316-1347)#### pub fn [try_from_fallible_iter](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.try_from_fallible_iter)<I, E>(
    iter: I,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, E>, [LengthError](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.LengthError.html)>

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/generic_array/lib.rs.html#1316-1347)

#### pub fn [try_from_fallible_iter](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.try_from_fallible_iter)<I, E>(
    iter: I,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, E>, [LengthError](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.LengthError.html)>

Fallible equivalent of [ FromFallibleIterator::from_fallible_iter](https://fizyk20.github.io/sequence/trait.FromFallibleIterator.html#tymethod.from_fallible_iter).

Unlike `.collect::<Result<GenericArray<T, N>, E>>()`, this method will not panic
on length mismatch, instead returning a `LengthError`.

Given iterator must yield exactly `N` elements or an error will be returned. Using [ .take(N)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#method.take)
with an iterator longer than the array may be helpful.

Returns a mutable reference to the first element of the slice, or `None` if it is empty.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-3)Examples

```
let x = &mut [0, 1, 2];
if let Some(first) = x.first_mut() {
    *first = 5;
}
assert_eq!(x, &[5, 1, 2]);
let y: &mut [i32] = &mut [];
assert_eq!(None, y.first_mut());
```

Returns a reference to an element or subslice depending on the type of index.

- If given a position, returns a reference to the element at that
position or `None`if out of bounds.
- If given a range, returns the subslice corresponding to that range,
or `None`if out of bounds.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-18)Examples

```
let v = [10, 40, 30];
assert_eq!(Some(&40), v.get(1));
assert_eq!(Some(&[10, 40][..]), v.get(0..2));
assert_eq!(None, v.get(3));

Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is * undefined behavior*
even if the resulting reference is not used.

You can think of this like `.get(index).unwrap_unchecked()`.  It’s UB
to call `.get_unchecked(len)`, even if you immediately convert to a

Returns a raw pointer to the slice’s buffer.

The caller must ensure that the slice outlives the pointer this function returns, or else it will end up dangling.

The caller must also ensure that the memory the pointer (non-transitively) points to
is never written to (except inside an `UnsafeCell`) using this pointer or any pointer
derived from it. If you need to mutate the contents of the slice, use [ as_mut_ptr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_mut_ptr).

Modifying the container referenced by this slice may cause its buffer to be reallocated, which would also make any pointers to it invalid.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-22)Examples

```
let x = &[1, 2, 4];

unsafe {
    for i in 0..x.len() {
        assert_eq!(x.get_unchecked(i), &*x_ptr.add(i));
    }
}
```

1.48.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#796)#### pub fn [as_ptr_range](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.as_ptr_range)(&self) -> [Range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.Range.html)<[*const T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)>

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#796)

#### pub fn [as_ptr_range](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.as_ptr_range)(&self) -> [Range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.Range.html)<[*const T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)>

Returns the two raw pointers spanning the slice.

The returned range is half-open, which means that the end pointer
points *one past* the last element of the slice. This way, an empty
slice is represented by two equal pointers, and the difference between
the two pointers represents the size of the slice.

See [ as_ptr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_ptr) for warnings on using these pointers. The end pointer
requires extra caution, as it does not point to a valid element in the
slice.

This function is useful for interacting with foreign interfaces which use two pointers to refer to a range of elements in memory, as is common in C++.

It can also be useful to check if a pointer to an element refers to an element of this slice:

```
let a = [1, 2, 3];
let x = &a[1] as *const _;
let y = &5 as *const _;
assert!(a.as_ptr_range().contains(&x));
assert!(!a.as_ptr_range().contains(&y));
```

Returns an iterator over all contiguous windows of length
`size`. The windows overlap. If the slice is shorter than
`size`, the iterator returns no values.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#panics-5)Panics

Panics if `size` is zero.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-29)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let mut iter = slice.windows(3);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['l', 'o', 'r']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['o', 'r', 'e']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['r', 'e', 'm']);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
If the slice is shorter than `size`:

```
let slice = ['f', 'o', 'o'];
let mut iter = slice.windows(4);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
Because the [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html) trait cannot represent the required lifetimes,
there is no `windows_mut` analog to `windows`;
`[0,1,2].windows_mut(2).collect()` would violate [the rules of references](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch04-02-references-and-borrowing.html#the-rules-of-references)
(though a [LendingIterator](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2022/10/28/gats-stabilization.html) analog is possible). You can sometimes use
[ Cell::as_slice_of_cells](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cell/struct.Cell.html#method.as_slice_of_cells) in
conjunction with

`windows` instead:```
use std::cell::Cell;
let mut array = ['R', 'u', 's', 't', ' ', '2', '0', '1', '5'];
let slice = &mut array[..];
let slice_of_cells: &[Cell<char>] = Cell::from_mut(slice).as_slice_of_cells();
for w in slice_of_cells.windows(3) {
    Cell::swap(&w[0], &w[2]);
}
assert_eq!(array, ['s', 't', ' ', '2', '0', '1', '5', 'u', 'R']);
```
Returns an iterator over `chunk_size` elements of the slice at a time, starting at the
beginning of the slice.

The chunks are slices and do not overlap. If `chunk_size` does not divide the length of the
slice, then the last chunk will not have length `chunk_size`.

See [ chunks_exact](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks_exact) for a variant of this iterator that returns chunks of always exactly

`chunk_size` elements, and [for the same iterator but starting at the end of the slice.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.rchunks)

`rchunks`If your `chunk_size` is a constant, consider using [ as_chunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_chunks) instead, which will
give references to arrays of exactly that length, rather than slices.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#panics-6)Panics

Panics if `chunk_size` is zero.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-30)Examples

```

assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['r', 'e']);

Returns an iterator over `chunk_size` elements of the slice at a time, starting at the
beginning of the slice.

The chunks are slices and do not overlap. If `chunk_size` does not divide the length of the
slice, then the last up to `chunk_size-1` elements will be omitted and can be retrieved
from the `remainder` function of the iterator.

Due to each chunk having exactly `chunk_size` elements, the compiler can often optimize the
resulting code better than in the case of [ chunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks).

See [ chunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks) for a variant of this iterator that also returns the remainder as a smaller
chunk, and

[for the same iterator but starting at the end of the slice.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.rchunks_exact)

`rchunks_exact`If your `chunk_size` is a constant, consider using [ as_chunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_chunks) instead, which will
give references to arrays of exactly that length, rather than slices.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#panics-8)Panics

Panics if `chunk_size` is zero.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-32)Examples

1.88.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1341)#### pub unsafe fn [as_chunks_unchecked](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.as_chunks_unchecked)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> &[[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1341)

#### pub unsafe fn [as_chunks_unchecked](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.as_chunks_unchecked)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> &[[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]

Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
assuming that there’s no remainder.

This is the inverse operation to [ as_flattened](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened).

As this is `unsafe`, consider whether you could use [ as_chunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_chunks) or

[instead, perhaps via something like](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_rchunks)

`as_rchunks``if let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks()` or
`let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks() else { unreachable!() };`.[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#safety-4)Safety

This may only be called when

- The slice splits exactly into `N`-element chunks (aka`self.len() % N == 0`).
- `N != 0`.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-34)Examples

```
let slice: &[char] = &['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm', '!'];
let chunks: &[[char; 1]] =
    // SAFETY: 1-element chunks never have remainder
    unsafe { slice.as_chunks_unchecked() };
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['l'], ['o'], ['r'], ['e'], ['m'], ['!']]);
let chunks: &[[char; 3]] =
    // SAFETY: The slice length (6) is a multiple of 3
    unsafe { slice.as_chunks_unchecked() };
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['l', 'o', 'r'], ['e', 'm', '!']]);
// These would be unsound:
// let chunks: &[[_; 5]] = slice.as_chunks_unchecked() // The slice length is not a multiple of 5
// let chunks: &[[_; 0]] = slice.as_chunks_unchecked() // Zero-length chunks are never allowed
```
Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
starting at the beginning of the slice,
and a remainder slice with length strictly less than `N`.

The remainder is meaningful in the division sense.  Given
`let (chunks, remainder) = slice.as_chunks()`, then:

- `chunks.len()`equals- `slice.len() / N`,
- `remainder.len()`equals- `slice.len() % N`, and
- `slice.len()`equals- `chunks.len() * N + remainder.len()`.

You can flatten the chunks back into a slice-of-`T` with [ as_flattened](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened).

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#panics-10)Panics

Panics if `N` is zero.

Note that this check is against a const generic parameter, not a runtime value, and thus a particular monomorphization will either always panic or it will never panic.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-35)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let (chunks, remainder) = slice.as_chunks();
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['l', 'o'], ['r', 'e']]);
assert_eq!(remainder, &['m']);
```
If you expect the slice to be an exact multiple, you can combine
`let`-`else` with an empty slice pattern:

```
let slice = ['R', 'u', 's', 't'];
let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks::<2>() else {
    panic!("slice didn't have even length")
};
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['R', 'u'], ['s', 't']]);
```

1.31.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1778)#### pub fn [rchunks_exact](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.rchunks_exact)(&self, chunk_size: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [RChunksExact](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.RChunksExact.html)<'_, T>

#### pub fn [rchunks_exact](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.rchunks_exact)(&self, chunk_size: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [RChunksExact](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/iter/struct.RChunksExact.html)<'_, T>

Returns an iterator over `chunk_size` elements of the slice at a time, starting at the
end of the slice.

The chunks are slices and do not overlap. If `chunk_size` does not divide the length of the
slice, then the last up to `chunk_size-1` elements will be omitted and can be retrieved
from the `remainder` function of the iterator.

Due to each chunk having exactly `chunk_size` elements, the compiler can often optimize the
resulting code better than in the case of [ rchunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.rchunks).

See [ rchunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.rchunks) for a variant of this iterator that also returns the remainder as a smaller
chunk, and

[for the same iterator but starting at the beginning of the slice.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks_exact)

`chunks_exact`If your `chunk_size` is a constant, consider using [ as_rchunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_rchunks) instead, which will
give references to arrays of exactly that length, rather than slices.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#panics-17)Panics

Panics if `chunk_size` is zero.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-43)Examples

```

assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['e', 'm']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['o', 'r']);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
assert_eq!(iter.remainder(), &['l']);

Returns an iterator over the slice producing non-overlapping runs of elements using the predicate to separate them.

The predicate is called for every pair of consecutive elements,
meaning that it is called on `slice[0]` and `slice[1]`,
followed by `slice[1]` and `slice[2]`, and so on.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-45)Examples

```
let slice = &[1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2];
let mut iter = slice.chunk_by(|a, b| a == b);
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[1, 1, 1][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[3, 3][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[2, 2, 2][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);
```
This method can be used to extract the sorted subslices:

```
let slice = &[1, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4];
let mut iter = slice.chunk_by(|a, b| a <= b);
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[1, 1, 2, 3][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[2, 3][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[2, 3, 4][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);
```

Divides one slice into two at an index.

The first will contain all indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding
the index `mid` itself) and the second will contain all
indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index `len` itself).

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#panics-19)Panics

Panics if `mid > len`.  For a non-panicking alternative see

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-47)Examples

```

   assert_eq!(left, []);
   assert_eq!(right, ['a', 'b', 'c']);

    assert_eq!(left, ['a', 'b']);
    assert_eq!(right, ['c']);

{

```

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#safety-7)Safety

Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is * undefined behavior*
even if the resulting reference is not used. The caller has to ensure that

`0 <= mid <= self.len()`.[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-50)Examples

Divides one slice into two at an index, returning `None` if the slice is
too short.

If `mid ≤ len` returns a pair of slices where the first will contain all
indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding the index `mid` itself) and the
second will contain all indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index
`len` itself).

Otherwise, if `mid > len`, returns `None`.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-51)Examples

```

{
   let (left, right) = v.split_at_checked(0).unwrap();
   assert_eq!(left, []);
   assert_eq!(right, [1, -2, 3, -4, 5, -6]);
}
{
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_checked(2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(left, [1, -2]);
    assert_eq!(right, [3, -4, 5, -6]);
}
{
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_checked(6).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(left, [1, -2, 3, -4, 5, -6]);
    assert_eq!(right, []);
}
assert_eq!(None, v.split_at_checked(7));
```

Returns an iterator over subslices separated by elements that match
`pred`. The matched element is not contained in the subslices.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-53)Examples

```
let slice = [10, 40, 33, 20];
let mut iter = slice.split(|num| num % 3 == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[10, 40]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[20]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
If the first element is matched, an empty slice will be the first item returned by the iterator. Similarly, if the last element in the slice is matched, an empty slice will be the last item returned by the iterator:

```
let slice = [10, 40, 33];
let mut iter = slice.split(|num| num % 3 == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[10, 40]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
If two matched elements are directly adjacent, an empty slice will be present between them:

```
let slice = [10, 6, 33, 20];
let mut iter = slice.split(|num| num % 3 == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[10]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[20]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
Returns an iterator over mutable subslices separated by elements that
match `pred`. The matched element is not contained in the subslices.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-54)Examples

```
let mut v = [10, 40, 30, 20, 60, 50];
for group in v.split_mut(|num| *num % 3 == 0) {
    group[0] = 1;
}
assert_eq!(v, [1, 40, 30, 1, 60, 1]);
```

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2528-2530)#### pub fn [split_once](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.split_once)<F>(&self, pred: F) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))>

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2528-2530)

#### pub fn [split_once](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.split_once)<F>(&self, pred: F) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))>

`slice_split_once`)Splits the slice on the first element that matches the specified predicate.

If any matching elements are present in the slice, returns the prefix
before the match and suffix after. The matching element itself is not
included. If no elements match, returns `None`.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-63)Examples

```
#![feature(slice_split_once)]
let s = [1, 2, 3, 2, 4];
assert_eq!(s.split_once(|&x| x == 2), Some((
    &[1][..],
    &[3, 2, 4][..]
)));
assert_eq!(s.split_once(|&x| x == 0), None);
```
[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2556-2558)#### pub fn [rsplit_once](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.rsplit_once)<F>(&self, pred: F) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))>

`slice_split_once`)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#2556-2558)

#### pub fn [rsplit_once](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.rsplit_once)<F>(&self, pred: F) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))>

If any matching elements are present in the slice, returns the prefix
before the match and suffix after. The matching element itself is not
included. If no elements match, returns `None`.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#examples-64)Examples
