[544](https://fizyk20.github.io#544)/// Defines a `GenericSequence` which can be shortened by removing an element at a given index.
[545](https://fizyk20.github.io#545)///
[546](https://fizyk20.github.io#546)/// # Safety
[547](https://fizyk20.github.io#547)/// While the [`remove`](Remove::remove) and [`swap_remove`](Remove::swap_remove) methods are marked safe,
[548](https://fizyk20.github.io#548)/// care must be taken when implementing it. The [`remove_unchecked`](Remove::remove_unchecked)
[549](https://fizyk20.github.io#549)/// and [`swap_remove_unchecked`](Remove::swap_remove_unchecked) methods are unsafe
[550](https://fizyk20.github.io#550)/// and must be used with caution.
[551](https://fizyk20.github.io#551)pub unsafe trait Remove<T, N: ArrayLength>: GenericSequence<T> {
[552](https://fizyk20.github.io#552)    /// Resulting sequence formed by removing an element at the given index.
[553](https://fizyk20.github.io#553)    type Output: GenericSequence<T>;
[554](https://fizyk20.github.io#554)
[555](https://fizyk20.github.io#555)    /// Removes an element at the given index, shifting elements
[556](https://fizyk20.github.io#556)    /// after the given index to the left to fill the gap, resulting
[557](https://fizyk20.github.io#557)    /// in a time complexity of O(n) where `n=N-idx-1`
[558](https://fizyk20.github.io#558)    ///
[559](https://fizyk20.github.io#559)    /// # Example
[560](https://fizyk20.github.io#560)    ///
[561](https://fizyk20.github.io#561)    /// ```rust
[562](https://fizyk20.github.io#562)    /// # use generic_array::{arr, sequence::Remove};
[563](https://fizyk20.github.io#563)    /// let a = arr![1, 2, 3, 4];
[564](https://fizyk20.github.io#564)    ///
[565](https://fizyk20.github.io#565)    /// let (removed, b) = a.remove(2);
[566](https://fizyk20.github.io#566)    /// assert_eq!(removed, 3);
[567](https://fizyk20.github.io#567)    /// assert_eq!(b, arr![1, 2, 4]);
[568](https://fizyk20.github.io#568)    /// ```
[569](https://fizyk20.github.io#569)    ///
[570](https://fizyk20.github.io#570)    /// # Panics
[571](https://fizyk20.github.io#571)    ///
[572](https://fizyk20.github.io#572)    /// Panics if the index is out of bounds.
[573](https://fizyk20.github.io#573)    #[inline]
[574](https://fizyk20.github.io#574)    fn remove(self, idx: usize) -> (T, Self::Output) {
[575](https://fizyk20.github.io#575)        assert!(
[576](https://fizyk20.github.io#576)            idx < N::USIZE,
[577](https://fizyk20.github.io#577)            "Index out of bounds: the len is {} but the index is {}",
[578](https://fizyk20.github.io#578)            N::USIZE,
[579](https://fizyk20.github.io#579)            idx
[580](https://fizyk20.github.io#580)        );
[581](https://fizyk20.github.io#581)
[582](https://fizyk20.github.io#582)        unsafe { self.remove_unchecked(idx) }
[583](https://fizyk20.github.io#583)    }
[584](https://fizyk20.github.io#584)
[585](https://fizyk20.github.io#585)    /// Removes an element at the given index, swapping it with the last element.
[586](https://fizyk20.github.io#586)    ///
[587](https://fizyk20.github.io#587)    /// # Example
[588](https://fizyk20.github.io#588)    ///
[589](https://fizyk20.github.io#589)    /// ```rust
[590](https://fizyk20.github.io#590)    /// # use generic_array::{arr, sequence::Remove};
[591](https://fizyk20.github.io#591)    /// let a = arr![1, 2, 3, 4];
[592](https://fizyk20.github.io#592)    ///
[593](https://fizyk20.github.io#593)    /// let (removed, b) = a.swap_remove(1);
[594](https://fizyk20.github.io#594)    /// assert_eq!(removed, 2);
[595](https://fizyk20.github.io#595)    /// assert_eq!(b, arr![1, 4, 3]); // note 4 is now at index 1
[596](https://fizyk20.github.io#596)    /// ```
[597](https://fizyk20.github.io#597)    ///
[598](https://fizyk20.github.io#598)    /// # Panics
[599](https://fizyk20.github.io#599)    ///
[600](https://fizyk20.github.io#600)    /// Panics if the index is out of bounds.
[601](https://fizyk20.github.io#601)    fn swap_remove(self, idx: usize) -> (T, Self::Output) {
[602](https://fizyk20.github.io#602)        assert!(
[603](https://fizyk20.github.io#603)            idx < N::USIZE,
[604](https://fizyk20.github.io#604)            "Index out of bounds: the len is {} but the index is {}",
[605](https://fizyk20.github.io#605)            N::USIZE,
[606](https://fizyk20.github.io#606)            idx
[607](https://fizyk20.github.io#607)        );
[608](https://fizyk20.github.io#608)
[609](https://fizyk20.github.io#609)        unsafe { self.swap_remove_unchecked(idx) }
[610](https://fizyk20.github.io#610)    }
[611](https://fizyk20.github.io#611)
[612](https://fizyk20.github.io#612)    /// Removes an element at the given index without bounds checking,
[613](https://fizyk20.github.io#613)    /// shifting elements after the given index to the left to fill the gap,
[614](https://fizyk20.github.io#614)    /// resulting in a time complexity of O(n) where `n=N-idx-1`
[615](https://fizyk20.github.io#615)    ///
[616](https://fizyk20.github.io#616)    /// See [`remove`](Remove::remove) for an example.
[617](https://fizyk20.github.io#617)    ///
[618](https://fizyk20.github.io#618)    /// # Safety
[619](https://fizyk20.github.io#619)    /// The caller must ensure that the index is within bounds, otherwise
[620](https://fizyk20.github.io#620)    /// it is undefined behavior.
[621](https://fizyk20.github.io#621)    unsafe fn remove_unchecked(self, idx: usize) -> (T, Self::Output);
[622](https://fizyk20.github.io#622)
[623](https://fizyk20.github.io#623)    /// Removes an element at the given index without bounds checking, swapping it with the last element.
[624](https://fizyk20.github.io#624)    ///
[625](https://fizyk20.github.io#625)    /// See [`swap_remove`](Remove::swap_remove) for an example.
[626](https://fizyk20.github.io#626)    ///
[627](https://fizyk20.github.io#627)    /// # Safety
[628](https://fizyk20.github.io#628)    /// The caller must ensure that the index is within bounds, otherwise
[629](https://fizyk20.github.io#629)    /// it is undefined behavior.
[630](https://fizyk20.github.io#630)    unsafe fn swap_remove_unchecked(self, idx: usize) -> (T, Self::Output);
[631](https://fizyk20.github.io#631)}
[632](https://fizyk20.github.io#632)
[633](https://fizyk20.github.io#633)unsafe impl<T, N> Remove<T, N> for GenericArray<T, N>
[634](https://fizyk20.github.io#634)where
[635](https://fizyk20.github.io#635)    N: ArrayLength + Sub<B1>,
[636](https://fizyk20.github.io#636)    Sub1<N>: ArrayLength,
[637](https://fizyk20.github.io#637){
[638](https://fizyk20.github.io#638)    type Output = GenericArray<T, Sub1<N>>;
[639](https://fizyk20.github.io#639)
[640](https://fizyk20.github.io#640)    #[inline]
[641](https://fizyk20.github.io#641)    unsafe fn remove_unchecked(self, idx: usize) -> (T, Self::Output) {
[642](https://fizyk20.github.io#642)        if idx >= N::USIZE || N::USIZE == 0 {
[643](https://fizyk20.github.io#643)            core::hint::unreachable_unchecked();
[644](https://fizyk20.github.io#644)        }
[645](https://fizyk20.github.io#645)
[646](https://fizyk20.github.io#646)        let mut array = ManuallyDrop::new(self);
[647](https://fizyk20.github.io#647)
[648](https://fizyk20.github.io#648)        let dst = array.as_mut_ptr().add(idx);
[649](https://fizyk20.github.io#649)
[650](https://fizyk20.github.io#650)        let removed = ptr::read(dst);
[651](https://fizyk20.github.io#651)
[652](https://fizyk20.github.io#652)        // shift all elements over by one to fill gap
[653](https://fizyk20.github.io#653)        ptr::copy(dst.add(1), dst, N::USIZE - idx - 1);
[654](https://fizyk20.github.io#654)
[655](https://fizyk20.github.io#655)        // return removed element and truncated array
[656](https://fizyk20.github.io#656)        (removed, mem::transmute_copy(&array))
[657](https://fizyk20.github.io#657)    }
[658](https://fizyk20.github.io#658)
[659](https://fizyk20.github.io#659)    #[inline]
[660](https://fizyk20.github.io#660)    unsafe fn swap_remove_unchecked(self, idx: usize) -> (T, Self::Output) {
[661](https://fizyk20.github.io#661)        if idx >= N::USIZE || N::USIZE == 0 {
[662](https://fizyk20.github.io#662)            core::hint::unreachable_unchecked();
[663](https://fizyk20.github.io#663)        }
[664](https://fizyk20.github.io#664)
[665](https://fizyk20.github.io#665)        let mut array = ManuallyDrop::new(self);
[666](https://fizyk20.github.io#666)
[667](https://fizyk20.github.io#667)        array.swap(idx, N::USIZE - 1);
[668](https://fizyk20.github.io#668)
[669](https://fizyk20.github.io#669)        // remove the last element
[670](https://fizyk20.github.io#670)        let removed = ptr::read(array.as_ptr().add(N::USIZE - 1));
[671](https://fizyk20.github.io#671)
[672](https://fizyk20.github.io#672)        // return removed element and truncated array
[673](https://fizyk20.github.io#673)        (removed, mem::transmute_copy(&array))
[674](https://fizyk20.github.io#674)    }

# ConditionallySelectable in subtle - Rust

Source: https://fizyk20.github.io/generic-array/subtle/trait.ConditionallySelectable.html

`pub trait ConditionallySelectable: `[Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html) {
    // Required method
    fn [conditional_select](https://fizyk20.github.io#tymethod.conditional_select)(a: &Self, b: &Self, choice: [Choice](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.Choice.html)) -> Self;
    // Provided methods
    fn [conditional_assign](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.conditional_assign)(&mut self, other: &Self, choice: [Choice](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.Choice.html)) { ... }
[conditional_swap](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.conditional_swap)(a: &mut Self, b: &mut Self, choice: [Choice](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.Choice.html)) { ... }
}## Expand description

A type which can be conditionally selected in constant time.

This trait also provides generic implementations of conditional assignment and conditional swaps.

## Required Methods[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#required-methods)

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/subtle/lib.rs.html#420)#### fn [conditional_select](https://fizyk20.github.io#tymethod.conditional_select)(a: &Self, b: &Self, choice: [Choice](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.Choice.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/subtle/lib.rs.html#420)

#### fn [conditional_select](https://fizyk20.github.io#tymethod.conditional_select)(a: &Self, b: &Self, choice: [Choice](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.Choice.html)) -> Self

Select `a` or `b` according to `choice`.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#returns)Returns

- `a`if- `choice == Choice(0)`;
- `b`if- `choice == Choice(1)`.

This function should execute in constant time.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#example)Example

```
use subtle::ConditionallySelectable;
let x: u8 = 13;
let y: u8 = 42;
let z = u8::conditional_select(&x, &y, 0.into());
assert_eq!(z, x);
let z = u8::conditional_select(&x, &y, 1.into());
assert_eq!(z, y);
```
## Provided Methods[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#provided-methods)

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/subtle/lib.rs.html#442-444)#### fn [conditional_assign](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.conditional_assign)(&mut self, other: &Self, choice: [Choice](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.Choice.html))

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/subtle/lib.rs.html#442-444)

#### fn [conditional_assign](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.conditional_assign)(&mut self, other: &Self, choice: [Choice](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.Choice.html))

Conditionally assign `other` to `self`, according to `choice`.

This function should execute in constant time.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#example-1)Example

```
use subtle::ConditionallySelectable;
let mut x: u8 = 13;
let mut y: u8 = 42;
x.conditional_assign(&y, 0.into());
assert_eq!(x, 13);
x.conditional_assign(&y, 1.into());
assert_eq!(x, 42);
```
[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/subtle/lib.rs.html#469-473)#### fn [conditional_swap](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.conditional_swap)(a: &mut Self, b: &mut Self, choice: [Choice](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.Choice.html))

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/subtle/lib.rs.html#469-473)

#### fn [conditional_swap](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.conditional_swap)(a: &mut Self, b: &mut Self, choice: [Choice](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.Choice.html))

Conditionally swap `self` and `other` if `choice == 1`; otherwise,
reassign both unto themselves.

This function should execute in constant time.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#example-2)Example

```
use subtle::ConditionallySelectable;
let mut x: u8 = 13;
let mut y: u8 = 42;
u8::conditional_swap(&mut x, &mut y, 0.into());
assert_eq!(x, 13);
assert_eq!(y, 42);
u8::conditional_swap(&mut x, &mut y, 1.into());
assert_eq!(x, 42);
assert_eq!(y, 13);
```

- `Less`=> -1
- `Equal`=> 0
- `Greater`=> 1

Given this, it’s possible to operate on orderings as if they’re integers, which allows leveraging conditional masking for predication.

# Choice in subtle - Rust

Source: https://fizyk20.github.io/generic-array/subtle/struct.Choice.html

`pub struct Choice(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

The `Choice` struct represents a choice for use in conditional assignment.

It is a wrapper around a `u8`, which should have the value either `1` (true)
or `0` (false).

The conversion from `u8` to `Choice` passes the value through an optimization
barrier, as a best-effort attempt to prevent the compiler from inferring that
the `Choice` value is a boolean. This strategy is based on Tim Maclean’s
[work on  rust-timing-shield](https://www.chosenplaintext.ca/open-source/rust-timing-shield/security), which attempts to provide
a more comprehensive approach for preventing software side-channels in Rust
code.

The `Choice` struct implements operators for AND, OR, XOR, and NOT, to allow
combining `Choice` values. These operations do not short-circuit.

## Implementations[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#implementations)

### impl [ConditionallySelectable](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.ConditionallySelectable.html) for [Choice](https://fizyk20.github.io/struct.Choice.html)

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/subtle/lib.rs.html#119)

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#impl-Copy-for-Choice)

Convert the `Choice` wrapper into a `bool`, depending on whether
the underlying `u8` was a `0` or a `1`.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#note-1)Note

This function exists to avoid having higher-level cryptographic protocol implementations duplicating this pattern.

The intended use case for this conversion is at the *end* of a
higher-level primitive implementation: for example, in checking a keyed
MAC, where the verification should happen in constant-time (and thus use
a `Choice`) but it is safe to return a `bool` at the end of the
verification.

[14](https://fizyk20.github.io#14)#![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/subtle/2.6.0")]

[16](https://fizyk20.github.io#16)//! # subtle [![](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/subtle.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/subtle) [![](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json.svg?label=docs&uri=https%3A%2F%2Fcrates.io%2Fapi%2Fv1%2Fcrates%2Fsubtle%2Fversions&query=%24.versions%5B0%5D.num&colorB=4F74A6)](https://doc.dalek.rs/subtle) [![](https://travis-ci.org/dalek-cryptography/subtle.svg?branch=master)](https://travis-ci.org/dalek-cryptography/subtle)
[17](https://fizyk20.github.io#17)//!
[18](https://fizyk20.github.io#18)//! **Pure-Rust traits and utilities for constant-time cryptographic implementations.**
[19](https://fizyk20.github.io#19)//!
[20](https://fizyk20.github.io#20)//! It consists of a `Choice` type, and a collection of traits using `Choice`
[21](https://fizyk20.github.io#21)//! instead of `bool` which are intended to execute in constant-time.  The `Choice`
[22](https://fizyk20.github.io#22)//! type is a wrapper around a `u8` that holds a `0` or `1`.
[23](https://fizyk20.github.io#23)//!
[24](https://fizyk20.github.io#24)//! ```toml
[25](https://fizyk20.github.io#25)//! subtle = "2.6"
[26](https://fizyk20.github.io#26)//! ```
[27](https://fizyk20.github.io#27)//!
[28](https://fizyk20.github.io#28)//! This crate represents a “best-effort” attempt, since side-channels
[29](https://fizyk20.github.io#29)//! are ultimately a property of a deployed cryptographic system
[30](https://fizyk20.github.io#30)//! including the hardware it runs on, not just of software.
[31](https://fizyk20.github.io#31)//!
[32](https://fizyk20.github.io#32)//! The traits are implemented using bitwise operations, and should execute in
[33](https://fizyk20.github.io#33)//! constant time provided that a) the bitwise operations are constant-time and
[34](https://fizyk20.github.io#34)//! b) the bitwise operations are not recognized as a conditional assignment and
[35](https://fizyk20.github.io#35)//! optimized back into a branch.
[36](https://fizyk20.github.io#36)//!
[37](https://fizyk20.github.io#37)//! For a compiler to recognize that bitwise operations represent a conditional
[38](https://fizyk20.github.io#38)//! assignment, it needs to know that the value used to generate the bitmasks is
[39](https://fizyk20.github.io#39)//! really a boolean `i1` rather than an `i8` byte value. In an attempt to
[40](https://fizyk20.github.io#40)//! prevent this refinement, the crate tries to hide the value of a `Choice`'s
[41](https://fizyk20.github.io#41)//! inner `u8` by passing it through a volatile read. For more information, see
[42](https://fizyk20.github.io#42)//! the _About_ section below.
[43](https://fizyk20.github.io#43)//!
[44](https://fizyk20.github.io#44)//! Rust versions from 1.51 or higher have const generics support. You may enable
[45](https://fizyk20.github.io#45)//! `const-generics` feautre to have `subtle` traits implemented for arrays `[T; N]`.
[46](https://fizyk20.github.io#46)//!
[47](https://fizyk20.github.io#47)//! Versions prior to `2.2` recommended use of the `nightly` feature to enable an
[48](https://fizyk20.github.io#48)//! optimization barrier; this is not required in versions `2.2` and above.
[49](https://fizyk20.github.io#49)//!
[50](https://fizyk20.github.io#50)//! Note: the `subtle` crate contains `debug_assert`s to check invariants during
[51](https://fizyk20.github.io#51)//! debug builds. These invariant checks involve secret-dependent branches, and
[52](https://fizyk20.github.io#52)//! are not present when compiled in release mode. This crate is intended to be
[53](https://fizyk20.github.io#53)//! used in release mode.
[54](https://fizyk20.github.io#54)//!
[55](https://fizyk20.github.io#55)//! ## Documentation
[56](https://fizyk20.github.io#56)//!
[57](https://fizyk20.github.io#57)//! Documentation is available [here][docs].
[58](https://fizyk20.github.io#58)//!
[59](https://fizyk20.github.io#59)//! ## Minimum Supported Rust Version
[60](https://fizyk20.github.io#60)//!
[61](https://fizyk20.github.io#61)//! Rust **1.41** or higher.
[62](https://fizyk20.github.io#62)//!
[63](https://fizyk20.github.io#63)//! Minimum supported Rust version can be changed in the future, but it will be done with a minor version bump.
[64](https://fizyk20.github.io#64)//!
[65](https://fizyk20.github.io#65)//! ## About
[66](https://fizyk20.github.io#66)//!
[67](https://fizyk20.github.io#67)//! This library aims to be the Rust equivalent of Go’s `crypto/subtle` module.
[68](https://fizyk20.github.io#68)//!
[69](https://fizyk20.github.io#69)//! Old versions of the optimization barrier in `impl From<u8> for Choice` were
[70](https://fizyk20.github.io#70)//! based on Tim Maclean's [work on `rust-timing-shield`][rust-timing-shield],
[71](https://fizyk20.github.io#71)//! which attempts to provide a more comprehensive approach for preventing
[72](https://fizyk20.github.io#72)//! software side-channels in Rust code.
[73](https://fizyk20.github.io#73)//! From version `2.2`, it was based on Diane Hosfelt and Amber Sprenkels' work on
[74](https://fizyk20.github.io#74)//! "Secret Types in Rust".
[75](https://fizyk20.github.io#75)//!
[76](https://fizyk20.github.io#76)//! `subtle` is authored by isis agora lovecruft and Henry de Valence.
[77](https://fizyk20.github.io#77)//!
[78](https://fizyk20.github.io#78)//! ## Warning
[79](https://fizyk20.github.io#79)//!
[80](https://fizyk20.github.io#80)//! This code is a low-level library, intended for specific use-cases implementing
[81](https://fizyk20.github.io#81)//! cryptographic protocols.  It represents a best-effort attempt to protect
[82](https://fizyk20.github.io#82)//! against some software side-channels.  Because side-channel resistance is not a
[83](https://fizyk20.github.io#83)//! property of software alone, but of software together with hardware, any such
[84](https://fizyk20.github.io#84)//! effort is fundamentally limited.
[85](https://fizyk20.github.io#85)//!
[86](https://fizyk20.github.io#86)//! **USE AT YOUR OWN RISK**
[87](https://fizyk20.github.io#87)//!

[89](https://fizyk20.github.io#89)//! [rust-timing-shield]: https://www.chosenplaintext.ca/open-source/rust-timing-shield/security

[102](https://fizyk20.github.io#102)/// The `Choice` struct represents a choice for use in conditional assignment.
[103](https://fizyk20.github.io#103)///
[104](https://fizyk20.github.io#104)/// It is a wrapper around a `u8`, which should have the value either `1` (true)
[105](https://fizyk20.github.io#105)/// or `0` (false).
[106](https://fizyk20.github.io#106)///
[107](https://fizyk20.github.io#107)/// The conversion from `u8` to `Choice` passes the value through an optimization
[108](https://fizyk20.github.io#108)/// barrier, as a best-effort attempt to prevent the compiler from inferring that
[109](https://fizyk20.github.io#109)/// the `Choice` value is a boolean. This strategy is based on Tim Maclean's
[110](https://fizyk20.github.io#110)/// [work on `rust-timing-shield`][rust-timing-shield], which attempts to provide
[111](https://fizyk20.github.io#111)/// a more comprehensive approach for preventing software side-channels in Rust
[112](https://fizyk20.github.io#112)/// code.
[113](https://fizyk20.github.io#113)///
[114](https://fizyk20.github.io#114)/// The `Choice` struct implements operators for AND, OR, XOR, and NOT, to allow
[115](https://fizyk20.github.io#115)/// combining `Choice` values. These operations do not short-circuit.
[116](https://fizyk20.github.io#116)///
[117](https://fizyk20.github.io#117)/// [rust-timing-shield]:
[118](https://fizyk20.github.io#118)/// https://www.chosenplaintext.ca/open-source/rust-timing-shield/security
[119](https://fizyk20.github.io#119)#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug)]
[120](https://fizyk20.github.io#120)pub struct Choice(u8);
[121](https://fizyk20.github.io#121)
[122](https://fizyk20.github.io#122)impl Choice {
[123](https://fizyk20.github.io#123)    /// Unwrap the `Choice` wrapper to reveal the underlying `u8`.
[124](https://fizyk20.github.io#124)    ///
[125](https://fizyk20.github.io#125)    /// # Note
[126](https://fizyk20.github.io#126)    ///
[127](https://fizyk20.github.io#127)    /// This function only exists as an **escape hatch** for the rare case
[128](https://fizyk20.github.io#128)    /// where it's not possible to use one of the `subtle`-provided
[129](https://fizyk20.github.io#129)    /// trait impls.
[130](https://fizyk20.github.io#130)    ///
[131](https://fizyk20.github.io#131)    /// **To convert a `Choice` to a `bool`, use the `From` implementation instead.**
[132](https://fizyk20.github.io#132)    #[inline]
[133](https://fizyk20.github.io#133)    pub fn unwrap_u8(&self) -> u8 {
[134](https://fizyk20.github.io#134)        self.0
[135](https://fizyk20.github.io#135)    }
[136](https://fizyk20.github.io#136)}

[138](https://fizyk20.github.io#138)impl From<Choice> for bool {
[139](https://fizyk20.github.io#139)    /// Convert the `Choice` wrapper into a `bool`, depending on whether
[140](https://fizyk20.github.io#140)    /// the underlying `u8` was a `0` or a `1`.
[141](https://fizyk20.github.io#141)    ///
[142](https://fizyk20.github.io#142)    /// # Note
[143](https://fizyk20.github.io#143)    ///
[144](https://fizyk20.github.io#144)    /// This function exists to avoid having higher-level cryptographic protocol
[145](https://fizyk20.github.io#145)    /// implementations duplicating this pattern.
[146](https://fizyk20.github.io#146)    ///
[147](https://fizyk20.github.io#147)    /// The intended use case for this conversion is at the _end_ of a
[148](https://fizyk20.github.io#148)    /// higher-level primitive implementation: for example, in checking a keyed
[149](https://fizyk20.github.io#149)    /// MAC, where the verification should happen in constant-time (and thus use
[150](https://fizyk20.github.io#150)    /// a `Choice`) but it is safe to return a `bool` at the end of the
[151](https://fizyk20.github.io#151)    /// verification.
[152](https://fizyk20.github.io#152)    #[inline]
[153](https://fizyk20.github.io#153)    fn from(source: Choice) -> bool {
[154](https://fizyk20.github.io#154)        debug_assert!((source.0 == 0u8) | (source.0 == 1u8));
[155](https://fizyk20.github.io#155)        source.0 != 0
[156](https://fizyk20.github.io#156)    }
[157](https://fizyk20.github.io#157)}
[158](https://fizyk20.github.io#158)
[159](https://fizyk20.github.io#159)impl BitAnd for Choice {

[162](https://fizyk20.github.io#162)    fn bitand(self, rhs: Choice) -> Choice {
[163](https://fizyk20.github.io#163)        (self.0 & rhs.0).into()
[164](https://fizyk20.github.io#164)    }
[165](https://fizyk20.github.io#165)}

[211](https://fizyk20.github.io#211)
[212](https://fizyk20.github.io#212)/// This function is a best-effort attempt to prevent the compiler from knowing
[213](https://fizyk20.github.io#213)/// anything about the value of the returned `u8`, other than its type.
[214](https://fizyk20.github.io#214)///
[215](https://fizyk20.github.io#215)/// Because we want to support stable Rust, we don't have access to inline
[216](https://fizyk20.github.io#216)/// assembly or test::black_box, so we use the fact that volatile values will
[217](https://fizyk20.github.io#217)/// never be elided to register values.
[218](https://fizyk20.github.io#218)///
[219](https://fizyk20.github.io#219)/// Note: Rust's notion of "volatile" is subject to change over time. While this
[220](https://fizyk20.github.io#220)/// code may break in a non-destructive way in the future, “constant-time” code
[221](https://fizyk20.github.io#221)/// is a continually moving target, and this is better than doing nothing.
[222](https://fizyk20.github.io#222)#[cfg(not(feature = "core_hint_black_box"))]
[223](https://fizyk20.github.io#223)#[inline(never)]
[224](https://fizyk20.github.io#224)fn black_box<T: Copy>(input: T) -> T {
[225](https://fizyk20.github.io#225)    unsafe {
[226](https://fizyk20.github.io#226)        // Optimization barrier
[227](https://fizyk20.github.io#227)        //
[228](https://fizyk20.github.io#228)        // SAFETY:
[229](https://fizyk20.github.io#229)        //   - &input is not NULL because we own input;
[230](https://fizyk20.github.io#230)        //   - input is Copy and always live;
[231](https://fizyk20.github.io#231)        //   - input is always properly aligned.
[232](https://fizyk20.github.io#232)        core::ptr::read_volatile(&input)
[233](https://fizyk20.github.io#233)    }
[234](https://fizyk20.github.io#234)}
[235](https://fizyk20.github.io#235)
[236](https://fizyk20.github.io#236)impl From<u8> for Choice {
[237](https://fizyk20.github.io#237)    #[inline]
[238](https://fizyk20.github.io#238)    fn from(input: u8) -> Choice {
[239](https://fizyk20.github.io#239)        debug_assert!((input == 0u8) | (input == 1u8));
[240](https://fizyk20.github.io#240)
[241](https://fizyk20.github.io#241)        // Our goal is to prevent the compiler from inferring that the value held inside the
[242](https://fizyk20.github.io#242)        // resulting `Choice` struct is really a `bool` instead of a `u8`.
[243](https://fizyk20.github.io#243)        Choice(black_box(input))
[244](https://fizyk20.github.io#244)    }
[245](https://fizyk20.github.io#245)}
[246](https://fizyk20.github.io#246)
[247](https://fizyk20.github.io#247)/// An `Eq`-like trait that produces a `Choice` instead of a `bool`.
[248](https://fizyk20.github.io#248)///
[249](https://fizyk20.github.io#249)/// # Example
[250](https://fizyk20.github.io#250)///
[251](https://fizyk20.github.io#251)/// ```
[252](https://fizyk20.github.io#252)/// use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
[253](https://fizyk20.github.io#253)/// let x: u8 = 5;
[254](https://fizyk20.github.io#254)/// let y: u8 = 13;
[255](https://fizyk20.github.io#255)///
[256](https://fizyk20.github.io#256)/// assert_eq!(x.ct_eq(&y).unwrap_u8(), 0);
[257](https://fizyk20.github.io#257)/// assert_eq!(x.ct_eq(&x).unwrap_u8(), 1);
[258](https://fizyk20.github.io#258)/// ```
[259](https://fizyk20.github.io#259)//
[260](https://fizyk20.github.io#260)// #[inline] is specified on these function prototypes to signify that they
[261](https://fizyk20.github.io#261)#[allow(unused_attributes)] // should be in the actual implementation
[262](https://fizyk20.github.io#262)pub trait ConstantTimeEq {
[263](https://fizyk20.github.io#263)    /// Determine if two items are equal.
[264](https://fizyk20.github.io#264)    ///
[265](https://fizyk20.github.io#265)    /// The `ct_eq` function should execute in constant time.
[266](https://fizyk20.github.io#266)    ///
[267](https://fizyk20.github.io#267)    /// # Returns
[268](https://fizyk20.github.io#268)    ///
[269](https://fizyk20.github.io#269)    /// * `Choice(1u8)` if `self == other`;
[270](https://fizyk20.github.io#270)    /// * `Choice(0u8)` if `self != other`.
[271](https://fizyk20.github.io#271)    #[inline]
[272](https://fizyk20.github.io#272)    #[allow(unused_attributes)]
[273](https://fizyk20.github.io#273)    fn ct_eq(&self, other: &Self) -> Choice;
[274](https://fizyk20.github.io#274)
[275](https://fizyk20.github.io#275)    /// Determine if two items are NOT equal.
[276](https://fizyk20.github.io#276)    ///
[277](https://fizyk20.github.io#277)    /// The `ct_ne` function should execute in constant time.
[278](https://fizyk20.github.io#278)    ///
[279](https://fizyk20.github.io#279)    /// # Returns
[280](https://fizyk20.github.io#280)    ///
[281](https://fizyk20.github.io#281)    /// * `Choice(0u8)` if `self == other`;
[282](https://fizyk20.github.io#282)    /// * `Choice(1u8)` if `self != other`.
[283](https://fizyk20.github.io#283)    #[inline]
[284](https://fizyk20.github.io#284)    fn ct_ne(&self, other: &Self) -> Choice {
[285](https://fizyk20.github.io#285)        !self.ct_eq(other)
[286](https://fizyk20.github.io#286)    }
[287](https://fizyk20.github.io#287)}
[288](https://fizyk20.github.io#288)
[289](https://fizyk20.github.io#289)impl<T: ConstantTimeEq> ConstantTimeEq for [T] {
[290](https://fizyk20.github.io#290)    /// Check whether two slices of `ConstantTimeEq` types are equal.
[291](https://fizyk20.github.io#291)    ///
[292](https://fizyk20.github.io#292)    /// # Note
[293](https://fizyk20.github.io#293)    ///
[294](https://fizyk20.github.io#294)    /// This function short-circuits if the lengths of the input slices
[295](https://fizyk20.github.io#295)    /// are different.  Otherwise, it should execute in time independent
[296](https://fizyk20.github.io#296)    /// of the slice contents.
[297](https://fizyk20.github.io#297)    ///
[298](https://fizyk20.github.io#298)    /// Since arrays coerce to slices, this function works with fixed-size arrays:
[299](https://fizyk20.github.io#299)    ///
[300](https://fizyk20.github.io#300)    /// ```
[301](https://fizyk20.github.io#301)    /// # use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
[302](https://fizyk20.github.io#302)    /// #
[303](https://fizyk20.github.io#303)    /// let a: [u8; 8] = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7];
[304](https://fizyk20.github.io#304)    /// let b: [u8; 8] = [0,1,2,3,0,1,2,3];
[305](https://fizyk20.github.io#305)    ///
[306](https://fizyk20.github.io#306)    /// let a_eq_a = a.ct_eq(&a);
[307](https://fizyk20.github.io#307)    /// let a_eq_b = a.ct_eq(&b);
[308](https://fizyk20.github.io#308)    ///
[309](https://fizyk20.github.io#309)    /// assert_eq!(a_eq_a.unwrap_u8(), 1);
[310](https://fizyk20.github.io#310)    /// assert_eq!(a_eq_b.unwrap_u8(), 0);
[311](https://fizyk20.github.io#311)    /// ```
[312](https://fizyk20.github.io#312)    #[inline]
[313](https://fizyk20.github.io#313)    fn ct_eq(&self, _rhs: &[T]) -> Choice {
[314](https://fizyk20.github.io#314)        let len = self.len();
[315](https://fizyk20.github.io#315)
[316](https://fizyk20.github.io#316)        // Short-circuit on the *lengths* of the slices, not their
[317](https://fizyk20.github.io#317)        // contents.
[318](https://fizyk20.github.io#318)        if len != _rhs.len() {
[319](https://fizyk20.github.io#319)            return Choice::from(0);
[320](https://fizyk20.github.io#320)        }
[321](https://fizyk20.github.io#321)
[322](https://fizyk20.github.io#322)        // This loop shouldn't be shortcircuitable, since the compiler
[323](https://fizyk20.github.io#323)        // shouldn't be able to reason about the value of the `u8`
[324](https://fizyk20.github.io#324)        // unwrapped from the `ct_eq` result.
[325](https://fizyk20.github.io#325)        let mut x = 1u8;
[326](https://fizyk20.github.io#326)        for (ai, bi) in self.iter().zip(_rhs.iter()) {
[327](https://fizyk20.github.io#327)            x &= ai.ct_eq(bi).unwrap_u8();
[328](https://fizyk20.github.io#328)        }
[329](https://fizyk20.github.io#329)
[330](https://fizyk20.github.io#330)        x.into()
[331](https://fizyk20.github.io#331)    }
[332](https://fizyk20.github.io#332)}
[333](https://fizyk20.github.io#333)
[334](https://fizyk20.github.io#334)impl ConstantTimeEq for Choice {
[335](https://fizyk20.github.io#335)    #[inline]
[336](https://fizyk20.github.io#336)    fn ct_eq(&self, rhs: &Choice) -> Choice {
[337](https://fizyk20.github.io#337)        !(*self ^ *rhs)
[338](https://fizyk20.github.io#338)    }
[339](https://fizyk20.github.io#339)}
[340](https://fizyk20.github.io#340)
[341](https://fizyk20.github.io#341)/// Given the bit-width `$bit_width` and the corresponding primitive
[342](https://fizyk20.github.io#342)/// unsigned and signed types `$t_u` and `$t_i` respectively, generate
[343](https://fizyk20.github.io#343)/// an `ConstantTimeEq` implementation.
[344](https://fizyk20.github.io#344)macro_rules! generate_integer_equal {
[345](https://fizyk20.github.io#345)    ($t_u:ty, $t_i:ty, $bit_width:expr) => {
[346](https://fizyk20.github.io#346)        impl ConstantTimeEq for $t_u {
[347](https://fizyk20.github.io#347)            #[inline]
[348](https://fizyk20.github.io#348)            fn ct_eq(&self, other: &$t_u) -> Choice {
[349](https://fizyk20.github.io#349)                // x == 0 if and only if self == other
[350](https://fizyk20.github.io#350)                let x: $t_u = self ^ other;
[351](https://fizyk20.github.io#351)
[352](https://fizyk20.github.io#352)                // If x == 0, then x and -x are both equal to zero;
[353](https://fizyk20.github.io#353)                // otherwise, one or both will have its high bit set.
[354](https://fizyk20.github.io#354)                let y: $t_u = (x | x.wrapping_neg()) >> ($bit_width - 1);
[355](https://fizyk20.github.io#355)
[356](https://fizyk20.github.io#356)                // Result is the opposite of the high bit (now shifted to low).
[357](https://fizyk20.github.io#357)                ((y ^ (1 as $t_u)) as u8).into()
[358](https://fizyk20.github.io#358)            }
[359](https://fizyk20.github.io#359)        }
[360](https://fizyk20.github.io#360)        impl ConstantTimeEq for $t_i {
[361](https://fizyk20.github.io#361)            #[inline]
[362](https://fizyk20.github.io#362)            fn ct_eq(&self, other: &$t_i) -> Choice {
[363](https://fizyk20.github.io#363)                // Bitcast to unsigned and call that implementation.
[364](https://fizyk20.github.io#364)                (*self as $t_u).ct_eq(&(*other as $t_u))
[365](https://fizyk20.github.io#365)            }
[366](https://fizyk20.github.io#366)        }
[367](https://fizyk20.github.io#367)    };
[368](https://fizyk20.github.io#368)}

[386](https://fizyk20.github.io#386)/// A type which can be conditionally selected in constant time.
[387](https://fizyk20.github.io#387)///
[388](https://fizyk20.github.io#388)/// This trait also provides generic implementations of conditional
[389](https://fizyk20.github.io#389)/// assignment and conditional swaps.

[395](https://fizyk20.github.io#395)    ///
[396](https://fizyk20.github.io#396)    /// # Returns

[400](https://fizyk20.github.io#400)    ///
[401](https://fizyk20.github.io#401)    /// This function should execute in constant time.
[402](https://fizyk20.github.io#402)    ///

[404](https://fizyk20.github.io#404)    ///

[416](https://fizyk20.github.io#416)    /// # }
[417](https://fizyk20.github.io#417)    /// ```

[420](https://fizyk20.github.io#420)    fn conditional_select(a: &Self, b: &Self, choice: Choice) -> Self;

[422](https://fizyk20.github.io#422)    /// Conditionally assign `other` to `self`, according to `choice`.
[423](https://fizyk20.github.io#423)    ///
[424](https://fizyk20.github.io#424)    /// This function should execute in constant time.
[425](https://fizyk20.github.io#425)    ///
[426](https://fizyk20.github.io#426)    /// # Example
[427](https://fizyk20.github.io#427)    ///

[429](https://fizyk20.github.io#429)    /// use subtle::ConditionallySelectable;
[430](https://fizyk20.github.io#430)    /// #
[431](https://fizyk20.github.io#431)    /// # fn main() {
[432](https://fizyk20.github.io#432)    /// let mut x: u8 = 13;
[433](https://fizyk20.github.io#433)    /// let mut y: u8 = 42;
[434](https://fizyk20.github.io#434)    ///
[435](https://fizyk20.github.io#435)    /// x.conditional_assign(&y, 0.into());
[436](https://fizyk20.github.io#436)    /// assert_eq!(x, 13);
[437](https://fizyk20.github.io#437)    /// x.conditional_assign(&y, 1.into());
[438](https://fizyk20.github.io#438)    /// assert_eq!(x, 42);
[439](https://fizyk20.github.io#439)    /// # }
[440](https://fizyk20.github.io#440)    /// ```
[441](https://fizyk20.github.io#441)    #[inline]
[442](https://fizyk20.github.io#442)    fn conditional_assign(&mut self, other: &Self, choice: Choice) {
[443](https://fizyk20.github.io#443)        *self = Self::conditional_select(self, other, choice);
[444](https://fizyk20.github.io#444)    }
[445](https://fizyk20.github.io#445)
[446](https://fizyk20.github.io#446)    /// Conditionally swap `self` and `other` if `choice == 1`; otherwise,
[447](https://fizyk20.github.io#447)    /// reassign both unto themselves.
[448](https://fizyk20.github.io#448)    ///
[449](https://fizyk20.github.io#449)    /// This function should execute in constant time.
[450](https://fizyk20.github.io#450)    ///
[451](https://fizyk20.github.io#451)    /// # Example
[452](https://fizyk20.github.io#452)    ///
[453](https://fizyk20.github.io#453)    /// ```
[454](https://fizyk20.github.io#454)    /// use subtle::ConditionallySelectable;
[455](https://fizyk20.github.io#455)    /// #
[456](https://fizyk20.github.io#456)    /// # fn main() {
[457](https://fizyk20.github.io#457)    /// let mut x: u8 = 13;
[458](https://fizyk20.github.io#458)    /// let mut y: u8 = 42;
[459](https://fizyk20.github.io#459)    ///
[460](https://fizyk20.github.io#460)    /// u8::conditional_swap(&mut x, &mut y, 0.into());
[461](https://fizyk20.github.io#461)    /// assert_eq!(x, 13);
[462](https://fizyk20.github.io#462)    /// assert_eq!(y, 42);
[463](https://fizyk20.github.io#463)    /// u8::conditional_swap(&mut x, &mut y, 1.into());
[464](https://fizyk20.github.io#464)    /// assert_eq!(x, 42);
[465](https://fizyk20.github.io#465)    /// assert_eq!(y, 13);
[466](https://fizyk20.github.io#466)    /// # }
[467](https://fizyk20.github.io#467)    /// ```
[468](https://fizyk20.github.io#468)    #[inline]
[469](https://fizyk20.github.io#469)    fn conditional_swap(a: &mut Self, b: &mut Self, choice: Choice) {
[470](https://fizyk20.github.io#470)        let t: Self = *a;
[471](https://fizyk20.github.io#471)        a.conditional_assign(&b, choice);
[472](https://fizyk20.github.io#472)        b.conditional_assign(&t, choice);
[473](https://fizyk20.github.io#473)    }

[509](https://fizyk20.github.io#509)macro_rules! generate_integer_conditional_select {
[510](https://fizyk20.github.io#510)    ($($t:tt)*) => ($(
[511](https://fizyk20.github.io#511)        impl ConditionallySelectable for $t {
[512](https://fizyk20.github.io#512)            #[inline]
[513](https://fizyk20.github.io#513)            fn conditional_select(a: &Self, b: &Self, choice: Choice) -> Self {
[514](https://fizyk20.github.io#514)                // if choice = 0, mask = (-0) = 0000...0000
[515](https://fizyk20.github.io#515)                // if choice = 1, mask = (-1) = 1111...1111
[516](https://fizyk20.github.io#516)                let mask = -(choice.unwrap_u8() as to_signed_int!($t)) as $t;
[517](https://fizyk20.github.io#517)                a ^ (mask & (a ^ b))
[518](https://fizyk20.github.io#518)            }
[519](https://fizyk20.github.io#519)
[520](https://fizyk20.github.io#520)            #[inline]
[521](https://fizyk20.github.io#521)            fn conditional_assign(&mut self, other: &Self, choice: Choice) {
[522](https://fizyk20.github.io#522)                // if choice = 0, mask = (-0) = 0000...0000
[523](https://fizyk20.github.io#523)                // if choice = 1, mask = (-1) = 1111...1111
[524](https://fizyk20.github.io#524)                let mask = -(choice.unwrap_u8() as to_signed_int!($t)) as $t;
[525](https://fizyk20.github.io#525)                *self ^= mask & (*self ^ *other);
[526](https://fizyk20.github.io#526)            }
[527](https://fizyk20.github.io#527)
[528](https://fizyk20.github.io#528)            #[inline]
[529](https://fizyk20.github.io#529)            fn conditional_swap(a: &mut Self, b: &mut Self, choice: Choice) {
[530](https://fizyk20.github.io#530)                // if choice = 0, mask = (-0) = 0000...0000
[531](https://fizyk20.github.io#531)                // if choice = 1, mask = (-1) = 1111...1111
[532](https://fizyk20.github.io#532)                let mask = -(choice.unwrap_u8() as to_signed_int!($t)) as $t;
[533](https://fizyk20.github.io#533)                let t = mask & (*a ^ *b);
[534](https://fizyk20.github.io#534)                *a ^= t;
[535](https://fizyk20.github.io#535)                *b ^= t;
[536](https://fizyk20.github.io#536)            }
[537](https://fizyk20.github.io#537)         }
[538](https://fizyk20.github.io#538)    )*)

[548](https://fizyk20.github.io#548)/// `Ordering` is `#[repr(i8)]` where:
[549](https://fizyk20.github.io#549)///
[550](https://fizyk20.github.io#550)/// - `Less` => -1
[551](https://fizyk20.github.io#551)/// - `Equal` => 0
[552](https://fizyk20.github.io#552)/// - `Greater` => 1
[553](https://fizyk20.github.io#553)///
[554](https://fizyk20.github.io#554)/// Given this, it's possible to operate on orderings as if they're integers,
[555](https://fizyk20.github.io#555)/// which allows leveraging conditional masking for predication.
[556](https://fizyk20.github.io#556)impl ConditionallySelectable for cmp::Ordering {
[557](https://fizyk20.github.io#557)    fn conditional_select(a: &Self, b: &Self, choice: Choice) -> Self {
[558](https://fizyk20.github.io#558)        let a = *a as i8;
[559](https://fizyk20.github.io#559)        let b = *b as i8;
[560](https://fizyk20.github.io#560)        let ret = i8::conditional_select(&a, &b, choice);
[561](https://fizyk20.github.io#561)
[562](https://fizyk20.github.io#562)        // SAFETY: `Ordering` is `#[repr(i8)]` and `ret` has been assigned to
[563](https://fizyk20.github.io#563)        // a value which was originally a valid `Ordering` then cast to `i8`
[564](https://fizyk20.github.io#564)        unsafe { *((&ret as *const _) as *const cmp::Ordering) }
[565](https://fizyk20.github.io#565)    }

[627](https://fizyk20.github.io#627)/// The `CtOption<T>` type represents an optional value similar to the
[628](https://fizyk20.github.io#628)/// [`Option<T>`](core::option::Option) type but is intended for
[629](https://fizyk20.github.io#629)/// use in constant time APIs.
[630](https://fizyk20.github.io#630)///
[631](https://fizyk20.github.io#631)/// Any given `CtOption<T>` is either `Some` or `None`, but unlike
[632](https://fizyk20.github.io#632)/// `Option<T>` these variants are not exposed. The
[633](https://fizyk20.github.io#633)/// [`is_some()`](CtOption::is_some) method is used to determine if
[634](https://fizyk20.github.io#634)/// the value is `Some`, and [`unwrap_or()`](CtOption::unwrap_or) and
[635](https://fizyk20.github.io#635)/// [`unwrap_or_else()`](CtOption::unwrap_or_else) methods are
[636](https://fizyk20.github.io#636)/// provided to access the underlying value. The value can also be
[637](https://fizyk20.github.io#637)/// obtained with [`unwrap()`](CtOption::unwrap) but this will panic
[638](https://fizyk20.github.io#638)/// if it is `None`.
[639](https://fizyk20.github.io#639)///
[640](https://fizyk20.github.io#640)/// Functions that are intended to be constant time may not produce
[641](https://fizyk20.github.io#641)/// valid results for all inputs, such as square root and inversion
[642](https://fizyk20.github.io#642)/// operations in finite field arithmetic. Returning an `Option<T>`
[643](https://fizyk20.github.io#643)/// from these functions makes it difficult for the caller to reason
[644](https://fizyk20.github.io#644)/// about the result in constant time, and returning an incorrect
[645](https://fizyk20.github.io#645)/// value burdens the caller and increases the chance of bugs.
[646](https://fizyk20.github.io#646)#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
[647](https://fizyk20.github.io#647)pub struct CtOption<T> {
[648](https://fizyk20.github.io#648)    value: T,
[649](https://fizyk20.github.io#649)    is_some: Choice,
[650](https://fizyk20.github.io#650)}
[651](https://fizyk20.github.io#651)
[652](https://fizyk20.github.io#652)impl<T> From<CtOption<T>> for Option<T> {
[653](https://fizyk20.github.io#653)    /// Convert the `CtOption<T>` wrapper into an `Option<T>`, depending on whether
[654](https://fizyk20.github.io#654)    /// the underlying `is_some` `Choice` was a `0` or a `1` once unwrapped.
[655](https://fizyk20.github.io#655)    ///
[656](https://fizyk20.github.io#656)    /// # Note
[657](https://fizyk20.github.io#657)    ///
[658](https://fizyk20.github.io#658)    /// This function exists to avoid ending up with ugly, verbose and/or bad handled
[659](https://fizyk20.github.io#659)    /// conversions from the `CtOption<T>` wraps to an `Option<T>` or `Result<T, E>`.
[660](https://fizyk20.github.io#660)    /// This implementation doesn't intend to be constant-time nor try to protect the
[661](https://fizyk20.github.io#661)    /// leakage of the `T` since the `Option<T>` will do it anyways.
[662](https://fizyk20.github.io#662)    fn from(source: CtOption<T>) -> Option<T> {
[663](https://fizyk20.github.io#663)        if source.is_some().unwrap_u8() == 1u8 {
[664](https://fizyk20.github.io#664)            Option::Some(source.value)
[665](https://fizyk20.github.io#665)        } else {
[666](https://fizyk20.github.io#666)            None
[667](https://fizyk20.github.io#667)        }
[668](https://fizyk20.github.io#668)    }

[829](https://fizyk20.github.io#829)impl<T: ConstantTimeEq> ConstantTimeEq for CtOption<T> {
[830](https://fizyk20.github.io#830)    /// Two `CtOption<T>`s are equal if they are both `Some` and
[831](https://fizyk20.github.io#831)    /// their values are equal, or both `None`.
[832](https://fizyk20.github.io#832)    #[inline]
[833](https://fizyk20.github.io#833)    fn ct_eq(&self, rhs: &CtOption<T>) -> Choice {
[834](https://fizyk20.github.io#834)        let a = self.is_some();
[835](https://fizyk20.github.io#835)        let b = rhs.is_some();
[836](https://fizyk20.github.io#836)
[837](https://fizyk20.github.io#837)        (a & b & self.value.ct_eq(&rhs.value)) | (!a & !b)
[838](https://fizyk20.github.io#838)    }

[841](https://fizyk20.github.io#841)/// A type which can be compared in some manner and be determined to be greater
[842](https://fizyk20.github.io#842)/// than another of the same type.
[843](https://fizyk20.github.io#843)pub trait ConstantTimeGreater {
[844](https://fizyk20.github.io#844)    /// Determine whether `self > other`.
[845](https://fizyk20.github.io#845)    ///
[846](https://fizyk20.github.io#846)    /// The bitwise-NOT of the return value of this function should be usable to
[847](https://fizyk20.github.io#847)    /// determine if `self <= other`.
[848](https://fizyk20.github.io#848)    ///
[849](https://fizyk20.github.io#849)    /// This function should execute in constant time.
[850](https://fizyk20.github.io#850)    ///
[851](https://fizyk20.github.io#851)    /// # Returns
[852](https://fizyk20.github.io#852)    ///
[853](https://fizyk20.github.io#853)    /// A `Choice` with a set bit if `self > other`, and with no set bits
[854](https://fizyk20.github.io#854)    /// otherwise.
[855](https://fizyk20.github.io#855)    ///
[856](https://fizyk20.github.io#856)    /// # Example
[857](https://fizyk20.github.io#857)    ///
[858](https://fizyk20.github.io#858)    /// ```
[859](https://fizyk20.github.io#859)    /// use subtle::ConstantTimeGreater;
[860](https://fizyk20.github.io#860)    ///
[861](https://fizyk20.github.io#861)    /// let x: u8 = 13;
[862](https://fizyk20.github.io#862)    /// let y: u8 = 42;
[863](https://fizyk20.github.io#863)    ///
[864](https://fizyk20.github.io#864)    /// let x_gt_y = x.ct_gt(&y);
[865](https://fizyk20.github.io#865)    ///
[866](https://fizyk20.github.io#866)    /// assert_eq!(x_gt_y.unwrap_u8(), 0);
[867](https://fizyk20.github.io#867)    ///
[868](https://fizyk20.github.io#868)    /// let y_gt_x = y.ct_gt(&x);
[869](https://fizyk20.github.io#869)    ///
[870](https://fizyk20.github.io#870)    /// assert_eq!(y_gt_x.unwrap_u8(), 1);
[871](https://fizyk20.github.io#871)    ///
[872](https://fizyk20.github.io#872)    /// let x_gt_x = x.ct_gt(&x);
[873](https://fizyk20.github.io#873)    ///
[874](https://fizyk20.github.io#874)    /// assert_eq!(x_gt_x.unwrap_u8(), 0);
[875](https://fizyk20.github.io#875)    /// ```
[876](https://fizyk20.github.io#876)    fn ct_gt(&self, other: &Self) -> Choice;
[877](https://fizyk20.github.io#877)}
[878](https://fizyk20.github.io#878)
[879](https://fizyk20.github.io#879)macro_rules! generate_unsigned_integer_greater {
[880](https://fizyk20.github.io#880)    ($t_u: ty, $bit_width: expr) => {
[881](https://fizyk20.github.io#881)        impl ConstantTimeGreater for $t_u {
[882](https://fizyk20.github.io#882)            /// Returns Choice::from(1) iff x > y, and Choice::from(0) iff x <= y.
[883](https://fizyk20.github.io#883)            ///
[884](https://fizyk20.github.io#884)            /// # Note
[885](https://fizyk20.github.io#885)            ///
[886](https://fizyk20.github.io#886)            /// This algoritm would also work for signed integers if we first
[887](https://fizyk20.github.io#887)            /// flip the top bit, e.g. `let x: u8 = x ^ 0x80`, etc.
[888](https://fizyk20.github.io#888)            #[inline]
[889](https://fizyk20.github.io#889)            fn ct_gt(&self, other: &$t_u) -> Choice {
[890](https://fizyk20.github.io#890)                let gtb = self & !other; // All the bits in self that are greater than their corresponding bits in other.
[891](https://fizyk20.github.io#891)                let mut ltb = !self & other; // All the bits in self that are less than their corresponding bits in other.
[892](https://fizyk20.github.io#892)                let mut pow = 1;
[893](https://fizyk20.github.io#893)
[894](https://fizyk20.github.io#894)                // Less-than operator is okay here because it's dependent on the bit-width.
[895](https://fizyk20.github.io#895)                while pow < $bit_width {
[896](https://fizyk20.github.io#896)                    ltb |= ltb >> pow; // Bit-smear the highest set bit to the right.
[897](https://fizyk20.github.io#897)                    pow += pow;
[898](https://fizyk20.github.io#898)                }
[899](https://fizyk20.github.io#899)                let mut bit = gtb & !ltb; // Select the highest set bit.
[900](https://fizyk20.github.io#900)                let mut pow = 1;
[901](https://fizyk20.github.io#901)
[902](https://fizyk20.github.io#902)                while pow < $bit_width {
[903](https://fizyk20.github.io#903)                    bit |= bit >> pow; // Shift it to the right until we end up with either 0 or 1.
[904](https://fizyk20.github.io#904)                    pow += pow;
[905](https://fizyk20.github.io#905)                }
[906](https://fizyk20.github.io#906)                // XXX We should possibly do the above flattening to 0 or 1 in the
[907](https://fizyk20.github.io#907)                //     Choice constructor rather than making it a debug error?
[908](https://fizyk20.github.io#908)                Choice::from((bit & 1) as u8)
[909](https://fizyk20.github.io#909)            }
[910](https://fizyk20.github.io#910)        }
[911](https://fizyk20.github.io#911)    };
[912](https://fizyk20.github.io#912)}
[913](https://fizyk20.github.io#913)
[914](https://fizyk20.github.io#914)generate_unsigned_integer_greater!(u8, 8);
[915](https://fizyk20.github.io#915)generate_unsigned_integer_greater!(u16, 16);
[916](https://fizyk20.github.io#916)generate_unsigned_integer_greater!(u32, 32);
[917](https://fizyk20.github.io#917)generate_unsigned_integer_greater!(u64, 64);
[918](https://fizyk20.github.io#918)#[cfg(feature = "i128")]
[919](https://fizyk20.github.io#919)generate_unsigned_integer_greater!(u128, 128);

[921](https://fizyk20.github.io#921)impl ConstantTimeGreater for cmp::Ordering {
[922](https://fizyk20.github.io#922)    #[inline]
[923](https://fizyk20.github.io#923)    fn ct_gt(&self, other: &Self) -> Choice {
[924](https://fizyk20.github.io#924)        // No impl of `ConstantTimeGreater` for `i8`, so use `u8`
[925](https://fizyk20.github.io#925)        let a = (*self as i8) + 1;
[926](https://fizyk20.github.io#926)        let b = (*other as i8) + 1;
[927](https://fizyk20.github.io#927)        (a as u8).ct_gt(&(b as u8))
[928](https://fizyk20.github.io#928)    }

[931](https://fizyk20.github.io#931)/// A type which can be compared in some manner and be determined to be less
[932](https://fizyk20.github.io#932)/// than another of the same type.
[933](https://fizyk20.github.io#933)pub trait ConstantTimeLess: ConstantTimeEq + ConstantTimeGreater {
[934](https://fizyk20.github.io#934)    /// Determine whether `self < other`.
[935](https://fizyk20.github.io#935)    ///
[936](https://fizyk20.github.io#936)    /// The bitwise-NOT of the return value of this function should be usable to
[937](https://fizyk20.github.io#937)    /// determine if `self >= other`.
[938](https://fizyk20.github.io#938)    ///
[939](https://fizyk20.github.io#939)    /// A default implementation is provided and implemented for the unsigned
[940](https://fizyk20.github.io#940)    /// integer types.
[941](https://fizyk20.github.io#941)    ///
[942](https://fizyk20.github.io#942)    /// This function should execute in constant time.
[943](https://fizyk20.github.io#943)    ///
[944](https://fizyk20.github.io#944)    /// # Returns
[945](https://fizyk20.github.io#945)    ///
[946](https://fizyk20.github.io#946)    /// A `Choice` with a set bit if `self < other`, and with no set bits
[947](https://fizyk20.github.io#947)    /// otherwise.
[948](https://fizyk20.github.io#948)    ///
[949](https://fizyk20.github.io#949)    /// # Example
[950](https://fizyk20.github.io#950)    ///
[951](https://fizyk20.github.io#951)    /// ```
[952](https://fizyk20.github.io#952)    /// use subtle::ConstantTimeLess;
[953](https://fizyk20.github.io#953)    ///
[954](https://fizyk20.github.io#954)    /// let x: u8 = 13;
[955](https://fizyk20.github.io#955)    /// let y: u8 = 42;
[956](https://fizyk20.github.io#956)    ///
[957](https://fizyk20.github.io#957)    /// let x_lt_y = x.ct_lt(&y);
[958](https://fizyk20.github.io#958)    ///
[959](https://fizyk20.github.io#959)    /// assert_eq!(x_lt_y.unwrap_u8(), 1);
[960](https://fizyk20.github.io#960)    ///
[961](https://fizyk20.github.io#961)    /// let y_lt_x = y.ct_lt(&x);
[962](https://fizyk20.github.io#962)    ///
[963](https://fizyk20.github.io#963)    /// assert_eq!(y_lt_x.unwrap_u8(), 0);
[964](https://fizyk20.github.io#964)    ///
[965](https://fizyk20.github.io#965)    /// let x_lt_x = x.ct_lt(&x);
[966](https://fizyk20.github.io#966)    ///
[967](https://fizyk20.github.io#967)    /// assert_eq!(x_lt_x.unwrap_u8(), 0);
[968](https://fizyk20.github.io#968)    /// ```
[969](https://fizyk20.github.io#969)    #[inline]
[970](https://fizyk20.github.io#970)    fn ct_lt(&self, other: &Self) -> Choice {
[971](https://fizyk20.github.io#971)        !self.ct_gt(other) & !self.ct_eq(other)
[972](https://fizyk20.github.io#972)    }
[973](https://fizyk20.github.io#973)}

}## Expand description

An `Eq`-like trait that produces a `Choice` instead of a `bool`.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#example)Example

```
use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
let x: u8 = 5;
let y: u8 = 13;
assert_eq!(x.ct_eq(&y).unwrap_u8(), 0);
assert_eq!(x.ct_eq(&x).unwrap_u8(), 1);
```

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/subtle/lib.rs.html#289-332)

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#impl-ConstantTimeEq-for-%5BT%5D)

### impl<T: [ConstantTimeEq](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.ConstantTimeEq.html)> [ConstantTimeEq](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.ConstantTimeEq.html) for [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.slice.html)

Check whether two slices of `ConstantTimeEq` types are equal.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#note)Note

This function short-circuits if the lengths of the input slices are different. Otherwise, it should execute in time independent of the slice contents.

Since arrays coerce to slices, this function works with fixed-size arrays:

```
let a: [u8; 8] = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7];
let b: [u8; 8] = [0,1,2,3,0,1,2,3];
let a_eq_a = a.ct_eq(&a);
let a_eq_b = a.ct_eq(&b);
assert_eq!(a_eq_a.unwrap_u8(), 1);
assert_eq!(a_eq_b.unwrap_u8(), 0);
```

# Deserialize in serde_core::de - Rust

Source: https://fizyk20.github.io/generic-array/serde_core/de/trait.Deserialize.html

`pub trait Deserialize<'de>: `[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) {
    // Required method
    fn [deserialize](https://fizyk20.github.io#tymethod.deserialize)<D>(deserializer: D) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, D::[Error](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.Deserializer.html#associatedtype.Error)>
       where D: [Deserializer](https://fizyk20.github.io/trait.Deserializer.html)<'de>;
}## Expand description

A **data structure** that can be deserialized from any data format supported
by Serde.

Serde provides `Deserialize` implementations for many Rust primitive and
standard library types. The complete list is [here](https://fizyk20.github.io/index.html). All of these
can be deserialized using Serde out of the box.

Additionally, Serde provides a procedural macro called `serde_derive` to
automatically generate `Deserialize` implementations for structs and enums
in your program. See the [derive section of the manual](https://serde.rs/derive.html) for how to
use this.

In rare cases it may be necessary to implement `Deserialize` manually for
some type in your program. See the [Implementing
 Deserialize](https://serde.rs/impl-deserialize.html) section of the manual for more about this.

Third-party crates may provide `Deserialize` implementations for types that
they expose. For example the `linked-hash-map` crate provides a
`LinkedHashMap<K, V>` type that is deserializable by Serde because the crate
provides an implementation of `Deserialize` for it.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#lifetime)Lifetime

The `'de` lifetime of this trait is the lifetime of data that may be
borrowed by `Self` when deserialized. See the page [Understanding
deserializer lifetimes](https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html) for a more detailed explanation of these lifetimes.

}## Expand description

A **data format** that can deserialize any data structure supported by
Serde.

The role of this trait is to define the deserialization half of the [Serde
data model](https://serde.rs/data-model.html), which is a way to categorize every Rust data type into one of
29 possible types. Each method of the `Deserializer` trait corresponds to one
of the types of the data model.

Implementations of `Deserialize` map themselves into this data model by
passing to the `Deserializer` a `Visitor` implementation that can receive
these various types.

The types that make up the Serde data model are:

- **14 primitive types**- bool
- i8, i16, i32, i64, i128
- u8, u16, u32, u64, u128
- f32, f64
- char

- **string**- UTF-8 bytes with a length and no null terminator.
- When serializing, all strings are handled equally. When deserializing, there are three flavors of strings: transient, owned, and borrowed.

- **byte array**- [u8]- Similar to strings, during deserialization byte arrays can be transient, owned, or borrowed.

- **option**- Either none or some value.

- **unit**- The type of `()`in Rust. It represents an anonymous value containing no data.

- The type of
- **unit_struct**- For example `struct Unit`or`PhantomData<T>`. It represents a named value containing no data.

- For example
- **unit_variant**- For example the `E::A`and`E::B`in`enum E { A, B }`.

- For example the
- **newtype_struct**- For example `struct Millimeters(u8)`.

- For example
- **newtype_variant**- For example the `E::N`in`enum E { N(u8) }`.

- For example the
- **seq**- A variably sized heterogeneous sequence of values, for example `Vec<T>`or`HashSet<T>`. When serializing, the length may or may not be known before iterating through all the data. When deserializing, the length is determined by looking at the serialized data.

- A variably sized heterogeneous sequence of values, for example
- **tuple**- A statically sized heterogeneous sequence of values for which the
length will be known at deserialization time without looking at the
serialized data, for example `(u8,)`or`(String, u64, Vec<T>)`or`[u64; 10]`.

- A statically sized heterogeneous sequence of values for which the
length will be known at deserialization time without looking at the
serialized data, for example
- **tuple_struct**- A named tuple, for example `struct Rgb(u8, u8, u8)`.

- A named tuple, for example
- **tuple_variant**- For example the `E::T`in`enum E { T(u8, u8) }`.

- For example the
- **map**- A heterogeneous key-value pairing, for example `BTreeMap<K, V>`.

- A heterogeneous key-value pairing, for example
- **struct**- A heterogeneous key-value pairing in which the keys are strings and
will be known at deserialization time without looking at the serialized
data, for example `struct S { r: u8, g: u8, b: u8 }`.

- A heterogeneous key-value pairing in which the keys are strings and
will be known at deserialization time without looking at the serialized
data, for example
- **struct_variant**- For example the `E::S`in`enum E { S { r: u8, g: u8, b: u8 } }`.

- For example the

The `Deserializer` trait supports two entry point styles which enables
different kinds of deserialization.

-
The `deserialize_any`method. Self-describing data formats like JSON are able to look at the serialized data and tell what it represents. For example the JSON deserializer may see an opening curly brace (`{`) and know that it is seeing a map. If the data format supports`Deserializer::deserialize_any`, it will drive the Visitor using whatever type it sees in the input. JSON uses this approach when deserializing`serde_json::Value`which is an enum that can represent any JSON document. Without knowing what is in a JSON document, we can deserialize it to`serde_json::Value`by going through`Deserializer::deserialize_any`.
-
The various `deserialize_*`methods. Non-self-describing formats like Postcard need to be told what is in the input in order to deserialize it. The`deserialize_*`methods are hints to the deserializer for how to interpret the next piece of input. Non-self-describing formats are not able to deserialize something like`serde_json::Value`which relies on`Deserializer::deserialize_any`.

When implementing `Deserialize`, you should avoid relying on
`Deserializer::deserialize_any` unless you need to be told by the
Deserializer what type is in the input. Know that relying on
`Deserializer::deserialize_any` means your data type will be able to
deserialize from self-describing formats only, ruling out Postcard and many
others.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#lifetime)Lifetime

The `'de` lifetime of this trait is the lifetime of data that may be
borrowed from the input when deserializing. See the page [Understanding
deserializer lifetimes](https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html) for a more detailed explanation of these lifetimes.

[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#example-implementation)Example implementation

The [example data format](https://serde.rs/data-format.html) presented on the website contains example code for
a basic JSON `Deserializer`.

[Source](https://fizyk20.github.io/src/serde_core/de/mod.rs.html#1253-1255)

#### fn [is_human_readable](https://fizyk20.github.io#method.is_human_readable)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.bool.html)

Determine whether `Deserialize` implementations should expect to
deserialize their human-readable form.

Some types have a human-readable form that may be somewhat expensive to construct, as well as a binary form that is compact and efficient. Generally text-based formats like JSON and YAML will prefer to use the human-readable one and binary formats like Postcard will prefer the compact one.

[ⓘ](https://fizyk20.github.io)

```
use serde::de::{self, Deserialize, Deserializer};
impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Timestamp {
    fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
    where
        D: Deserializer<'de>,
    {
        if deserializer.is_human_readable() {
            // Deserialize from a human-readable string like "2015-05-15T17:01:00Z".
            let s = String::deserialize(deserializer)?;
            Timestamp::from_str(&s).map_err(de::Error::custom)
        } else {
            // Deserialize from a compact binary representation, seconds since
            // the Unix epoch.
            let n = u64::deserialize(deserializer)?;
            Ok(Timestamp::EPOCH + Duration::seconds(n))
        }
    }
}
```
The default implementation of this method returns `true`. Data formats
may override this to `false` to request a compact form for types that
support one. Note that modifying this method to change a format from
human-readable to compact or vice versa should be regarded as a breaking
change, as a value serialized in human-readable mode is not required to
deserialize from the same data in compact mode.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://fizyk20.github.io#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# generic_array/iter.rs

[1](https://fizyk20.github.io#1)//! `GenericArray` iterator implementation.
[2](https://fizyk20.github.io#2)
[3](https://fizyk20.github.io#3)use super::{ArrayLength, GenericArray};

[7](https://fizyk20.github.io#7)
[8](https://fizyk20.github.io#8)/// Build a raw slice pointer over the live sub-range `array[start..end]` of an iterator's
[9](https://fizyk20.github.io#9)/// backing `ManuallyDrop<GenericArray<T, N>>`, without ever forming a reference (not even a
[10](https://fizyk20.github.io#10)/// transient `&[T]`) that spans the moved-out slots outside `start..end`.
[11](https://fizyk20.github.io#11)///
[12](https://fizyk20.github.io#12)/// The base pointer is taken via `addr_of!`/`addr_of_mut!` on the array place (the same raw
[13](https://fizyk20.github.io#13)/// cast `GenericArray::as_slice` uses), so the only reference - if any - is the one the
[14](https://fizyk20.github.io#14)/// *caller* materializes from the returned raw pointer at the use site.
[15](https://fizyk20.github.io#15)///
[16](https://fizyk20.github.io#16)/// Forms:
[17](https://fizyk20.github.io#17)/// - `raw_subslice!(const $array, $start, $end)` -> `*const [T]`
[18](https://fizyk20.github.io#18)/// - `raw_subslice!(mut   $array, $start, $end)` -> `*mut [T]`
[19](https://fizyk20.github.io#19)///
[20](https://fizyk20.github.io#20)/// # Safety
[21](https://fizyk20.github.io#21)///
[22](https://fizyk20.github.io#22)/// The caller must ensure `$start <= $end <= N` (the iterator's `index <= index_back <= N`
[23](https://fizyk20.github.io#23)/// invariant) so the range is in bounds, and - for the `mut` form - that no other live
[24](https://fizyk20.github.io#24)/// borrow of the array overlaps `$start..$end`.
[25](https://fizyk20.github.io#25)macro_rules! raw_subslice {
[26](https://fizyk20.github.io#26)    (const $array:expr, $start:expr, $end:expr) => {{
[27](https://fizyk20.github.io#27)        let base = ::core::ptr::addr_of!(*$array) as *const T;
[28](https://fizyk20.github.io#28)        ::core::ptr::slice_from_raw_parts(base.add($start), $end - $start)
[29](https://fizyk20.github.io#29)    }};
[30](https://fizyk20.github.io#30)    (mut $array:expr, $start:expr, $end:expr) => {{
[31](https://fizyk20.github.io#31)        let base = ::core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(*$array) as *mut T;
[32](https://fizyk20.github.io#32)        ::core::ptr::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(base.add($start), $end - $start)
[33](https://fizyk20.github.io#33)    }};
[34](https://fizyk20.github.io#34)}
[35](https://fizyk20.github.io#35)
[36](https://fizyk20.github.io#36)/// An iterator that moves out of a [`GenericArray`]
[37](https://fizyk20.github.io#37)pub struct GenericArrayIter<T, N: ArrayLength> {
[38](https://fizyk20.github.io#38)    // Invariants: index <= index_back <= N
[39](https://fizyk20.github.io#39)    // Only values in array[index..index_back] are alive at any given time.
[40](https://fizyk20.github.io#40)    // Values from array[..index] and array[index_back..] are already moved/dropped.
[41](https://fizyk20.github.io#41)    array: ManuallyDrop<GenericArray<T, N>>,
[42](https://fizyk20.github.io#42)    index: usize,
[43](https://fizyk20.github.io#43)    index_back: usize,
[44](https://fizyk20.github.io#44)}
[45](https://fizyk20.github.io#45)
[46](https://fizyk20.github.io#46)impl<T, N: ArrayLength> GenericArrayIter<T, N> {
[47](https://fizyk20.github.io#47)    /// Raw `*const T` to element 0 of the backing array.
[48](https://fizyk20.github.io#48)    ///
[49](https://fizyk20.github.io#49)    /// Taken via a raw cast of the array's address (the same cast `GenericArray::as_slice`
[50](https://fizyk20.github.io#50)    /// uses), so that callers offsetting into the live range never form a reference - not
[51](https://fizyk20.github.io#51)    /// even a transient `&[T]` - spanning the moved-out slots in `..index`/`index_back..`.
[52](https://fizyk20.github.io#52)    #[inline(always)]
[53](https://fizyk20.github.io#53)    fn base_ptr(&self) -> *const T {
[54](https://fizyk20.github.io#54)        ptr::addr_of!(*self.array) as *const T
[55](https://fizyk20.github.io#55)    }
[56](https://fizyk20.github.io#56)
[57](https://fizyk20.github.io#57)    /// Returns the remaining items of this iterator as a slice
[58](https://fizyk20.github.io#58)    #[inline(always)]
[59](https://fizyk20.github.io#59)    pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[T] {
[60](https://fizyk20.github.io#60)        // SAFETY: By the type invariant, `index <= index_back <= N`, so `index` is in
[61](https://fizyk20.github.io#61)        // bounds and `index_back - index` does not exceed the backing allocation. We form
[62](https://fizyk20.github.io#62)        // the slice directly over the live `index..index_back` range rather than letting
[63](https://fizyk20.github.io#63)        // `GenericArray`'s `Deref` materialize a `&[T]` spanning all `0..N` and then
[64](https://fizyk20.github.io#64)        // re-slicing: this way no reference ever spans the moved-out slots in `..index`
[65](https://fizyk20.github.io#65)        // or `index_back..` (same discipline as `core::array::IntoIter::as_slice`). The
[66](https://fizyk20.github.io#66)        // live elements are initialized and valid for reads. (Codegen is identical to the
[67](https://fizyk20.github.io#67)        // old `get_unchecked` form; see `examples/asm.rs`.)
[68](https://fizyk20.github.io#68)        unsafe { &*raw_subslice!(const self.array, self.index, self.index_back) }
[69](https://fizyk20.github.io#69)    }
[70](https://fizyk20.github.io#70)
[71](https://fizyk20.github.io#71)    /// Returns the remaining items of this iterator as a mutable slice
[72](https://fizyk20.github.io#72)    #[inline(always)]
[73](https://fizyk20.github.io#73)    pub fn as_mut_slice(&mut self) -> &mut [T] {
[74](https://fizyk20.github.io#74)        // SAFETY: By the type invariant, `index <= index_back <= N`, so `index` is in
[75](https://fizyk20.github.io#75)        // bounds and the length `index_back - index` does not exceed the backing
[76](https://fizyk20.github.io#76)        // allocation. The slice spans only the live range, so it never references the
[77](https://fizyk20.github.io#77)        // moved-out slots, and uniqueness holds because it is derived from `&mut self`.
[78](https://fizyk20.github.io#78)        unsafe { &mut *raw_subslice!(mut self.array, self.index, self.index_back) }
[79](https://fizyk20.github.io#79)    }
[80](https://fizyk20.github.io#80)}
[81](https://fizyk20.github.io#81)
[82](https://fizyk20.github.io#82)impl<T, N: ArrayLength> IntoIterator for GenericArray<T, N> {

[84](https://fizyk20.github.io#84)    type IntoIter = GenericArrayIter<T, N>;
[85](https://fizyk20.github.io#85)
[86](https://fizyk20.github.io#86)    #[inline]
[87](https://fizyk20.github.io#87)    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
[88](https://fizyk20.github.io#88)        GenericArrayIter {
[89](https://fizyk20.github.io#89)            array: ManuallyDrop::new(self),
[90](https://fizyk20.github.io#90)            index: 0,
[91](https://fizyk20.github.io#91)            index_back: N::USIZE,
[92](https://fizyk20.github.io#92)        }
[93](https://fizyk20.github.io#93)    }

[105](https://fizyk20.github.io#105)impl<T, N: ArrayLength> Drop for GenericArrayIter<T, N> {
[106](https://fizyk20.github.io#106)    fn drop(&mut self) {
[107](https://fizyk20.github.io#107)        unsafe {
[108](https://fizyk20.github.io#108)            ptr::drop_in_place(self.as_mut_slice());
[109](https://fizyk20.github.io#109)        }
