[136](https://fizyk20.github.io#136)
[137](https://fizyk20.github.io#137)macro_rules! declare_error_trait {
[138](https://fizyk20.github.io#138)    (Error: Sized $(+ $($supertrait:ident)::+)*) => {
[139](https://fizyk20.github.io#139)        /// The `Error` trait allows `Deserialize` implementations to create descriptive
[140](https://fizyk20.github.io#140)        /// error messages belonging to the `Deserializer` against which they are
[141](https://fizyk20.github.io#141)        /// currently running.
[142](https://fizyk20.github.io#142)        ///
[143](https://fizyk20.github.io#143)        /// Every `Deserializer` declares an `Error` type that encompasses both
[144](https://fizyk20.github.io#144)        /// general-purpose deserialization errors as well as errors specific to the
[145](https://fizyk20.github.io#145)        /// particular deserialization format. For example the `Error` type of
[146](https://fizyk20.github.io#146)        /// `serde_json` can represent errors like an invalid JSON escape sequence or an
[147](https://fizyk20.github.io#147)        /// unterminated string literal, in addition to the error cases that are part of
[148](https://fizyk20.github.io#148)        /// this trait.
[149](https://fizyk20.github.io#149)        ///
[150](https://fizyk20.github.io#150)        /// Most deserializers should only need to provide the `Error::custom` method
[151](https://fizyk20.github.io#151)        /// and inherit the default behavior for the other methods.
[152](https://fizyk20.github.io#152)        ///
[153](https://fizyk20.github.io#153)        /// # Example implementation
[154](https://fizyk20.github.io#154)        ///
[155](https://fizyk20.github.io#155)        /// The [example data format] presented on the website shows an error
[156](https://fizyk20.github.io#156)        /// type appropriate for a basic JSON data format.
[157](https://fizyk20.github.io#157)        ///
[158](https://fizyk20.github.io#158)        /// [example data format]: https://serde.rs/data-format.html
[159](https://fizyk20.github.io#159)        #[cfg_attr(
[160](https://fizyk20.github.io#160)            not(no_diagnostic_namespace),
[161](https://fizyk20.github.io#161)            diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
[162](https://fizyk20.github.io#162)                message = "the trait bound `{Self}: serde::de::Error` is not satisfied",
[163](https://fizyk20.github.io#163)            )
[164](https://fizyk20.github.io#164)        )]
[165](https://fizyk20.github.io#165)        pub trait Error: Sized $(+ $($supertrait)::+)* {
[166](https://fizyk20.github.io#166)            /// Raised when there is general error when deserializing a type.
[167](https://fizyk20.github.io#167)            ///
[168](https://fizyk20.github.io#168)            /// The message should not be capitalized and should not end with a period.
[169](https://fizyk20.github.io#169)            ///
[170](https://fizyk20.github.io#170)            /// ```edition2021
[171](https://fizyk20.github.io#171)            /// # use std::str::FromStr;
[172](https://fizyk20.github.io#172)            /// #
[173](https://fizyk20.github.io#173)            /// # struct IpAddr;
[174](https://fizyk20.github.io#174)            /// #
[175](https://fizyk20.github.io#175)            /// # impl FromStr for IpAddr {
[176](https://fizyk20.github.io#176)            /// #     type Err = String;
[177](https://fizyk20.github.io#177)            /// #
[178](https://fizyk20.github.io#178)            /// #     fn from_str(_: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
[179](https://fizyk20.github.io#179)            /// #         unimplemented!()
[180](https://fizyk20.github.io#180)            /// #     }
[181](https://fizyk20.github.io#181)            /// # }
[182](https://fizyk20.github.io#182)            /// #
[183](https://fizyk20.github.io#183)            /// use serde::de::{self, Deserialize, Deserializer};
[184](https://fizyk20.github.io#184)            ///
[185](https://fizyk20.github.io#185)            /// impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for IpAddr {
[186](https://fizyk20.github.io#186)            ///     fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
[187](https://fizyk20.github.io#187)            ///     where
[188](https://fizyk20.github.io#188)            ///         D: Deserializer<'de>,
[189](https://fizyk20.github.io#189)            ///     {
[190](https://fizyk20.github.io#190)            ///         let s = String::deserialize(deserializer)?;
[191](https://fizyk20.github.io#191)            ///         s.parse().map_err(de::Error::custom)
[192](https://fizyk20.github.io#192)            ///     }
[193](https://fizyk20.github.io#193)            /// }
[194](https://fizyk20.github.io#194)            /// ```
[195](https://fizyk20.github.io#195)            fn custom<T>(msg: T) -> Self
[196](https://fizyk20.github.io#196)            where
[197](https://fizyk20.github.io#197)                T: Display;
[198](https://fizyk20.github.io#198)
[199](https://fizyk20.github.io#199)            /// Raised when a `Deserialize` receives a type different from what it was
[200](https://fizyk20.github.io#200)            /// expecting.
[201](https://fizyk20.github.io#201)            ///
[202](https://fizyk20.github.io#202)            /// The `unexp` argument provides information about what type was received.
[203](https://fizyk20.github.io#203)            /// This is the type that was present in the input file or other source data
[204](https://fizyk20.github.io#204)            /// of the Deserializer.
[205](https://fizyk20.github.io#205)            ///
[206](https://fizyk20.github.io#206)            /// The `exp` argument provides information about what type was being
[207](https://fizyk20.github.io#207)            /// expected. This is the type that is written in the program.
[208](https://fizyk20.github.io#208)            ///
[209](https://fizyk20.github.io#209)            /// For example if we try to deserialize a String out of a JSON file
[210](https://fizyk20.github.io#210)            /// containing an integer, the unexpected type is the integer and the
[211](https://fizyk20.github.io#211)            /// expected type is the string.
[212](https://fizyk20.github.io#212)            #[cold]
[213](https://fizyk20.github.io#213)            fn invalid_type(unexp: Unexpected, exp: &dyn Expected) -> Self {
[214](https://fizyk20.github.io#214)                Error::custom(format_args!("invalid type: {}, expected {}", unexp, exp))
[215](https://fizyk20.github.io#215)            }
[216](https://fizyk20.github.io#216)
[217](https://fizyk20.github.io#217)            /// Raised when a `Deserialize` receives a value of the right type but that
[218](https://fizyk20.github.io#218)            /// is wrong for some other reason.
[219](https://fizyk20.github.io#219)            ///
[220](https://fizyk20.github.io#220)            /// The `unexp` argument provides information about what value was received.
[221](https://fizyk20.github.io#221)            /// This is the value that was present in the input file or other source
[222](https://fizyk20.github.io#222)            /// data of the Deserializer.
[223](https://fizyk20.github.io#223)            ///
[224](https://fizyk20.github.io#224)            /// The `exp` argument provides information about what value was being
[225](https://fizyk20.github.io#225)            /// expected. This is the type that is written in the program.
[226](https://fizyk20.github.io#226)            ///
[227](https://fizyk20.github.io#227)            /// For example if we try to deserialize a String out of some binary data
[228](https://fizyk20.github.io#228)            /// that is not valid UTF-8, the unexpected value is the bytes and the
[229](https://fizyk20.github.io#229)            /// expected value is a string.
[230](https://fizyk20.github.io#230)            #[cold]
[231](https://fizyk20.github.io#231)            fn invalid_value(unexp: Unexpected, exp: &dyn Expected) -> Self {
[232](https://fizyk20.github.io#232)                Error::custom(format_args!("invalid value: {}, expected {}", unexp, exp))
[233](https://fizyk20.github.io#233)            }
[234](https://fizyk20.github.io#234)
[235](https://fizyk20.github.io#235)            /// Raised when deserializing a sequence or map and the input data contains
[236](https://fizyk20.github.io#236)            /// too many or too few elements.
[237](https://fizyk20.github.io#237)            ///
[238](https://fizyk20.github.io#238)            /// The `len` argument is the number of elements encountered. The sequence
[239](https://fizyk20.github.io#239)            /// or map may have expected more arguments or fewer arguments.
[240](https://fizyk20.github.io#240)            ///
[241](https://fizyk20.github.io#241)            /// The `exp` argument provides information about what data was being
[242](https://fizyk20.github.io#242)            /// expected. For example `exp` might say that a tuple of size 6 was
[243](https://fizyk20.github.io#243)            /// expected.
[244](https://fizyk20.github.io#244)            #[cold]
[245](https://fizyk20.github.io#245)            fn invalid_length(len: usize, exp: &dyn Expected) -> Self {
[246](https://fizyk20.github.io#246)                Error::custom(format_args!("invalid length {}, expected {}", len, exp))
[247](https://fizyk20.github.io#247)            }
[248](https://fizyk20.github.io#248)
[249](https://fizyk20.github.io#249)            /// Raised when a `Deserialize` enum type received a variant with an
[250](https://fizyk20.github.io#250)            /// unrecognized name.
[251](https://fizyk20.github.io#251)            #[cold]
[252](https://fizyk20.github.io#252)            fn unknown_variant(variant: &str, expected: &'static [&'static str]) -> Self {
[253](https://fizyk20.github.io#253)                if expected.is_empty() {
[254](https://fizyk20.github.io#254)                    Error::custom(format_args!(
[255](https://fizyk20.github.io#255)                        "unknown variant `{}`, there are no variants",
[256](https://fizyk20.github.io#256)                        variant
[257](https://fizyk20.github.io#257)                    ))
[258](https://fizyk20.github.io#258)                } else {
[259](https://fizyk20.github.io#259)                    Error::custom(format_args!(
[260](https://fizyk20.github.io#260)                        "unknown variant `{}`, expected {}",
[261](https://fizyk20.github.io#261)                        variant,
[262](https://fizyk20.github.io#262)                        OneOf { names: expected }
[263](https://fizyk20.github.io#263)                    ))
[264](https://fizyk20.github.io#264)                }
[265](https://fizyk20.github.io#265)            }
[266](https://fizyk20.github.io#266)
[267](https://fizyk20.github.io#267)            /// Raised when a `Deserialize` struct type received a field with an
[268](https://fizyk20.github.io#268)            /// unrecognized name.
[269](https://fizyk20.github.io#269)            #[cold]
[270](https://fizyk20.github.io#270)            fn unknown_field(field: &str, expected: &'static [&'static str]) -> Self {
[271](https://fizyk20.github.io#271)                if expected.is_empty() {
[272](https://fizyk20.github.io#272)                    Error::custom(format_args!(
[273](https://fizyk20.github.io#273)                        "unknown field `{}`, there are no fields",
[274](https://fizyk20.github.io#274)                        field
[275](https://fizyk20.github.io#275)                    ))
[276](https://fizyk20.github.io#276)                } else {
[277](https://fizyk20.github.io#277)                    Error::custom(format_args!(
[278](https://fizyk20.github.io#278)                        "unknown field `{}`, expected {}",
[279](https://fizyk20.github.io#279)                        field,
[280](https://fizyk20.github.io#280)                        OneOf { names: expected }
[281](https://fizyk20.github.io#281)                    ))
[282](https://fizyk20.github.io#282)                }
[283](https://fizyk20.github.io#283)            }
[284](https://fizyk20.github.io#284)
[285](https://fizyk20.github.io#285)            /// Raised when a `Deserialize` struct type expected to receive a required
[286](https://fizyk20.github.io#286)            /// field with a particular name but that field was not present in the
[287](https://fizyk20.github.io#287)            /// input.
[288](https://fizyk20.github.io#288)            #[cold]
[289](https://fizyk20.github.io#289)            fn missing_field(field: &'static str) -> Self {
[290](https://fizyk20.github.io#290)                Error::custom(format_args!("missing field `{}`", field))
[291](https://fizyk20.github.io#291)            }
[292](https://fizyk20.github.io#292)
[293](https://fizyk20.github.io#293)            /// Raised when a `Deserialize` struct type received more than one of the
[294](https://fizyk20.github.io#294)            /// same field.
[295](https://fizyk20.github.io#295)            #[cold]
[296](https://fizyk20.github.io#296)            fn duplicate_field(field: &'static str) -> Self {
[297](https://fizyk20.github.io#297)                Error::custom(format_args!("duplicate field `{}`", field))
[298](https://fizyk20.github.io#298)            }
[299](https://fizyk20.github.io#299)        }
[300](https://fizyk20.github.io#300)    }
[301](https://fizyk20.github.io#301)}
[302](https://fizyk20.github.io#302)
[303](https://fizyk20.github.io#303)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[304](https://fizyk20.github.io#304)declare_error_trait!(Error: Sized + StdError);
[305](https://fizyk20.github.io#305)
[306](https://fizyk20.github.io#306)#[cfg(not(feature = "std"))]
[307](https://fizyk20.github.io#307)declare_error_trait!(Error: Sized + Debug + Display);
[308](https://fizyk20.github.io#308)
[309](https://fizyk20.github.io#309)/// `Unexpected` represents an unexpected invocation of any one of the `Visitor`
[310](https://fizyk20.github.io#310)/// trait methods.
[311](https://fizyk20.github.io#311)///
[312](https://fizyk20.github.io#312)/// This is used as an argument to the `invalid_type`, `invalid_value`, and
[313](https://fizyk20.github.io#313)/// `invalid_length` methods of the `Error` trait to build error messages.
[314](https://fizyk20.github.io#314)///
[315](https://fizyk20.github.io#315)/// ```edition2021
[316](https://fizyk20.github.io#316)/// # use std::fmt;
[317](https://fizyk20.github.io#317)/// #
[318](https://fizyk20.github.io#318)/// # use serde::de::{self, Unexpected, Visitor};
[319](https://fizyk20.github.io#319)/// #
[320](https://fizyk20.github.io#320)/// # struct Example;
[321](https://fizyk20.github.io#321)/// #
[322](https://fizyk20.github.io#322)/// # impl<'de> Visitor<'de> for Example {
[323](https://fizyk20.github.io#323)/// #     type Value = ();
[324](https://fizyk20.github.io#324)/// #
[325](https://fizyk20.github.io#325)/// #     fn expecting(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[326](https://fizyk20.github.io#326)/// #         write!(formatter, "definitely not a boolean")
[327](https://fizyk20.github.io#327)/// #     }
[328](https://fizyk20.github.io#328)/// #
[329](https://fizyk20.github.io#329)/// fn visit_bool<E>(self, v: bool) -> Result<Self::Value, E>
[330](https://fizyk20.github.io#330)/// where
[331](https://fizyk20.github.io#331)///     E: de::Error,
[332](https://fizyk20.github.io#332)/// {
[333](https://fizyk20.github.io#333)///     Err(de::Error::invalid_type(Unexpected::Bool(v), &self))
[334](https://fizyk20.github.io#334)/// }
[335](https://fizyk20.github.io#335)/// # }
[336](https://fizyk20.github.io#336)/// ```
[337](https://fizyk20.github.io#337)#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
[338](https://fizyk20.github.io#338)pub enum Unexpected<'a> {
[339](https://fizyk20.github.io#339)    /// The input contained a boolean value that was not expected.
[340](https://fizyk20.github.io#340)    Bool(bool),
[341](https://fizyk20.github.io#341)
[342](https://fizyk20.github.io#342)    /// The input contained an unsigned integer `u8`, `u16`, `u32` or `u64` that
[343](https://fizyk20.github.io#343)    /// was not expected.
[344](https://fizyk20.github.io#344)    Unsigned(u64),
[345](https://fizyk20.github.io#345)
[346](https://fizyk20.github.io#346)    /// The input contained a signed integer `i8`, `i16`, `i32` or `i64` that
[347](https://fizyk20.github.io#347)    /// was not expected.
[348](https://fizyk20.github.io#348)    Signed(i64),
[349](https://fizyk20.github.io#349)
[350](https://fizyk20.github.io#350)    /// The input contained a floating point `f32` or `f64` that was not
[351](https://fizyk20.github.io#351)    /// expected.
[352](https://fizyk20.github.io#352)    Float(f64),
[353](https://fizyk20.github.io#353)
[354](https://fizyk20.github.io#354)    /// The input contained a `char` that was not expected.
[355](https://fizyk20.github.io#355)    Char(char),
[356](https://fizyk20.github.io#356)
[357](https://fizyk20.github.io#357)    /// The input contained a `&str` or `String` that was not expected.
[358](https://fizyk20.github.io#358)    Str(&'a str),
[359](https://fizyk20.github.io#359)
[360](https://fizyk20.github.io#360)    /// The input contained a `&[u8]` or `Vec<u8>` that was not expected.
[361](https://fizyk20.github.io#361)    Bytes(&'a [u8]),
[362](https://fizyk20.github.io#362)
[363](https://fizyk20.github.io#363)    /// The input contained a unit `()` that was not expected.
[364](https://fizyk20.github.io#364)    Unit,
[365](https://fizyk20.github.io#365)
[366](https://fizyk20.github.io#366)    /// The input contained an `Option<T>` that was not expected.
[367](https://fizyk20.github.io#367)    Option,
[368](https://fizyk20.github.io#368)
[369](https://fizyk20.github.io#369)    /// The input contained a newtype struct that was not expected.
[370](https://fizyk20.github.io#370)    NewtypeStruct,
[371](https://fizyk20.github.io#371)
[372](https://fizyk20.github.io#372)    /// The input contained a sequence that was not expected.
[373](https://fizyk20.github.io#373)    Seq,
[374](https://fizyk20.github.io#374)
[375](https://fizyk20.github.io#375)    /// The input contained a map that was not expected.
[376](https://fizyk20.github.io#376)    Map,
[377](https://fizyk20.github.io#377)
[378](https://fizyk20.github.io#378)    /// The input contained an enum that was not expected.
[379](https://fizyk20.github.io#379)    Enum,
[380](https://fizyk20.github.io#380)
[381](https://fizyk20.github.io#381)    /// The input contained a unit variant that was not expected.
[382](https://fizyk20.github.io#382)    UnitVariant,
[383](https://fizyk20.github.io#383)
[384](https://fizyk20.github.io#384)    /// The input contained a newtype variant that was not expected.
[385](https://fizyk20.github.io#385)    NewtypeVariant,
[386](https://fizyk20.github.io#386)
[387](https://fizyk20.github.io#387)    /// The input contained a tuple variant that was not expected.
[388](https://fizyk20.github.io#388)    TupleVariant,
[389](https://fizyk20.github.io#389)
[390](https://fizyk20.github.io#390)    /// The input contained a struct variant that was not expected.
[391](https://fizyk20.github.io#391)    StructVariant,
[392](https://fizyk20.github.io#392)
[393](https://fizyk20.github.io#393)    /// A message stating what uncategorized thing the input contained that was
[394](https://fizyk20.github.io#394)    /// not expected.
[395](https://fizyk20.github.io#395)    ///
[396](https://fizyk20.github.io#396)    /// The message should be a noun or noun phrase, not capitalized and without
[397](https://fizyk20.github.io#397)    /// a period. An example message is "unoriginal superhero".
[398](https://fizyk20.github.io#398)    Other(&'a str),
[399](https://fizyk20.github.io#399)}
[400](https://fizyk20.github.io#400)
[401](https://fizyk20.github.io#401)impl<'a> fmt::Display for Unexpected<'a> {
[402](https://fizyk20.github.io#402)    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[403](https://fizyk20.github.io#403)        use self::Unexpected::*;
[404](https://fizyk20.github.io#404)        match *self {
[405](https://fizyk20.github.io#405)            Bool(b) => write!(formatter, "boolean `{}`", b),
[406](https://fizyk20.github.io#406)            Unsigned(i) => write!(formatter, "integer `{}`", i),
[407](https://fizyk20.github.io#407)            Signed(i) => write!(formatter, "integer `{}`", i),
[408](https://fizyk20.github.io#408)            Float(f) => write!(formatter, "floating point `{}`", WithDecimalPoint(f)),
[409](https://fizyk20.github.io#409)            Char(c) => write!(formatter, "character `{}`", c),
[410](https://fizyk20.github.io#410)            Str(s) => write!(formatter, "string {:?}", s),
[411](https://fizyk20.github.io#411)            Bytes(_) => formatter.write_str("byte array"),
[412](https://fizyk20.github.io#412)            Unit => formatter.write_str("unit value"),
[413](https://fizyk20.github.io#413)            Option => formatter.write_str("Option value"),
[414](https://fizyk20.github.io#414)            NewtypeStruct => formatter.write_str("newtype struct"),
[415](https://fizyk20.github.io#415)            Seq => formatter.write_str("sequence"),
[416](https://fizyk20.github.io#416)            Map => formatter.write_str("map"),
[417](https://fizyk20.github.io#417)            Enum => formatter.write_str("enum"),
[418](https://fizyk20.github.io#418)            UnitVariant => formatter.write_str("unit variant"),
[419](https://fizyk20.github.io#419)            NewtypeVariant => formatter.write_str("newtype variant"),
[420](https://fizyk20.github.io#420)            TupleVariant => formatter.write_str("tuple variant"),
[421](https://fizyk20.github.io#421)            StructVariant => formatter.write_str("struct variant"),
[422](https://fizyk20.github.io#422)            Other(other) => formatter.write_str(other),
[423](https://fizyk20.github.io#423)        }
[424](https://fizyk20.github.io#424)    }

[427](https://fizyk20.github.io#427)/// `Expected` represents an explanation of what data a `Visitor` was expecting
[428](https://fizyk20.github.io#428)/// to receive.
[429](https://fizyk20.github.io#429)///
[430](https://fizyk20.github.io#430)/// This is used as an argument to the `invalid_type`, `invalid_value`, and
[431](https://fizyk20.github.io#431)/// `invalid_length` methods of the `Error` trait to build error messages. The
[432](https://fizyk20.github.io#432)/// message should be a noun or noun phrase that completes the sentence "This
[433](https://fizyk20.github.io#433)/// Visitor expects to receive ...", for example the message could be "an
[434](https://fizyk20.github.io#434)/// integer between 0 and 64". The message should not be capitalized and should
[435](https://fizyk20.github.io#435)/// not end with a period.
[436](https://fizyk20.github.io#436)///
[437](https://fizyk20.github.io#437)/// Within the context of a `Visitor` implementation, the `Visitor` itself
[438](https://fizyk20.github.io#438)/// (`&self`) is an implementation of this trait.
[439](https://fizyk20.github.io#439)///
[440](https://fizyk20.github.io#440)/// ```edition2021
[441](https://fizyk20.github.io#441)/// # use serde::de::{self, Unexpected, Visitor};
[442](https://fizyk20.github.io#442)/// # use std::fmt;
[443](https://fizyk20.github.io#443)/// #
[444](https://fizyk20.github.io#444)/// # struct Example;
[445](https://fizyk20.github.io#445)/// #
[446](https://fizyk20.github.io#446)/// # impl<'de> Visitor<'de> for Example {
[447](https://fizyk20.github.io#447)/// #     type Value = ();
[448](https://fizyk20.github.io#448)/// #
[449](https://fizyk20.github.io#449)/// #     fn expecting(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[450](https://fizyk20.github.io#450)/// #         write!(formatter, "definitely not a boolean")
[451](https://fizyk20.github.io#451)/// #     }
[452](https://fizyk20.github.io#452)/// #
[453](https://fizyk20.github.io#453)/// fn visit_bool<E>(self, v: bool) -> Result<Self::Value, E>
[454](https://fizyk20.github.io#454)/// where
[455](https://fizyk20.github.io#455)///     E: de::Error,
[456](https://fizyk20.github.io#456)/// {
[457](https://fizyk20.github.io#457)///     Err(de::Error::invalid_type(Unexpected::Bool(v), &self))
[458](https://fizyk20.github.io#458)/// }
[459](https://fizyk20.github.io#459)/// # }
[460](https://fizyk20.github.io#460)/// ```
[461](https://fizyk20.github.io#461)///
[462](https://fizyk20.github.io#462)/// Outside of a `Visitor`, `&"..."` can be used.
[463](https://fizyk20.github.io#463)///
[464](https://fizyk20.github.io#464)/// ```edition2021
[465](https://fizyk20.github.io#465)/// # use serde::de::{self, Unexpected};
[466](https://fizyk20.github.io#466)/// #
[467](https://fizyk20.github.io#467)/// # fn example<E>() -> Result<(), E>
[468](https://fizyk20.github.io#468)/// # where
[469](https://fizyk20.github.io#469)/// #     E: de::Error,
[470](https://fizyk20.github.io#470)/// # {
[471](https://fizyk20.github.io#471)/// #     let v = true;
[472](https://fizyk20.github.io#472)/// return Err(de::Error::invalid_type(
[473](https://fizyk20.github.io#473)///     Unexpected::Bool(v),
[474](https://fizyk20.github.io#474)///     &"a negative integer",
[475](https://fizyk20.github.io#475)/// ));
[476](https://fizyk20.github.io#476)/// # }
[477](https://fizyk20.github.io#477)/// ```
[478](https://fizyk20.github.io#478)#[cfg_attr(
[479](https://fizyk20.github.io#479)    not(no_diagnostic_namespace),
[480](https://fizyk20.github.io#480)    diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
[481](https://fizyk20.github.io#481)        message = "the trait bound `{Self}: serde::de::Expected` is not satisfied",
[482](https://fizyk20.github.io#482)    )
[483](https://fizyk20.github.io#483))]

[485](https://fizyk20.github.io#485)    /// Format an explanation of what data was being expected. Same signature as

[488](https://fizyk20.github.io#488)}

[511](https://fizyk20.github.io#511)////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
[512](https://fizyk20.github.io#512)
[513](https://fizyk20.github.io#513)/// A **data structure** that can be deserialized from any data format supported
[514](https://fizyk20.github.io#514)/// by Serde.
[515](https://fizyk20.github.io#515)///
[516](https://fizyk20.github.io#516)/// Serde provides `Deserialize` implementations for many Rust primitive and
[517](https://fizyk20.github.io#517)/// standard library types. The complete list is [here][crate::de]. All of these
[518](https://fizyk20.github.io#518)/// can be deserialized using Serde out of the box.
[519](https://fizyk20.github.io#519)///
[520](https://fizyk20.github.io#520)/// Additionally, Serde provides a procedural macro called `serde_derive` to
[521](https://fizyk20.github.io#521)/// automatically generate `Deserialize` implementations for structs and enums
[522](https://fizyk20.github.io#522)/// in your program. See the [derive section of the manual][derive] for how to
[523](https://fizyk20.github.io#523)/// use this.
[524](https://fizyk20.github.io#524)///
[525](https://fizyk20.github.io#525)/// In rare cases it may be necessary to implement `Deserialize` manually for
[526](https://fizyk20.github.io#526)/// some type in your program. See the [Implementing
[527](https://fizyk20.github.io#527)/// `Deserialize`][impl-deserialize] section of the manual for more about this.
[528](https://fizyk20.github.io#528)///
[529](https://fizyk20.github.io#529)/// Third-party crates may provide `Deserialize` implementations for types that
[530](https://fizyk20.github.io#530)/// they expose. For example the `linked-hash-map` crate provides a
[531](https://fizyk20.github.io#531)/// `LinkedHashMap<K, V>` type that is deserializable by Serde because the crate
[532](https://fizyk20.github.io#532)/// provides an implementation of `Deserialize` for it.
[533](https://fizyk20.github.io#533)///
[534](https://fizyk20.github.io#534)/// [derive]: https://serde.rs/derive.html
[535](https://fizyk20.github.io#535)/// [impl-deserialize]: https://serde.rs/impl-deserialize.html
[536](https://fizyk20.github.io#536)///
[537](https://fizyk20.github.io#537)/// # Lifetime
[538](https://fizyk20.github.io#538)///
[539](https://fizyk20.github.io#539)/// The `'de` lifetime of this trait is the lifetime of data that may be
[540](https://fizyk20.github.io#540)/// borrowed by `Self` when deserialized. See the page [Understanding
[541](https://fizyk20.github.io#541)/// deserializer lifetimes] for a more detailed explanation of these lifetimes.
[542](https://fizyk20.github.io#542)///
[543](https://fizyk20.github.io#543)/// [Understanding deserializer lifetimes]: https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html
[544](https://fizyk20.github.io#544)#[cfg_attr(
[545](https://fizyk20.github.io#545)    not(no_diagnostic_namespace),
[546](https://fizyk20.github.io#546)    diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
[547](https://fizyk20.github.io#547)        // Prevents `serde_core::de::Deserialize` appearing in the error message
[548](https://fizyk20.github.io#548)        // in projects with no direct dependency on serde_core.
[549](https://fizyk20.github.io#549)        message = "the trait bound `{Self}: serde::Deserialize<'de>` is not satisfied",
[550](https://fizyk20.github.io#550)        note = "for local types consider adding `#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]` to your `{Self}` type",
[551](https://fizyk20.github.io#551)        note = "for types from other crates check whether the crate offers a `serde` feature flag",
[552](https://fizyk20.github.io#552)    )
[553](https://fizyk20.github.io#553))]
[554](https://fizyk20.github.io#554)pub trait Deserialize<'de>: Sized {
[555](https://fizyk20.github.io#555)    /// Deserialize this value from the given Serde deserializer.
[556](https://fizyk20.github.io#556)    ///
[557](https://fizyk20.github.io#557)    /// See the [Implementing `Deserialize`][impl-deserialize] section of the
[558](https://fizyk20.github.io#558)    /// manual for more information about how to implement this method.
[559](https://fizyk20.github.io#559)    ///
[560](https://fizyk20.github.io#560)    /// [impl-deserialize]: https://serde.rs/impl-deserialize.html
[561](https://fizyk20.github.io#561)    fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
[562](https://fizyk20.github.io#562)    where
[563](https://fizyk20.github.io#563)        D: Deserializer<'de>;
[564](https://fizyk20.github.io#564)
[565](https://fizyk20.github.io#565)    /// Deserializes a value into `self` from the given Deserializer.
[566](https://fizyk20.github.io#566)    ///
[567](https://fizyk20.github.io#567)    /// The purpose of this method is to allow the deserializer to reuse
[568](https://fizyk20.github.io#568)    /// resources and avoid copies. As such, if this method returns an error,
[569](https://fizyk20.github.io#569)    /// `self` will be in an indeterminate state where some parts of the struct
[570](https://fizyk20.github.io#570)    /// have been overwritten. Although whatever state that is will be
[571](https://fizyk20.github.io#571)    /// memory-safe.
[572](https://fizyk20.github.io#572)    ///
[573](https://fizyk20.github.io#573)    /// This is generally useful when repeatedly deserializing values that
[574](https://fizyk20.github.io#574)    /// are processed one at a time, where the value of `self` doesn't matter
[575](https://fizyk20.github.io#575)    /// when the next deserialization occurs.
[576](https://fizyk20.github.io#576)    ///
[577](https://fizyk20.github.io#577)    /// If you manually implement this, your recursive deserializations should
[578](https://fizyk20.github.io#578)    /// use `deserialize_in_place`.
[579](https://fizyk20.github.io#579)    ///
[580](https://fizyk20.github.io#580)    /// This method is stable and an official public API, but hidden from the
[581](https://fizyk20.github.io#581)    /// documentation because it is almost never what newbies are looking for.
[582](https://fizyk20.github.io#582)    /// Showing it in rustdoc would cause it to be featured more prominently
[583](https://fizyk20.github.io#583)    /// than it deserves.
[584](https://fizyk20.github.io#584)    #[doc(hidden)]
[585](https://fizyk20.github.io#585)    fn deserialize_in_place<D>(deserializer: D, place: &mut Self) -> Result<(), D::Error>
[586](https://fizyk20.github.io#586)    where
[587](https://fizyk20.github.io#587)        D: Deserializer<'de>,
[588](https://fizyk20.github.io#588)    {
[589](https://fizyk20.github.io#589)        // Default implementation just delegates to `deserialize` impl.
[590](https://fizyk20.github.io#590)        *place = tri!(Deserialize::deserialize(deserializer));
[591](https://fizyk20.github.io#591)        Ok(())
[592](https://fizyk20.github.io#592)    }
[593](https://fizyk20.github.io#593)}
[594](https://fizyk20.github.io#594)
[595](https://fizyk20.github.io#595)/// A data structure that can be deserialized without borrowing any data from
[596](https://fizyk20.github.io#596)/// the deserializer.
[597](https://fizyk20.github.io#597)///
[598](https://fizyk20.github.io#598)/// This is primarily useful for trait bounds on functions. For example a
[599](https://fizyk20.github.io#599)/// `from_str` function may be able to deserialize a data structure that borrows
[600](https://fizyk20.github.io#600)/// from the input string, but a `from_reader` function may only deserialize
[601](https://fizyk20.github.io#601)/// owned data.
[602](https://fizyk20.github.io#602)///
[603](https://fizyk20.github.io#603)/// ```edition2021
[604](https://fizyk20.github.io#604)/// # use serde::de::{Deserialize, DeserializeOwned};
[605](https://fizyk20.github.io#605)/// # use std::io::{Read, Result};
[606](https://fizyk20.github.io#606)/// #
[607](https://fizyk20.github.io#607)/// # trait Ignore {
[608](https://fizyk20.github.io#608)/// fn from_str<'a, T>(s: &'a str) -> Result<T>
[609](https://fizyk20.github.io#609)/// where
[610](https://fizyk20.github.io#610)///     T: Deserialize<'a>;
[611](https://fizyk20.github.io#611)///
[612](https://fizyk20.github.io#612)/// fn from_reader<R, T>(rdr: R) -> Result<T>
[613](https://fizyk20.github.io#613)/// where
[614](https://fizyk20.github.io#614)///     R: Read,
[615](https://fizyk20.github.io#615)///     T: DeserializeOwned;
[616](https://fizyk20.github.io#616)/// # }
[617](https://fizyk20.github.io#617)/// ```
[618](https://fizyk20.github.io#618)///
[619](https://fizyk20.github.io#619)/// # Lifetime
[620](https://fizyk20.github.io#620)///
[621](https://fizyk20.github.io#621)/// The relationship between `Deserialize` and `DeserializeOwned` in trait
[622](https://fizyk20.github.io#622)/// bounds is explained in more detail on the page [Understanding deserializer
[623](https://fizyk20.github.io#623)/// lifetimes].
[624](https://fizyk20.github.io#624)///
[625](https://fizyk20.github.io#625)/// [Understanding deserializer lifetimes]: https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html
[626](https://fizyk20.github.io#626)#[cfg_attr(
[627](https://fizyk20.github.io#627)    not(no_diagnostic_namespace),
[628](https://fizyk20.github.io#628)    diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
[629](https://fizyk20.github.io#629)        message = "the trait bound `{Self}: serde::de::DeserializeOwned` is not satisfied",
[630](https://fizyk20.github.io#630)    )
[631](https://fizyk20.github.io#631))]
[632](https://fizyk20.github.io#632)pub trait DeserializeOwned: for<'de> Deserialize<'de> {}
[633](https://fizyk20.github.io#633)impl<T> DeserializeOwned for T where T: for<'de> Deserialize<'de> {}
[634](https://fizyk20.github.io#634)
[635](https://fizyk20.github.io#635)/// `DeserializeSeed` is the stateful form of the `Deserialize` trait. If you
[636](https://fizyk20.github.io#636)/// ever find yourself looking for a way to pass data into a `Deserialize` impl,
[637](https://fizyk20.github.io#637)/// this trait is the way to do it.
[638](https://fizyk20.github.io#638)///
[639](https://fizyk20.github.io#639)/// As one example of stateful deserialization consider deserializing a JSON
[640](https://fizyk20.github.io#640)/// array into an existing buffer. Using the `Deserialize` trait we could
[641](https://fizyk20.github.io#641)/// deserialize a JSON array into a `Vec<T>` but it would be a freshly allocated
[642](https://fizyk20.github.io#642)/// `Vec<T>`; there is no way for `Deserialize` to reuse a previously allocated
[643](https://fizyk20.github.io#643)/// buffer. Using `DeserializeSeed` instead makes this possible as in the
[644](https://fizyk20.github.io#644)/// example code below.
[645](https://fizyk20.github.io#645)///
[646](https://fizyk20.github.io#646)/// The canonical API for stateless deserialization looks like this:
[647](https://fizyk20.github.io#647)///
[648](https://fizyk20.github.io#648)/// ```edition2021
[649](https://fizyk20.github.io#649)/// # use serde::Deserialize;
[650](https://fizyk20.github.io#650)/// #
[651](https://fizyk20.github.io#651)/// # enum Error {}
[652](https://fizyk20.github.io#652)/// #
[653](https://fizyk20.github.io#653)/// fn func<'de, T: Deserialize<'de>>() -> Result<T, Error>
[654](https://fizyk20.github.io#654)/// # {
[655](https://fizyk20.github.io#655)/// #     unimplemented!()
[656](https://fizyk20.github.io#656)/// # }
[657](https://fizyk20.github.io#657)/// ```
[658](https://fizyk20.github.io#658)///
[659](https://fizyk20.github.io#659)/// Adjusting an API like this to support stateful deserialization is a matter
[660](https://fizyk20.github.io#660)/// of accepting a seed as input:
[661](https://fizyk20.github.io#661)///
[662](https://fizyk20.github.io#662)/// ```edition2021
[663](https://fizyk20.github.io#663)/// # use serde::de::DeserializeSeed;
[664](https://fizyk20.github.io#664)/// #
[665](https://fizyk20.github.io#665)/// # enum Error {}
[666](https://fizyk20.github.io#666)/// #
[667](https://fizyk20.github.io#667)/// fn func_seed<'de, T: DeserializeSeed<'de>>(seed: T) -> Result<T::Value, Error>
[668](https://fizyk20.github.io#668)/// # {
[669](https://fizyk20.github.io#669)/// #     let _ = seed;
[670](https://fizyk20.github.io#670)/// #     unimplemented!()
[671](https://fizyk20.github.io#671)/// # }
[672](https://fizyk20.github.io#672)/// ```
[673](https://fizyk20.github.io#673)///
[674](https://fizyk20.github.io#674)/// In practice the majority of deserialization is stateless. An API expecting a
[675](https://fizyk20.github.io#675)/// seed can be appeased by passing `std::marker::PhantomData` as a seed in the
[676](https://fizyk20.github.io#676)/// case of stateless deserialization.
[677](https://fizyk20.github.io#677)///
[678](https://fizyk20.github.io#678)/// # Lifetime
[679](https://fizyk20.github.io#679)///
[680](https://fizyk20.github.io#680)/// The `'de` lifetime of this trait is the lifetime of data that may be
[681](https://fizyk20.github.io#681)/// borrowed by `Self::Value` when deserialized. See the page [Understanding
[682](https://fizyk20.github.io#682)/// deserializer lifetimes] for a more detailed explanation of these lifetimes.
[683](https://fizyk20.github.io#683)///
[684](https://fizyk20.github.io#684)/// [Understanding deserializer lifetimes]: https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html
[685](https://fizyk20.github.io#685)///
[686](https://fizyk20.github.io#686)/// # Example
[687](https://fizyk20.github.io#687)///
[688](https://fizyk20.github.io#688)/// Suppose we have JSON that looks like `[[1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6]]` and we need
[689](https://fizyk20.github.io#689)/// to deserialize it into a flat representation like `vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]`.
[690](https://fizyk20.github.io#690)/// Allocating a brand new `Vec<T>` for each subarray would be slow. Instead we
[691](https://fizyk20.github.io#691)/// would like to allocate a single `Vec<T>` and then deserialize each subarray
[692](https://fizyk20.github.io#692)/// into it. This requires stateful deserialization using the `DeserializeSeed`
[693](https://fizyk20.github.io#693)/// trait.
[694](https://fizyk20.github.io#694)///
[695](https://fizyk20.github.io#695)/// ```edition2021
[696](https://fizyk20.github.io#696)/// use serde::de::{Deserialize, DeserializeSeed, Deserializer, SeqAccess, Visitor};
[697](https://fizyk20.github.io#697)/// use std::fmt;
[698](https://fizyk20.github.io#698)/// use std::marker::PhantomData;
[699](https://fizyk20.github.io#699)///
[700](https://fizyk20.github.io#700)/// // A DeserializeSeed implementation that uses stateful deserialization to
[701](https://fizyk20.github.io#701)/// // append array elements onto the end of an existing vector. The preexisting
[702](https://fizyk20.github.io#702)/// // state ("seed") in this case is the Vec<T>. The `deserialize` method of
[703](https://fizyk20.github.io#703)/// // `ExtendVec` will be traversing the inner arrays of the JSON input and
[704](https://fizyk20.github.io#704)/// // appending each integer into the existing Vec.
[705](https://fizyk20.github.io#705)/// struct ExtendVec<'a, T: 'a>(&'a mut Vec<T>);
[706](https://fizyk20.github.io#706)///
[707](https://fizyk20.github.io#707)/// impl<'de, 'a, T> DeserializeSeed<'de> for ExtendVec<'a, T>
[708](https://fizyk20.github.io#708)/// where
[709](https://fizyk20.github.io#709)///     T: Deserialize<'de>,
[710](https://fizyk20.github.io#710)/// {
[711](https://fizyk20.github.io#711)///     // The return type of the `deserialize` method. This implementation
[712](https://fizyk20.github.io#712)///     // appends onto an existing vector but does not create any new data
[713](https://fizyk20.github.io#713)///     // structure, so the return type is ().
[714](https://fizyk20.github.io#714)///     type Value = ();
[715](https://fizyk20.github.io#715)///
[716](https://fizyk20.github.io#716)///     fn deserialize<D>(self, deserializer: D) -> Result<Self::Value, D::Error>
[717](https://fizyk20.github.io#717)///     where
[718](https://fizyk20.github.io#718)///         D: Deserializer<'de>,
[719](https://fizyk20.github.io#719)///     {
[720](https://fizyk20.github.io#720)///         // Visitor implementation that will walk an inner array of the JSON
[721](https://fizyk20.github.io#721)///         // input.
[722](https://fizyk20.github.io#722)///         struct ExtendVecVisitor<'a, T: 'a>(&'a mut Vec<T>);
[723](https://fizyk20.github.io#723)///
[724](https://fizyk20.github.io#724)///         impl<'de, 'a, T> Visitor<'de> for ExtendVecVisitor<'a, T>
[725](https://fizyk20.github.io#725)///         where
[726](https://fizyk20.github.io#726)///             T: Deserialize<'de>,
[727](https://fizyk20.github.io#727)///         {
[728](https://fizyk20.github.io#728)///             type Value = ();
[729](https://fizyk20.github.io#729)///
[730](https://fizyk20.github.io#730)///             fn expecting(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[731](https://fizyk20.github.io#731)///                 write!(formatter, "an array of integers")
[732](https://fizyk20.github.io#732)///             }
[733](https://fizyk20.github.io#733)///
[734](https://fizyk20.github.io#734)///             fn visit_seq<A>(self, mut seq: A) -> Result<(), A::Error>
[735](https://fizyk20.github.io#735)///             where
[736](https://fizyk20.github.io#736)///                 A: SeqAccess<'de>,
[737](https://fizyk20.github.io#737)///             {
[738](https://fizyk20.github.io#738)///                 // Decrease the number of reallocations if there are many elements
[739](https://fizyk20.github.io#739)///                 if let Some(size_hint) = seq.size_hint() {
[740](https://fizyk20.github.io#740)///                     self.0.reserve(size_hint);
[741](https://fizyk20.github.io#741)///                 }
[742](https://fizyk20.github.io#742)///
[743](https://fizyk20.github.io#743)///                 // Visit each element in the inner array and push it onto
[744](https://fizyk20.github.io#744)///                 // the existing vector.
[745](https://fizyk20.github.io#745)///                 while let Some(elem) = seq.next_element()? {
[746](https://fizyk20.github.io#746)///                     self.0.push(elem);
[747](https://fizyk20.github.io#747)///                 }
[748](https://fizyk20.github.io#748)///                 Ok(())
[749](https://fizyk20.github.io#749)///             }
[750](https://fizyk20.github.io#750)///         }
[751](https://fizyk20.github.io#751)///
[752](https://fizyk20.github.io#752)///         deserializer.deserialize_seq(ExtendVecVisitor(self.0))
[753](https://fizyk20.github.io#753)///     }
[754](https://fizyk20.github.io#754)/// }
[755](https://fizyk20.github.io#755)///
[756](https://fizyk20.github.io#756)/// // Visitor implementation that will walk the outer array of the JSON input.
[757](https://fizyk20.github.io#757)/// struct FlattenedVecVisitor<T>(PhantomData<T>);
[758](https://fizyk20.github.io#758)///
[759](https://fizyk20.github.io#759)/// impl<'de, T> Visitor<'de> for FlattenedVecVisitor<T>
[760](https://fizyk20.github.io#760)/// where
[761](https://fizyk20.github.io#761)///     T: Deserialize<'de>,
[762](https://fizyk20.github.io#762)/// {
[763](https://fizyk20.github.io#763)///     // This Visitor constructs a single Vec<T> to hold the flattened
[764](https://fizyk20.github.io#764)///     // contents of the inner arrays.
[765](https://fizyk20.github.io#765)///     type Value = Vec<T>;
[766](https://fizyk20.github.io#766)///
[767](https://fizyk20.github.io#767)///     fn expecting(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[768](https://fizyk20.github.io#768)///         write!(formatter, "an array of arrays")
[769](https://fizyk20.github.io#769)///     }
[770](https://fizyk20.github.io#770)///
[771](https://fizyk20.github.io#771)///     fn visit_seq<A>(self, mut seq: A) -> Result<Vec<T>, A::Error>
[772](https://fizyk20.github.io#772)///     where
[773](https://fizyk20.github.io#773)///         A: SeqAccess<'de>,
[774](https://fizyk20.github.io#774)///     {
[775](https://fizyk20.github.io#775)///         // Create a single Vec to hold the flattened contents.
[776](https://fizyk20.github.io#776)///         let mut vec = Vec::new();
[777](https://fizyk20.github.io#777)///
[778](https://fizyk20.github.io#778)///         // Each iteration through this loop is one inner array.
[779](https://fizyk20.github.io#779)///         while let Some(()) = seq.next_element_seed(ExtendVec(&mut vec))? {
[780](https://fizyk20.github.io#780)///             // Nothing to do; inner array has been appended into `vec`.
[781](https://fizyk20.github.io#781)///         }
[782](https://fizyk20.github.io#782)///
[783](https://fizyk20.github.io#783)///         // Return the finished vec.
[784](https://fizyk20.github.io#784)///         Ok(vec)
[785](https://fizyk20.github.io#785)///     }
[786](https://fizyk20.github.io#786)/// }
[787](https://fizyk20.github.io#787)///
[788](https://fizyk20.github.io#788)/// # fn example<'de, D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<(), D::Error>
[789](https://fizyk20.github.io#789)/// # where
[790](https://fizyk20.github.io#790)/// #     D: Deserializer<'de>,
[791](https://fizyk20.github.io#791)/// # {
[792](https://fizyk20.github.io#792)/// let visitor = FlattenedVecVisitor(PhantomData);
[793](https://fizyk20.github.io#793)/// let flattened: Vec<u64> = deserializer.deserialize_seq(visitor)?;
[794](https://fizyk20.github.io#794)/// #     Ok(())
[795](https://fizyk20.github.io#795)/// # }
[796](https://fizyk20.github.io#796)/// ```
[797](https://fizyk20.github.io#797)#[cfg_attr(
[798](https://fizyk20.github.io#798)    not(no_diagnostic_namespace),
[799](https://fizyk20.github.io#799)    diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
[800](https://fizyk20.github.io#800)        message = "the trait bound `{Self}: serde::de::DeserializeSeed<'de>` is not satisfied",
[801](https://fizyk20.github.io#801)    )
[802](https://fizyk20.github.io#802))]
[803](https://fizyk20.github.io#803)pub trait DeserializeSeed<'de>: Sized {
[804](https://fizyk20.github.io#804)    /// The type produced by using this seed.
[805](https://fizyk20.github.io#805)    type Value;
[806](https://fizyk20.github.io#806)
[807](https://fizyk20.github.io#807)    /// Equivalent to the more common `Deserialize::deserialize` method, except
[808](https://fizyk20.github.io#808)    /// with some initial piece of data (the seed) passed in.
[809](https://fizyk20.github.io#809)    fn deserialize<D>(self, deserializer: D) -> Result<Self::Value, D::Error>
[810](https://fizyk20.github.io#810)    where
[811](https://fizyk20.github.io#811)        D: Deserializer<'de>;
[812](https://fizyk20.github.io#812)}
[813](https://fizyk20.github.io#813)
[814](https://fizyk20.github.io#814)impl<'de, T> DeserializeSeed<'de> for PhantomData<T>
[815](https://fizyk20.github.io#815)where
[816](https://fizyk20.github.io#816)    T: Deserialize<'de>,
[817](https://fizyk20.github.io#817){
[818](https://fizyk20.github.io#818)    type Value = T;
[819](https://fizyk20.github.io#819)
[820](https://fizyk20.github.io#820)    #[inline]
[821](https://fizyk20.github.io#821)    fn deserialize<D>(self, deserializer: D) -> Result<T, D::Error>
[822](https://fizyk20.github.io#822)    where
[823](https://fizyk20.github.io#823)        D: Deserializer<'de>,
[824](https://fizyk20.github.io#824)    {
[825](https://fizyk20.github.io#825)        T::deserialize(deserializer)
[826](https://fizyk20.github.io#826)    }
[827](https://fizyk20.github.io#827)}
[828](https://fizyk20.github.io#828)
[829](https://fizyk20.github.io#829)////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
[830](https://fizyk20.github.io#830)
[831](https://fizyk20.github.io#831)/// A **data format** that can deserialize any data structure supported by
[832](https://fizyk20.github.io#832)/// Serde.
[833](https://fizyk20.github.io#833)///
[834](https://fizyk20.github.io#834)/// The role of this trait is to define the deserialization half of the [Serde
[835](https://fizyk20.github.io#835)/// data model], which is a way to categorize every Rust data type into one of
[836](https://fizyk20.github.io#836)/// 29 possible types. Each method of the `Deserializer` trait corresponds to one
[837](https://fizyk20.github.io#837)/// of the types of the data model.
[838](https://fizyk20.github.io#838)///
[839](https://fizyk20.github.io#839)/// Implementations of `Deserialize` map themselves into this data model by
[840](https://fizyk20.github.io#840)/// passing to the `Deserializer` a `Visitor` implementation that can receive
[841](https://fizyk20.github.io#841)/// these various types.
[842](https://fizyk20.github.io#842)///
[843](https://fizyk20.github.io#843)/// The types that make up the Serde data model are:
[844](https://fizyk20.github.io#844)///
[845](https://fizyk20.github.io#845)///  - **14 primitive types**
[846](https://fizyk20.github.io#846)///    - bool
[847](https://fizyk20.github.io#847)///    - i8, i16, i32, i64, i128
[848](https://fizyk20.github.io#848)///    - u8, u16, u32, u64, u128
[849](https://fizyk20.github.io#849)///    - f32, f64
[850](https://fizyk20.github.io#850)///    - char
[851](https://fizyk20.github.io#851)///  - **string**
[852](https://fizyk20.github.io#852)///    - UTF-8 bytes with a length and no null terminator.
[853](https://fizyk20.github.io#853)///    - When serializing, all strings are handled equally. When deserializing,
[854](https://fizyk20.github.io#854)///      there are three flavors of strings: transient, owned, and borrowed.
[855](https://fizyk20.github.io#855)///  - **byte array** - \[u8\]
[856](https://fizyk20.github.io#856)///    - Similar to strings, during deserialization byte arrays can be
[857](https://fizyk20.github.io#857)///      transient, owned, or borrowed.
[858](https://fizyk20.github.io#858)///  - **option**
[859](https://fizyk20.github.io#859)///    - Either none or some value.
[860](https://fizyk20.github.io#860)///  - **unit**
[861](https://fizyk20.github.io#861)///    - The type of `()` in Rust. It represents an anonymous value containing
[862](https://fizyk20.github.io#862)///      no data.
[863](https://fizyk20.github.io#863)///  - **unit_struct**
[864](https://fizyk20.github.io#864)///    - For example `struct Unit` or `PhantomData<T>`. It represents a named
[865](https://fizyk20.github.io#865)///      value containing no data.
[866](https://fizyk20.github.io#866)///  - **unit_variant**
[867](https://fizyk20.github.io#867)///    - For example the `E::A` and `E::B` in `enum E { A, B }`.
[868](https://fizyk20.github.io#868)///  - **newtype_struct**
[869](https://fizyk20.github.io#869)///    - For example `struct Millimeters(u8)`.
[870](https://fizyk20.github.io#870)///  - **newtype_variant**
[871](https://fizyk20.github.io#871)///    - For example the `E::N` in `enum E { N(u8) }`.
[872](https://fizyk20.github.io#872)///  - **seq**
[873](https://fizyk20.github.io#873)///    - A variably sized heterogeneous sequence of values, for example `Vec<T>`
[874](https://fizyk20.github.io#874)///      or `HashSet<T>`. When serializing, the length may or may not be known
[875](https://fizyk20.github.io#875)///      before iterating through all the data. When deserializing, the length
[876](https://fizyk20.github.io#876)///      is determined by looking at the serialized data.
[877](https://fizyk20.github.io#877)///  - **tuple**
[878](https://fizyk20.github.io#878)///    - A statically sized heterogeneous sequence of values for which the
[879](https://fizyk20.github.io#879)///      length will be known at deserialization time without looking at the
[880](https://fizyk20.github.io#880)///      serialized data, for example `(u8,)` or `(String, u64, Vec<T>)` or
[881](https://fizyk20.github.io#881)///      `[u64; 10]`.
[882](https://fizyk20.github.io#882)///  - **tuple_struct**
[883](https://fizyk20.github.io#883)///    - A named tuple, for example `struct Rgb(u8, u8, u8)`.
[884](https://fizyk20.github.io#884)///  - **tuple_variant**
[885](https://fizyk20.github.io#885)///    - For example the `E::T` in `enum E { T(u8, u8) }`.
[886](https://fizyk20.github.io#886)///  - **map**
[887](https://fizyk20.github.io#887)///    - A heterogeneous key-value pairing, for example `BTreeMap<K, V>`.
[888](https://fizyk20.github.io#888)///  - **struct**
[889](https://fizyk20.github.io#889)///    - A heterogeneous key-value pairing in which the keys are strings and
[890](https://fizyk20.github.io#890)///      will be known at deserialization time without looking at the serialized
[891](https://fizyk20.github.io#891)///      data, for example `struct S { r: u8, g: u8, b: u8 }`.
[892](https://fizyk20.github.io#892)///  - **struct_variant**
[893](https://fizyk20.github.io#893)///    - For example the `E::S` in `enum E { S { r: u8, g: u8, b: u8 } }`.
[894](https://fizyk20.github.io#894)///
[895](https://fizyk20.github.io#895)/// The `Deserializer` trait supports two entry point styles which enables
[896](https://fizyk20.github.io#896)/// different kinds of deserialization.
[897](https://fizyk20.github.io#897)///
[898](https://fizyk20.github.io#898)/// 1. The `deserialize_any` method. Self-describing data formats like JSON are
[899](https://fizyk20.github.io#899)///    able to look at the serialized data and tell what it represents. For
[900](https://fizyk20.github.io#900)///    example the JSON deserializer may see an opening curly brace (`{`) and
[901](https://fizyk20.github.io#901)///    know that it is seeing a map. If the data format supports
[902](https://fizyk20.github.io#902)///    `Deserializer::deserialize_any`, it will drive the Visitor using whatever
[903](https://fizyk20.github.io#903)///    type it sees in the input. JSON uses this approach when deserializing
[904](https://fizyk20.github.io#904)///    `serde_json::Value` which is an enum that can represent any JSON
[905](https://fizyk20.github.io#905)///    document. Without knowing what is in a JSON document, we can deserialize
[906](https://fizyk20.github.io#906)///    it to `serde_json::Value` by going through
[907](https://fizyk20.github.io#907)///    `Deserializer::deserialize_any`.
[908](https://fizyk20.github.io#908)///
[909](https://fizyk20.github.io#909)/// 2. The various `deserialize_*` methods. Non-self-describing formats like
[910](https://fizyk20.github.io#910)///    Postcard need to be told what is in the input in order to deserialize it.
[911](https://fizyk20.github.io#911)///    The `deserialize_*` methods are hints to the deserializer for how to
[912](https://fizyk20.github.io#912)///    interpret the next piece of input. Non-self-describing formats are not
[913](https://fizyk20.github.io#913)///    able to deserialize something like `serde_json::Value` which relies on
[914](https://fizyk20.github.io#914)///    `Deserializer::deserialize_any`.
[915](https://fizyk20.github.io#915)///
[916](https://fizyk20.github.io#916)/// When implementing `Deserialize`, you should avoid relying on
[917](https://fizyk20.github.io#917)/// `Deserializer::deserialize_any` unless you need to be told by the
[918](https://fizyk20.github.io#918)/// Deserializer what type is in the input. Know that relying on
[919](https://fizyk20.github.io#919)/// `Deserializer::deserialize_any` means your data type will be able to
[920](https://fizyk20.github.io#920)/// deserialize from self-describing formats only, ruling out Postcard and many
[921](https://fizyk20.github.io#921)/// others.
[922](https://fizyk20.github.io#922)///
[923](https://fizyk20.github.io#923)/// [Serde data model]: https://serde.rs/data-model.html
[924](https://fizyk20.github.io#924)///
[925](https://fizyk20.github.io#925)/// # Lifetime
[926](https://fizyk20.github.io#926)///
[927](https://fizyk20.github.io#927)/// The `'de` lifetime of this trait is the lifetime of data that may be
[928](https://fizyk20.github.io#928)/// borrowed from the input when deserializing. See the page [Understanding
[929](https://fizyk20.github.io#929)/// deserializer lifetimes] for a more detailed explanation of these lifetimes.
[930](https://fizyk20.github.io#930)///
[931](https://fizyk20.github.io#931)/// [Understanding deserializer lifetimes]: https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html
[932](https://fizyk20.github.io#932)///
[933](https://fizyk20.github.io#933)/// # Example implementation
[934](https://fizyk20.github.io#934)///
[935](https://fizyk20.github.io#935)/// The [example data format] presented on the website contains example code for
[936](https://fizyk20.github.io#936)/// a basic JSON `Deserializer`.
[937](https://fizyk20.github.io#937)///
[938](https://fizyk20.github.io#938)/// [example data format]: https://serde.rs/data-format.html
[939](https://fizyk20.github.io#939)#[cfg_attr(
[940](https://fizyk20.github.io#940)    not(no_diagnostic_namespace),
[941](https://fizyk20.github.io#941)    diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
[942](https://fizyk20.github.io#942)        message = "the trait bound `{Self}: serde::de::Deserializer<'de>` is not satisfied",
[943](https://fizyk20.github.io#943)    )
[944](https://fizyk20.github.io#944))]
[945](https://fizyk20.github.io#945)pub trait Deserializer<'de>: Sized {
[946](https://fizyk20.github.io#946)    /// The error type that can be returned if some error occurs during
[947](https://fizyk20.github.io#947)    /// deserialization.
[948](https://fizyk20.github.io#948)    type Error: Error;
[949](https://fizyk20.github.io#949)
[950](https://fizyk20.github.io#950)    /// Require the `Deserializer` to figure out how to drive the visitor based
[951](https://fizyk20.github.io#951)    /// on what data type is in the input.
[952](https://fizyk20.github.io#952)    ///
[953](https://fizyk20.github.io#953)    /// When implementing `Deserialize`, you should avoid relying on
[954](https://fizyk20.github.io#954)    /// `Deserializer::deserialize_any` unless you need to be told by the
[955](https://fizyk20.github.io#955)    /// Deserializer what type is in the input. Know that relying on

[1186](https://fizyk20.github.io#1186)    /// Determine whether `Deserialize` implementations should expect to
[1187](https://fizyk20.github.io#1187)    /// deserialize their human-readable form.
[1188](https://fizyk20.github.io#1188)    ///
[1189](https://fizyk20.github.io#1189)    /// Some types have a human-readable form that may be somewhat expensive to
[1190](https://fizyk20.github.io#1190)    /// construct, as well as a binary form that is compact and efficient.
[1191](https://fizyk20.github.io#1191)    /// Generally text-based formats like JSON and YAML will prefer to use the
[1192](https://fizyk20.github.io#1192)    /// human-readable one and binary formats like Postcard will prefer the
[1193](https://fizyk20.github.io#1193)    /// compact one.
[1194](https://fizyk20.github.io#1194)    ///
[1195](https://fizyk20.github.io#1195)    /// ```edition2021
[1196](https://fizyk20.github.io#1196)    /// # use std::ops::Add;
[1197](https://fizyk20.github.io#1197)    /// # use std::str::FromStr;
[1198](https://fizyk20.github.io#1198)    /// #
[1199](https://fizyk20.github.io#1199)    /// # struct Timestamp;
[1200](https://fizyk20.github.io#1200)    /// #
[1201](https://fizyk20.github.io#1201)    /// # impl Timestamp {
[1202](https://fizyk20.github.io#1202)    /// #     const EPOCH: Timestamp = Timestamp;
[1203](https://fizyk20.github.io#1203)    /// # }
[1204](https://fizyk20.github.io#1204)    /// #
[1205](https://fizyk20.github.io#1205)    /// # impl FromStr for Timestamp {
[1206](https://fizyk20.github.io#1206)    /// #     type Err = String;
[1207](https://fizyk20.github.io#1207)    /// #     fn from_str(_: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
[1208](https://fizyk20.github.io#1208)    /// #         unimplemented!()
[1209](https://fizyk20.github.io#1209)    /// #     }
[1210](https://fizyk20.github.io#1210)    /// # }
[1211](https://fizyk20.github.io#1211)    /// #
[1212](https://fizyk20.github.io#1212)    /// # struct Duration;
[1213](https://fizyk20.github.io#1213)    /// #
[1214](https://fizyk20.github.io#1214)    /// # impl Duration {
[1215](https://fizyk20.github.io#1215)    /// #     fn seconds(_: u64) -> Self { unimplemented!() }
[1216](https://fizyk20.github.io#1216)    /// # }
[1217](https://fizyk20.github.io#1217)    /// #
[1218](https://fizyk20.github.io#1218)    /// # impl Add<Duration> for Timestamp {
[1219](https://fizyk20.github.io#1219)    /// #     type Output = Timestamp;
[1220](https://fizyk20.github.io#1220)    /// #     fn add(self, _: Duration) -> Self::Output {
[1221](https://fizyk20.github.io#1221)    /// #         unimplemented!()
[1222](https://fizyk20.github.io#1222)    /// #     }
[1223](https://fizyk20.github.io#1223)    /// # }
[1224](https://fizyk20.github.io#1224)    /// #
[1225](https://fizyk20.github.io#1225)    /// use serde::de::{self, Deserialize, Deserializer};
[1226](https://fizyk20.github.io#1226)    ///
[1227](https://fizyk20.github.io#1227)    /// impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Timestamp {
[1228](https://fizyk20.github.io#1228)    ///     fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
[1229](https://fizyk20.github.io#1229)    ///     where
[1230](https://fizyk20.github.io#1230)    ///         D: Deserializer<'de>,
[1231](https://fizyk20.github.io#1231)    ///     {
[1232](https://fizyk20.github.io#1232)    ///         if deserializer.is_human_readable() {
[1233](https://fizyk20.github.io#1233)    ///             // Deserialize from a human-readable string like "2015-05-15T17:01:00Z".
[1234](https://fizyk20.github.io#1234)    ///             let s = String::deserialize(deserializer)?;
[1235](https://fizyk20.github.io#1235)    ///             Timestamp::from_str(&s).map_err(de::Error::custom)
[1236](https://fizyk20.github.io#1236)    ///         } else {
[1237](https://fizyk20.github.io#1237)    ///             // Deserialize from a compact binary representation, seconds since
[1238](https://fizyk20.github.io#1238)    ///             // the Unix epoch.
[1239](https://fizyk20.github.io#1239)    ///             let n = u64::deserialize(deserializer)?;
[1240](https://fizyk20.github.io#1240)    ///             Ok(Timestamp::EPOCH + Duration::seconds(n))
[1241](https://fizyk20.github.io#1241)    ///         }
[1242](https://fizyk20.github.io#1242)    ///     }
[1243](https://fizyk20.github.io#1243)    /// }
[1244](https://fizyk20.github.io#1244)    /// ```
[1245](https://fizyk20.github.io#1245)    ///
[1246](https://fizyk20.github.io#1246)    /// The default implementation of this method returns `true`. Data formats
[1247](https://fizyk20.github.io#1247)    /// may override this to `false` to request a compact form for types that
[1248](https://fizyk20.github.io#1248)    /// support one. Note that modifying this method to change a format from
[1249](https://fizyk20.github.io#1249)    /// human-readable to compact or vice versa should be regarded as a breaking
[1250](https://fizyk20.github.io#1250)    /// change, as a value serialized in human-readable mode is not required to
[1251](https://fizyk20.github.io#1251)    /// deserialize from the same data in compact mode.
[1252](https://fizyk20.github.io#1252)    #[inline]
[1253](https://fizyk20.github.io#1253)    fn is_human_readable(&self) -> bool {
[1254](https://fizyk20.github.io#1254)        true
[1255](https://fizyk20.github.io#1255)    }
[1256](https://fizyk20.github.io#1256)
[1257](https://fizyk20.github.io#1257)    // Not public API.
[1258](https://fizyk20.github.io#1258)    #[cfg(all(not(no_serde_derive), any(feature = "std", feature = "alloc")))]
[1259](https://fizyk20.github.io#1259)    #[doc(hidden)]
[1260](https://fizyk20.github.io#1260)    fn __deserialize_content_v1<V>(self, visitor: V) -> Result<V::Value, Self::Error>
[1261](https://fizyk20.github.io#1261)    where
[1262](https://fizyk20.github.io#1262)        V: Visitor<'de, Value = crate::private::Content<'de>>,
[1263](https://fizyk20.github.io#1263)    {
[1264](https://fizyk20.github.io#1264)        self.deserialize_any(visitor)
[1265](https://fizyk20.github.io#1265)    }
[1266](https://fizyk20.github.io#1266)}

[1270](https://fizyk20.github.io#1270)/// This trait represents a visitor that walks through a deserializer.
[1271](https://fizyk20.github.io#1271)///
[1272](https://fizyk20.github.io#1272)/// # Lifetime
[1273](https://fizyk20.github.io#1273)///
[1274](https://fizyk20.github.io#1274)/// The `'de` lifetime of this trait is the requirement for lifetime of data
[1275](https://fizyk20.github.io#1275)/// that may be borrowed by `Self::Value`. See the page [Understanding
[1276](https://fizyk20.github.io#1276)/// deserializer lifetimes] for a more detailed explanation of these lifetimes.
[1277](https://fizyk20.github.io#1277)///
[1278](https://fizyk20.github.io#1278)/// [Understanding deserializer lifetimes]: https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html
[1279](https://fizyk20.github.io#1279)///
[1280](https://fizyk20.github.io#1280)/// # Example
[1281](https://fizyk20.github.io#1281)///
[1282](https://fizyk20.github.io#1282)/// ```edition2021
[1283](https://fizyk20.github.io#1283)/// # use serde::de::{self, Unexpected, Visitor};
[1284](https://fizyk20.github.io#1284)/// # use std::fmt;
[1285](https://fizyk20.github.io#1285)/// #
[1286](https://fizyk20.github.io#1286)/// /// A visitor that deserializes a long string - a string containing at least
[1287](https://fizyk20.github.io#1287)/// /// some minimum number of bytes.
[1288](https://fizyk20.github.io#1288)/// struct LongString {
[1289](https://fizyk20.github.io#1289)///     min: usize,
[1290](https://fizyk20.github.io#1290)/// }
[1291](https://fizyk20.github.io#1291)///
[1292](https://fizyk20.github.io#1292)/// impl<'de> Visitor<'de> for LongString {
[1293](https://fizyk20.github.io#1293)///     type Value = String;
[1294](https://fizyk20.github.io#1294)///
[1295](https://fizyk20.github.io#1295)///     fn expecting(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[1296](https://fizyk20.github.io#1296)///         write!(formatter, "a string containing at least {} bytes", self.min)
[1297](https://fizyk20.github.io#1297)///     }
[1298](https://fizyk20.github.io#1298)///
[1299](https://fizyk20.github.io#1299)///     fn visit_str<E>(self, s: &str) -> Result<Self::Value, E>
[1300](https://fizyk20.github.io#1300)///     where
[1301](https://fizyk20.github.io#1301)///         E: de::Error,
[1302](https://fizyk20.github.io#1302)///     {
[1303](https://fizyk20.github.io#1303)///         if s.len() >= self.min {
[1304](https://fizyk20.github.io#1304)///             Ok(s.to_owned())
[1305](https://fizyk20.github.io#1305)///         } else {
[1306](https://fizyk20.github.io#1306)///             Err(de::Error::invalid_value(Unexpected::Str(s), &self))
[1307](https://fizyk20.github.io#1307)///         }
[1308](https://fizyk20.github.io#1308)///     }
[1309](https://fizyk20.github.io#1309)/// }
[1310](https://fizyk20.github.io#1310)/// ```
[1311](https://fizyk20.github.io#1311)#[cfg_attr(
[1312](https://fizyk20.github.io#1312)    not(no_diagnostic_namespace),
[1313](https://fizyk20.github.io#1313)    diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
[1314](https://fizyk20.github.io#1314)        message = "the trait bound `{Self}: serde::de::Visitor<'de>` is not satisfied",
[1315](https://fizyk20.github.io#1315)    )
[1316](https://fizyk20.github.io#1316))]
[1317](https://fizyk20.github.io#1317)pub trait Visitor<'de>: Sized {

[1515](https://fizyk20.github.io#1515)    /// The input contains a string. The lifetime of the string is ephemeral and
[1516](https://fizyk20.github.io#1516)    /// it may be destroyed after this method returns.
[1517](https://fizyk20.github.io#1517)    ///
[1518](https://fizyk20.github.io#1518)    /// This method allows the `Deserializer` to avoid a copy by retaining
[1519](https://fizyk20.github.io#1519)    /// ownership of any buffered data. `Deserialize` implementations that do
[1520](https://fizyk20.github.io#1520)    /// not benefit from taking ownership of `String` data should indicate that
[1521](https://fizyk20.github.io#1521)    /// to the deserializer by using `Deserializer::deserialize_str` rather than
[1522](https://fizyk20.github.io#1522)    /// `Deserializer::deserialize_string`.
[1523](https://fizyk20.github.io#1523)    ///
[1524](https://fizyk20.github.io#1524)    /// It is never correct to implement `visit_string` without implementing
[1525](https://fizyk20.github.io#1525)    /// `visit_str`. Implement neither, both, or just `visit_str`.
[1526](https://fizyk20.github.io#1526)    fn visit_str<E>(self, v: &str) -> Result<Self::Value, E>
[1527](https://fizyk20.github.io#1527)    where
[1528](https://fizyk20.github.io#1528)        E: Error,
[1529](https://fizyk20.github.io#1529)    {
[1530](https://fizyk20.github.io#1530)        Err(Error::invalid_type(Unexpected::Str(v), &self))
[1531](https://fizyk20.github.io#1531)    }

[1547](https://fizyk20.github.io#1547)        self.visit_str(v)
[1548](https://fizyk20.github.io#1548)    }
[1549](https://fizyk20.github.io#1549)
[1550](https://fizyk20.github.io#1550)    /// The input contains a string and ownership of the string is being given

[1552](https://fizyk20.github.io#1552)    ///
[1553](https://fizyk20.github.io#1553)    /// This method allows the `Visitor` to avoid a copy by taking ownership of

[1723](https://fizyk20.github.io#1723)
[1724](https://fizyk20.github.io#1724)/// Provides a `Visitor` access to each element of a sequence in the input.
[1725](https://fizyk20.github.io#1725)///
[1726](https://fizyk20.github.io#1726)/// This is a trait that a `Deserializer` passes to a `Visitor` implementation,
[1727](https://fizyk20.github.io#1727)/// which deserializes each item in a sequence.
[1728](https://fizyk20.github.io#1728)///
[1729](https://fizyk20.github.io#1729)/// # Lifetime
[1730](https://fizyk20.github.io#1730)///
[1731](https://fizyk20.github.io#1731)/// The `'de` lifetime of this trait is the lifetime of data that may be
[1732](https://fizyk20.github.io#1732)/// borrowed by deserialized sequence elements. See the page [Understanding
[1733](https://fizyk20.github.io#1733)/// deserializer lifetimes] for a more detailed explanation of these lifetimes.
[1734](https://fizyk20.github.io#1734)///
[1735](https://fizyk20.github.io#1735)/// [Understanding deserializer lifetimes]: https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html
[1736](https://fizyk20.github.io#1736)///
[1737](https://fizyk20.github.io#1737)/// # Example implementation
[1738](https://fizyk20.github.io#1738)///
[1739](https://fizyk20.github.io#1739)/// The [example data format] presented on the website demonstrates an
[1740](https://fizyk20.github.io#1740)/// implementation of `SeqAccess` for a basic JSON data format.
[1741](https://fizyk20.github.io#1741)///
[1742](https://fizyk20.github.io#1742)/// [example data format]: https://serde.rs/data-format.html
[1743](https://fizyk20.github.io#1743)#[cfg_attr(
[1744](https://fizyk20.github.io#1744)    not(no_diagnostic_namespace),
[1745](https://fizyk20.github.io#1745)    diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
[1746](https://fizyk20.github.io#1746)        message = "the trait bound `{Self}: serde::de::SeqAccess<'de>` is not satisfied",
[1747](https://fizyk20.github.io#1747)    )
[1748](https://fizyk20.github.io#1748))]
[1749](https://fizyk20.github.io#1749)pub trait SeqAccess<'de> {
[1750](https://fizyk20.github.io#1750)    /// The error type that can be returned if some error occurs during
[1751](https://fizyk20.github.io#1751)    /// deserialization.
[1752](https://fizyk20.github.io#1752)    type Error: Error;
[1753](https://fizyk20.github.io#1753)
[1754](https://fizyk20.github.io#1754)    /// This returns `Ok(Some(value))` for the next value in the sequence, or
[1755](https://fizyk20.github.io#1755)    /// `Ok(None)` if there are no more remaining items.
[1756](https://fizyk20.github.io#1756)    ///
[1757](https://fizyk20.github.io#1757)    /// `Deserialize` implementations should typically use
[1758](https://fizyk20.github.io#1758)    /// `SeqAccess::next_element` instead.
[1759](https://fizyk20.github.io#1759)    fn next_element_seed<T>(&mut self, seed: T) -> Result<Option<T::Value>, Self::Error>
[1760](https://fizyk20.github.io#1760)    where
[1761](https://fizyk20.github.io#1761)        T: DeserializeSeed<'de>;
[1762](https://fizyk20.github.io#1762)
[1763](https://fizyk20.github.io#1763)    /// This returns `Ok(Some(value))` for the next value in the sequence, or
[1764](https://fizyk20.github.io#1764)    /// `Ok(None)` if there are no more remaining items.
[1765](https://fizyk20.github.io#1765)    ///
[1766](https://fizyk20.github.io#1766)    /// This method exists as a convenience for `Deserialize` implementations.
[1767](https://fizyk20.github.io#1767)    /// `SeqAccess` implementations should not override the default behavior.
[1768](https://fizyk20.github.io#1768)    #[inline]
[1769](https://fizyk20.github.io#1769)    fn next_element<T>(&mut self) -> Result<Option<T>, Self::Error>
[1770](https://fizyk20.github.io#1770)    where
[1771](https://fizyk20.github.io#1771)        T: Deserialize<'de>,
[1772](https://fizyk20.github.io#1772)    {
[1773](https://fizyk20.github.io#1773)        self.next_element_seed(PhantomData)
[1774](https://fizyk20.github.io#1774)    }
[1775](https://fizyk20.github.io#1775)
[1776](https://fizyk20.github.io#1776)    /// Returns the number of elements remaining in the sequence, if known.
[1777](https://fizyk20.github.io#1777)    #[inline]
[1778](https://fizyk20.github.io#1778)    fn size_hint(&self) -> Option<usize> {
[1779](https://fizyk20.github.io#1779)        None
[1780](https://fizyk20.github.io#1780)    }
[1781](https://fizyk20.github.io#1781)}
[1782](https://fizyk20.github.io#1782)
[1783](https://fizyk20.github.io#1783)impl<'de, A> SeqAccess<'de> for &mut A
[1784](https://fizyk20.github.io#1784)where
[1785](https://fizyk20.github.io#1785)    A: ?Sized + SeqAccess<'de>,
[1786](https://fizyk20.github.io#1786){
[1787](https://fizyk20.github.io#1787)    type Error = A::Error;
[1788](https://fizyk20.github.io#1788)
[1789](https://fizyk20.github.io#1789)    #[inline]

[1791](https://fizyk20.github.io#1791)    where

[1813](https://fizyk20.github.io#1813)/// Provides a `Visitor` access to each entry of a map in the input.

[1829](https://fizyk20.github.io#1829)///
[1830](https://fizyk20.github.io#1830)/// [example data format]: https://serde.rs/data-format.html
[1831](https://fizyk20.github.io#1831)#[cfg_attr(
[1832](https://fizyk20.github.io#1832)    not(no_diagnostic_namespace),
[1833](https://fizyk20.github.io#1833)    diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
[1834](https://fizyk20.github.io#1834)        message = "the trait bound `{Self}: serde::de::MapAccess<'de>` is not satisfied",
[1835](https://fizyk20.github.io#1835)    )
